ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Hypermutant cancers frequently contain atypical driver gene variants, which may provide sub-optimal oncogenic advantages. The reason why weak cancer drivers prevail and are not outcompeted by stronger alternatives is unclear. Here, using mathematical modelling, we show that aberrant mutational processes alone can account for the detection of weak, rather than canonical, driver mutations. We find that simply increasing the mutation rate per cell division, without altering selection or mutational biases, can lead to the dominance of weak drivers due to rapidly occurring further driver events. This effect can be further enhanced by mutational biases towards specific nucleotide sequence contexts. Focusing on POLE-mutant (DNA polymerase epsilon proofreading-deficient) colorectal cancers, we quantify the mutation bias for varied KRAS drivers under both POLE-mutant and non-hypermutant mutational processes. In POLE-mutant cancers, the combination of the bias coupled with an elevated mutation rate is sufficient to explain the enrichment of atypical KRAS drivers. Furthermore, model predictions are consistent with the observed prevalence of atypical KRAS drivers observed in mismatch repair deficient colorectal cancer. Thus, differential selection across these cancer types need not be invoked to explain the variation in driver mutations. Our study clarifies the interplay of mutation and selection during the evolutionary dynamics of tumourigenesis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) has been reimbursed in Japan since 2019; however, the extent to which treatments recommended by expert panels are subsequently implemented and how this varies across cancer types remain unclear. Among 50,974 patients with solid tumors registered in the C-CAT database between June 2019 and April 2023, 44,669 adult patients met the eligibility criteria and were included in the analysis. Patients were grouped into three cohorts: non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), colorectal cancer (CRC), and other solid tumors. We evaluated the proportion of patients with at least one drug-based treatment recommended by an expert panel (PoTR) and the proportion who subsequently received an expert-panel-recommended treatment (PoTI). We also conducted exploratory multivariable analyses of factors associated with PoTR and, among patients who received a treatment recommendation, PoTI. The PoTR was 54.57% for NSCLC, 53.80% for CRC, and 39.92% for other solid tumors. The PoTI was 16.74%, 7.96%, and 7.74%, respectively. A substantial gap between treatment recommendation and implementation was observed across cancer types. Among the Cohort C organ groups, PoTI was higher in the prostate and breast groups and lower in the pancreatic and soft-tissue groups. Exploratory adjusted analyses showed that the associations of age, ECOG performance status, CGP panel, and cohort differed between the PoTR and conditional PoTI models. This nationwide analysis found substantial variation in treatment recommendation, recorded implementation, and the gap between them across the prespecified cancer cohorts. These descriptive findings may help frame patient counseling and expectations regarding treatment recommendation and subsequent implementation after CGP.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Gastrointestinal (GI) cancers account for a substantial cancer burden, yet contemporary incidence trends and future projections across cancer sites and demographic subgroups remain incompletely characterized. We aimed to analyze incidence trends from 2000-2022 and forecast rates through 2032 for eight major GI cancers in the United States. Using SEER Research Data (17 registries, 2000-2022), we identified patients with esophageal, gastric, liver, gallbladder, pancreatic, small intestine, and colorectal cancer. Age-adjusted incidence rates were calculated and stratified by sex, age group (<60 vs. ≥60 years), and race (White, Black, Asian/Pacific Islander, American Indian/Alaska Native). Time-series forecasting models (linear regression, ARIMA, ETS, NNAR) were applied to project incidence through 2032. Incidence trends varied markedly by cancer site. Pancreatic cancer showed sustained increases across most subgroups, with projected rates rising from 4.41 to 5.11 per 100,000 by 2032. Colorectal cancer demonstrated divergent age-specific patterns: incidence among individuals ≥60 years is projected to decline (25.48 to 14.89 per 100,000), while early-onset disease (<60 years) is expected to increase (5.35 to 5.84 per 100,000). Liver cancer incidence is forecast to decline (2.18 to 1.42 per 100,000). Esophageal and gastric cancers showed modest increases, while gallbladder cancer remained stable. Substantial disparities persisted by sex (male predominance for most sites, female predominance for gallbladder) and race (highest burden among Asian/Pacific Islander populations). GI cancer incidence trajectories are highly heterogeneous. The projected rise in pancreatic and early-onset colorectal cancers signals urgent needs for targeted prevention, risk-factor modification, and improved early detection strategies in at-risk populations.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cancer survivors face elevated risks of age- and treatment-related health conditions, possibly due to accelerated biological aging from cancer therapy. The role of social determinants of health (SDOH) in these aging trajectories remains understudied. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 109,224 curatively treated Danish cancer survivors (lung, breast, prostate, or colon cancer, diagnosed between 1997 and 2018) and 574,022 age- and sex-matched cancer-free individuals. SDOH was assessed using educational level and cohabitation status. Using national registries, we investigated associations between SDOH and 16 post-cancer new morbidities with Cox proportional hazard models and flexible parametric models. During a median 6.9-year follow-up, cancer survivors had significantly higher rates of new morbidities than cancer-free individuals. Lung cancer survivors had elevated hazard rates for 14 morbidities, breast cancer survivors had increased rates for 12 morbidities, prostate cancer survivors exhibited elevated rates for 8 morbidities, and colon cancer survivors had rates for 14 morbidities. Educational disparities were evident: survivors with short education had higher rates for chronic respiratory disease (HRs: 1.30-1.55 across cancer types), heart failure (HRs: 1.50-1.54 in breast and colon), diabetes (HRs: 1.67-1.95 in breast, prostate, and colon), and depression (HRs: 1.32-1.37 in breast and colon). Living alone was also associated with increased but less pronounced rates. Cancer survivors experience elevated rates for age- and treatment-related post-cancer new morbidities compared to cancer-free individuals. Sociodemographic disadvantages, particularly short education, further increase these rates. These findings suggest that SDOH play an important role in post-cancer aging, highlighting the need for targeted interventions addressing social determinants in survivorship care.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Repeat hepatectomies are challenging due to adhesions and altered anatomy. Robotic surgery, with enhanced dexterity and visualization, may expand the role of minimally invasive liver surgery (MILS) in this setting. The aim of this study was to explore the safety and efficacy of robotic repeat hepatectomy. We conducted a retrospective cohort study comparing repeat robotic (R-RLR), laparoscopic (L-RLR), and open liver resections (O-RLR) performed between January 2019 and December 2024. The primary outcome was postoperative morbidity. Secondary outcomes included conversion to laparotomy, use of Pringle maneuver, blood loss, hospital stay and postoperative mortality. For oncologic efficacy, rates of negative surgical margins (R0) or equivalent (R1 vascular), recurrences and survival were assessed. Forty-two patients underwent repeat hepatectomy (O-RLR = 15, L-RLR = 13, R-RLR = 14). Over time, O-RLR and L-RLR declined in favor of R-RLR. Main indications were colorectal liver metastases and hepatocellular carcinoma. Groups had similar age and comorbidities; however, cirrhosis and portal hypertension were more frequent in R-RLR. Mean Iwate scores were 6 (O-RLR), 4 (L-RLR), and 5 (R-RLR) (p = 0.240). Postoperative morbidity was significantly lower in L-RLR (7.6%) and R-RLR (7.7%) compared to O-RLR (40%) (p = 0.030). Mean Comprehensive Complication Index was 11.7 (O-RLR), 0.7 (L-RLR), and 0.6 (R-RLR) (p = 0.025). Two L-RLR cases required conversion. Pringle maneuver, blood loss, and hospital stay decreased progressively from O-RLR to L-RLR to R-RLR. There was no postoperative mortality.R0 resection was achieved in 73% (O-RLR), 100% (L-RLR), and 78.5% (R-RLR); R1 vascular rates were 13.3%, 0%, and 21.5%, respectively (p = 0.14). The three groups had similar overall and hepatic recurrence rates; survival (recurrence-free and overall) was also similar. Repeat robotic hepatectomy is safe and provides good oncologic outcomes. The robotic approach may allow MILS in more complex cases, including patients with cirrhosis and portal hypertension.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To evaluate the association between left colic artery (LCA) preservation during laparoscopic rectal cancer resection and the incidence of anastomotic leakage (AL) and perioperative outcomes. Clinical data were retrospectively collected from patients who underwent laparoscopic rectal cancer resection at the First Affiliated Hospital of Nanjing Medical University between July 2020 and February 2023. Patients were divided into an LCA-preservation group and a non-preservation group according to whether the left colic artery (LCA) was preserved intraoperatively. A 1:1 propensity score matching analysis was performed to balance baseline covariates, including sex, age, body mass index, comorbidities, American Society of Anesthesiologists classification, TNM stage, tumor differentiation, distance from the anal verge, and tumor size. Postoperative outcomes were subsequently compared between the two groups. A total of 500 patients were included, comprising 341 patients in the LCA-preservation group and 159 in the non-preservation group. Before matching, patients in the non-preservation group had more advanced TNM stages and a higher incidence of AL than those in the LCA-preservation group. After propensity score matching, baseline characteristics were well balanced between the two groups. The incidence of AL remained significantly higher in the non-preservation group than in the LCA-preservation group (P = 0.038). Operative time was significantly longer in the LCA-preservation group (P = 0.026), whereas no significant differences were observed in intraoperative blood loss, drainage volume on postoperative day 1, or postoperative length of hospital stay. In laparoscopic rectal cancer resection, LCA preservation was associated with a lower incidence of anastomotic leakage, potentially through the maintenance of proximal bowel perfusion. Although this technique may prolong operative time, it does not appear to increase other major perioperative adverse outcomes, supporting its potential clinical value.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Sphingolipids have emerged as critical bioactive molecules that orchestrate diverse cellular processes underlying cancer initiation, progression, and therapeutic resistance. Once considered structural membrane lipids, they are now recognized as dynamic regulators of proliferation, apoptosis, angiogenesis, metastasis, and immune evasion. Central to this biology is the ceramide and sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) balance, a metabolic switch that dictates cell fate between death and survival. However, accumulating evidence reveals that the "sphingolipid code" is cancer-type specific, shaped by the expression of distinct enzyme isoforms, metabolite profiles, and microenvironmental contexts. This review consolidates current knowledge on sphingolipid alterations across major malignancies, including hematological cancers, colorectal, gastric, pancreatic, breast, ovarian, endometrial, lung, glioblastoma, and melanoma. We have highlighted emerging common mechanistic themes, such as the roles of gangliosides in metastasis and chemoresistance driven by glucosylceramide synthase. Furthermore, we have discussed the therapeutic horizons of targeting sphingolipid metabolism, ranging from sphingosine kinase (SphK1/2) inhibitors and ceramide delivery systems to ganglioside-directed immunotherapy, with emphasis on preclinical and clinical advancements. By integrating sphingolipid biology with precision oncology frameworks, sphingolipids hold a promise as both therapeutic targets and biomarkers. Yet, challenges such as tumor heterogeneity, drug delivery barriers, and toxicity must be overcome to achieve positive clinical translations. Deciphering the sphingolipid code across cancers offers a transformative opportunity to unlock novel strategies for diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment, ultimately bridging basic lipid biology with personalized cancer therapy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To evaluate the visualization rates of the hypogastric and pelvic splanchnic nerves using magnetic resonance neurography (MRN) and to identify associated factors. This study included patients with rectal carcinoma who underwent preoperative MRN at our institution between December 2019 and September 2020. Two gastrointestinal surgeons evaluated the visibility of the hypogastric and pelvic splanchnic nerves on a per-nerve basis, with scores of "excellent" or "good" defined as successful visualization. The visualization rates of the hypogastric and pelvic splanchnic nerves were 21.6% and 81.8%, respectively. A large visceral fat area at the umbilical level (p = 0.0150) was an independent factor affecting the visualization rate of the hypogastric nerves. Early clinical T stage (cT1-3) (p = 0.0255) and a large visceral fat area at the level of the upper edge of the femoral head (p = 0.0096) were independent factors affecting the visualization rate of the pelvic splanchnic nerves. MRN demonstrated a high visualization rate for the pelvic splanchnic nerves but a low rate for the hypogastric nerves. Visualization appeared to be influenced by the visceral fat area and inflammatory responses or edema in surrounding structures.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal peritoneal metastases (PM) remain a major therapeutic challenge. Cytoreductive surgery (CRS) combined with hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC) offers prolonged survival in selected patients. Accurate preoperative assessment of resectability is crucial to avoid non-beneficial surgery. The Preoperative Predictive Score (PROP) integrates nine preoperative clinical and radiologic parameters to predict the completeness of cytoreduction (CC). This study aimed to externally validate the PROP Score in an independent European single-centre cohort. 63 Patients undergoing CRS ± HIPEC for colorectal PM between 2012 and 2022 were retrospectively analysed. PROP scores were calculated from preoperative data and compared with intraoperative CC scores (CC-0, CC-1, CC-2/3). Statistical analysis included χ², Spearman correlation, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve evaluation. Sixty-three patients were included (CC-0 = 41; CC-1 = 13; CC-2/3 = 9). Median PROP values increased with lower resectability (3.4 vs. 7.2 vs. 10.8; p < 0.001). A cutoff ≥ 6 predicted incomplete cytoreduction with 78% sensitivity and 90% specificity (AUC = 0.919). PROP correlated strongly with the Peritoneal Cancer Index (ρ = 0.673; p < 0.001). No 30- or 90-day mortality was observed. The PROP Score reliably predicts the likelihood of complete cytoreduction in colorectal PM using solely preoperative parameters. Moreover it is the first score which is able to preoperatively discriminate patients with a future CC-0 und CC-1 resection. Its external validation supports evidence-based patient selection for CRS ± HIPEC, optimizing surgical decision-making and resource utilization.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
It is estimated that about 20-30% cancer death is directly linked to the syndrome called cancer cachexia (CAC), which is characterized by debilitating skeletal muscle (SKM) and fat wasting. Recent studies have found that the myogenic ability of myogenic stem cells (MuSC) in the cachectic SKM is compromised, but the mechanisms remain to be clarified. Using the C26 colon cancer cells mediated cachexia model, the down-regulation of myogenic regulatory factors (MRF) MyoD and MyoG, but not Myf5 and Mrf4, was confirmed in vitro and in vivo. We further found the repression of myogenesis by C26 cells conditioned medium (C26M) in vitro could be rescued by inducible over-expression of either MyoD or MyoG, but not Myf5 or Mrf4. As MyoD is the major upstream activator of MyoG, these findings suggest the targeting of the MyoD-MyoG regulatory cascade by CAC signals. The transactivation of myogenic gene promoters by MyoD was also constantly repressed by C26M, suggesting MyoD dysfunction is critical to myogenesis repression in CAC. The repression of MyoD gene transcription by C26M was found to be mediated by the core enhancer (CE) located in the distal enhancer (DE) region. The activation of CE mediated promoter activity by MyoD, ß-Catenin*, and Pbx1 was significantly reduced by C26M, implying the repression of MyoD positive feedback loop. Taken together, these observations suggest that CAC signals repress both MyoD transactivational activity on target genes and its transcriptional activation by upstream activators, which subsequently leads to repression of myogenesis and failed regeneration in cachectic SKM.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Methyl-CpG-binding domain protein 4 (MBD4) is a base excision repair glycosylase that removes the thymine of a T:G mispair. If left unrepaired, these mismatches can cause C>T transitions. Human MBD4 uses an arginine finger, R468, to flip the mispaired thymine into its active site and to stabilize the orphaned guanine. MBD4 also possesses a second highly conserved arginine, R512, in close proximity to R468, whose role remains unknown despite an R512W mutation catalogued in colorectal cancers and an R512Q mutation reported in Myelodysplastic Syndromes. Here, we investigate the structural and functional significance of R512 using MBD4 variants R512A, R512K, R512Q, and R512W. We find that the native hydrogen-bonding network mediated by R512 is critical for active-site stability, and that R512K is the only variant to retain catalytic activity. This mutant preserves the wild-type rate of base excision despite a reduced affinity for the DNA substrate. Structural characterization of R512K MBD4 bound to T:G-mismatched DNA reveals an ordered water molecule in this pocket. This water molecule, along with the lysine amino group, retain 6 of the 7 native R512 hydrogen bonds, thereby preserving the local architecture of the enzyme. Comparative structural modeling of the catalytically inactive R512A, R512Q, and R512W variants suggests that loss of localized positive charge combined with disruption of the hydrogen-bonding network accounts for their inactivity. Together, these findings establish an essential role for R512 in catalytic activity and suggest how mutation of this residue can disrupt the BER pathway and contribute to tumorigenesis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
External exposures take time to accumulate and affect human health, leading to a time lag between initial exposure and the manifestation of clinical signs. Susceptible time window analysis aims to describe the relationship between the time since exposure and its effects. To obtain unbiased estimates in susceptible time window analysis, researchers may need to adjust for exposures measured at different times simultaneously. Conventional Cox proportional hazards models often fail in this regard due to the strong multicollinearity between lagged exposure terms. In addition to estimation challenges, missing data in historical exposures present another obstacle for long-term analysis. To address these challenges, we first impose flexible parametric models on the effects across historical exposures by assuming that they follow restricted cubic splines. Based on our proposed restricted cubic spline model, we develop two model selection algorithms to help researchers determine the optimal knot locations in the splines. Additionally, we propose using multiple imputations to handle the missing exposure data. We conducted simulation studies to evaluate the performance of the restricted cubic spline models and the imputation algorithms in various realistic settings. The results show that our model demonstrates strong performance, offering great flexibility and robustness to misspecified maximum length of effect. Compared to the complete-person-time analysis, our multiple imputation algorithm exhibits significantly lower variance, with only a slight increase in bias. Finally, as an illustrative example, we apply our proposed models to analyze the effect of folate consumption on colorectal cancer incidence in the Nurses' Health Study from 1976 to 2016.

Recurrence risk after hepatectomy for colorectal liver metastases (CRLMs) changes during follow-up, but whether baseline tumor burden remains prognostically relevant with increasing recurrence-free time is unclear. In supplementary expanded models, the associations remained directionally similar but were attenuated. Recurrence risk improved with increasing recurrence-free time, but survivors remained heterogeneous according to baseline tumor burden. Liver metastasis number retained prognostic relevance at early postoperative landmarks.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Portomesenteric venous thrombosis (PMVT) after colorectal cancer (CRC) surgery is most often reported in symptomatic patients, leaving its frequency and natural history across the asymptomatic spectrum poorly defined. When encountered incidentally, it frequently prompts anticoagulation, hypercoagulability evaluation, or delays in oncologic treatment, despite limited evidence that intervention alters its course. Using a cohort with routine postoperative imaging, we characterized the incidence, anatomic distribution, risk factors, and clinical course of asymptomatic PMVT. We retrospectively studied 799 consecutive patients who underwent CRC surgery between April 2019 and June 2025. All patients underwent standardized abdominal computed tomography (CT) on postoperative day (POD) 6 as part of our institutional clinical pathway for immediate postoperative follow-up. PMVT was defined radiologically, and thrombus location was classified as peripheral intrahepatic branches or main portal/superior mesenteric vein. Management followed a risk-stratified pathway of therapeutic anticoagulation or active surveillance, with radiologic resolution assessed on follow-up CT. Given the limited number of events, multivariable analysis was considered exploratory. Asymptomatic PMVT was identified in 33 patients (4.1%), none symptomatic at detection. Thrombi were predominantly confined to the distal intrahepatic branches. In exploratory multivariable analysis, age ≤ 60 years (OR 2.45, 95% CI 1.19-5.03, p = 0.015) and POD 5 WBC > 10 × 10 When postoperative imaging is routinely performed, asymptomatic PMVT after CRC surgery is detected in approximately 4% of patients. It is typically confined to peripheral intrahepatic branches, and follows a uniformly benign self-limiting course, even in patients managed without anticoagulation. These findings argue against reflexive anticoagulation and extensive workup for short-segment, non-occlusive PMVT confined to peripheral intrahepatic branches, and support an individualized, predominantly conservative approach. We do not advocate routine postoperative CT; rather, surgeons who encounter incidental PMVT can be reassured regarding its favorable prognosis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Describe the technical complications of hepatic artery infusion pump (HAIP) placement and characterize salvage rates. HAIP chemotherapy is an effective tool used in the treatment of hepatic malignancies and has become increasingly adopted at select centers. Much of the safety data is reported from small, newer programs or older, large series. Retrospective analysis of all patients who underwent HAIP placement at our institution between 2000 and 2022 was conducted. Pump salvage was defined as the ability to receive HAIP chemotherapy after a pump-associated complication. Pump failure was defined as an HAIP-related complication permanently stopping ongoing HAIP chemotherapy. Over the study period, 2935 patients had an HAIP placed for colorectal liver metastases (n=2582, 88%), intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (n=294, 10%) or another malignancy (n=59, 2%). Of all patients, 759 (26%) had an HAIP-related complication, with 404/759 (53%) having their pump salvaged. The most common complications were abnormal perfusion (n=360 [12%], 285/360 [79%] salvaged), arterial pseudoaneurysm and/or hemorrhage (n=117 [4%], 7/117 [6%] salvaged), and pump-pocket infection (n=115 [4%], 60/115 [52%] salvaged). The complications with the highest salvage rates were pump-pocket seroma (n=15/16, 94%), pump-flipping (n=41/44, 93%), and pump-pocket hematoma (n=45/49, 92%). Unsalvaged complications were catheter dislodgement from vessel (n=0/47, 0%), catheter erosion into bowel (n=0/25, 0%), and arterial thrombosis (n=0/19, 0%). The cumulative incidence of pump failure at 1 year in patients receiving adjuvant therapy was 6.6%, and 4.5% among those receiving palliative therapy. HAIP-related complications occur in about one quarter of patients, predominantly perfusion and pump-pocket complications. These are salvageable in the majority of cases with multidisciplinary interventions.

(A. vera) as an adjuvant to hydroxycamptothecin (HCPT) for CRC treatment and to explore the underlying mechanisms, specifically focusing on nucleotide metabolism, as perturbations in intracellular nucleotide pools are closely linked to various human pathologies. This effect was mediated by exacerbated DNA damage, imbalanced purine/pyrimidine metabolism, and inhibition of the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The five pore-forming gasdermins (GSDMs, namely GSDMA-E) are best known for executing pyroptosis, a lytic and highly inflammatory form of programmed cell death. Accumulating evidence over the past decade has unveiled diverse nonlytic functions of GSDMs in digestive homeostasis and disease. GSDMs preserve intestinal barrier integrity and mucosal immunity under physiological conditions, whereas their dysregulated activation fuels tissue injury across a spectrum of digestive diseases, including inflammatory bowel disease, acute intestinal injury, radiation enteritis, acute pancreatitis, and liver disorders. Notably, the functional outcome of GSDM activation is highly context-dependent: the same protein can be either protective or injurious. This duality extends to digestive oncology, where GSDM-mediated pyroptosis can stimulate or suppress antitumor immunity. GSDM-targeted drugs, including GSDMD agonists, GSDMD inhibitors, and GSDME inhibitors, have shown encouraging efficacy in preclinical models, although none have yet reached the clinic. Here, we review the dual roles of GSDMs across the digestive system, outline the mechanistic basis of their form-, cell-, and tissue-specific functions, and discuss the progress and remaining challenges in GSDM-targeted therapy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
BACKGROUND Colorectal cancer (CRC) is extremely rare in adolescents and often presents with advanced disease because of nonspecific symptoms. Deficient mismatch repair (dMMR) and microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) are important biomarkers that influence prognosis, treatment selection, and the need for genetic evaluation. We report the case of an adolescent with MSI-H-associated CRC presenting with acute intestinal obstruction. CASE REPORT A 16-year-old male initially underwent appendectomy for presumed acute appendicitis. Persistent postoperative bowel obstruction prompted computed tomography (CT), revealing a descending colon tumor requiring emergency Hartmann's procedure. Histopathology demonstrated mucinous adenocarcinoma, pT4N0M0, with vascular invasion. Immunohistochemistry showed loss of MSH2/MSH6 expression with retained MLH1/PMS2, indicating dMMR and findings highly suggestive of Lynch syndrome, although germline testing was unavailable. Molecular analysis identified a KRAS mutation without NRAS alterations. Given his multiple high-risk features, including T4 disease, bowel obstruction, vascular invasion, mucinous histology, and very young age, he received 12 cycles of adjuvant FOLFOX chemotherapy. Treatment was well tolerated, and he remains disease-free more than 5 years after completion of therapy. CONCLUSIONS This case highlights the diagnostic complexity of adolescent CRC and the need to consider colorectal malignancy in young patients with persistent or atypical abdominal symptoms. Routine MMR/MSI testing and comprehensive molecular profiling are essential in young-onset CRC to identify patients who may have hereditary cancer syndromes and require genetic counseling. Although limited to a single case, this report underscores the importance of multidisciplinary decision-making and individualized treatment based on clinicopathological and molecular characteristics, which may contribute to favorable long-term outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Early mobilization is a key component of enhanced recovery after elective colorectal surgery. This pilot trial evaluated the safety and feasibility of an early supervised postoperative exercise intervention in addition to standard care. In this single-center randomized controlled pilot trial, 31 patients undergoing elective colorectal surgery were randomized to an intervention group (n = 16) or control group (n = 15). One patient withdrew after randomization, leaving 30 patients for modified intention-to-treat analysis. The intervention consisted of individualized, physiotherapist-supervised exercise sessions on postoperative days 1, 3, and 5. The control group received standard postoperative care according to the institutional ERAS protocol. The originally registered primary endpoint was time to first bowel movement; prior to final analysis, safety and feasibility were designated as the primary outcomes in accordance with the pilot nature of the study. The change was documented transparently. Secondary outcomes included physical performance (Short Physical Performance Battery [SPPB], handgrip strength), time to first bowel movement, patient-reported outcomes, and postoperative complications. Thirty patients completed the study (retention 96.8%). Adherence to the intervention was 100%, and no intervention-related adverse events occurred. The intervention group showed significantly better preservation of physical performance, reflected by a more favorable change in SPPB score from baseline to postoperative assessment. No significant between-group differences were observed for time to first bowel movement, handgrip strength, postoperative complications, or other secondary outcomes. Early supervised postoperative exercise after elective colorectal surgery was safe and feasible. Although no differences were found for most secondary outcomes, the intervention improved postoperative physical performance. These exploratory findings warrant confirmation in adequately powered randomized trials. German Clinical Trials Register, DRKS00036327 (retrospectively registered, 22.04.2025).

Colorectal cancer liver metastasis (CRLM) remains a major cause of cancer mortality, yet the metabolic mechanisms that remodel metastatic RNA-splicing programs are poorly defined. Here, integrated quantitative proteomics and lysine 2-hydroxyisobutyrylation (Khib) proteomics of patient-matched normal mucosa, primary CRCs, and liver metastases revealed a progressive increase in global Khib, with enrichment on RNA-splicing proteins. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Radiation-induced intestinal injury (RIII) remains a severe complication of radiotherapy. Although p53 activation is known to be protective, no clinically available p53 activators exist. Different p53 activation dynamics (transient or sustained) are linked with radio-sensitivity, yet their therapeutic relevance to RIII has not been explored. The emerging role of N6-methyladenosine (m6A) in radiation injury is recognized, but the mechanistic link between m6A and p53 signaling in RIII remains elusive. Here, we investigated how m6A regulates p53 signaling, as well as the functional consequences and mechanisms of transient or sustained p53 activation via pharmacologically targeting m6A in RIII. After radiation, m6A writer METTL3 increases m6A on MDM2 mRNA, which is recognized by m6A reader IGF2BP3, upregulating MDM2 and suppressing intestinal p53. Then, METTL3 inhibitor S-Adenosylhomocysteine (SAH) was used to induce transient or sustained p53 activation. Functionally, a single dose of SAH suppressed MDM2 and induced transient p53 activation, thereby protecting against RIII, whereas multiple dosing induced sustained p53 activation but failed to confer a protective benefit. Mechanistically, transient p53 activation prevented RIII by stimulating YAP signaling and revival stem cells (revSCs) regeneration, a newly defined stress-induced intestinal stem cell population, whereas sustained p53 activation failed to. Importantly, SAH did not protect colorectal cancer cells from radiation. Together, these findings reveal that radiation inhibits intestinal p53 expression through the METTL3/m6A/IGF2BP3/MDM2 axis, and that transient p53 activation via METTL3 inhibition offers a promising protective strategy for RIII through YAP-mediated revSCs regeneration.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
6-O-Carboxypropyl-α-tocotrienol (T3E), a derivative of α-tocotrienol, has been reported to exert anticancer activity. However, the molecular determinants underlying T3E-induced cytotoxicity in cancer cells remain unclear. Recent studies have reported that ion transporters play important roles in cancer cell survival. In this study, we investigated whether ion transporters are involved in the cytotoxic effects of T3E in colorectal cancer (CRC) cells. T3E exerted cytotoxic effects in multiple CRC cell lines, while showing minimal cytotoxicity in immortalized normal colonic epithelial cells. The cytotoxicity of T3E was markedly attenuated by syrosingopine, an inhibitor of monocarboxylate transporter 1 (MCT1) and 4 (MCT4). Knockdown of MCT1 significantly attenuated T3E-induced cytotoxicity, whereas knockdown of MCT4 significantly enhanced the cytotoxic effects of T3E. T3E induced cytotoxicity in CRC cells through inducing endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, and inhibition of MCT1 partially attenuated T3E-induced ER stress. Our findings demonstrate that MCT1 is involved in T3E-induced cytotoxicity in CRC cells and suggest a potential pharmacological strategy targeting MCT1-dependent cytotoxicity.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Research over the past two decades has repositioned exercise from a general lifestyle recommendation to a potential anticancer intervention. Pooled analyses of more than 1.4 million participants link regular physical activity with lower incidence of at least 13 tumour types, and prospective cohort data report cancer-specific mortality 24-31% lower among the most active patients with breast, colorectal, prostate and lung cancer, although these estimates derive from observational designs using self-reported activity. In 2025, a phase III trial in stage III colon cancer provided the first randomised evidence that a structured exercise and behaviour-change programme improves disease-free and overall survival after adjuvant chemotherapy; a randomised trial in ovarian cancer subsequently did not show a progression-free survival benefit. Candidate mechanisms include insulin and growth-factor signalling, myokine secretion, immune mobilisation, reduced chronic inflammation and gut microbiome remodelling, although these rest on evidence ranging from cell culture to human trials and are rarely distinguished by level. Despite this evidence, structural, educational and economic barriers prevent integration of exercise into routine oncology care. This Review synthesises the available evidence and identifies the steps required for clinical adoption.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the leading causes of death globally. Chemotherapy is considered as one of the standard treatment option for CRC. Although effective in many cases, drugs used in chemotherapy are often associated with adverse toxicity. Inter-individual variations in drug response are often attributed to pharmacogenomic associations, and current evidence suggests involvement of gut microbes as a contributor to drug response variations. While several studies have implemented machine learning to predict drug responses mediated by gut microbial enzymes, these predictions mainly rely on substrate information and bacterial genome data. In this study, we have developed CRCGMMeta Predictor, a tool that predicts gut microbial enzymes and species capable of biotransforming drugs. Unlike existing tools, CRCGMMeta Predictor integrates enzyme prediction with species-level abundance in CRC metagenomes using eight geographically diverse metagenomic studies. The tool was trained on 437,079 species-specific enzyme data, incorporating 3457 substrate and protein-encoding features. Multiple machine learning models were evaluated, with the random forest model achieving 99% accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score and ROC-AUC metrics. Validation of the generated model with a blind set achieved 97% accuracy, while 10-fold cross-validation achieved an accuracy of 0.831 ± 0.068. Based on the above results, the random forest model was selected to build the CRCGMMeta Predictor tool. This was further assessed against fluoropyrimidine drugs and its ability to predict enzymes supported by literature evidence and those predicted by existing computational tools. These findings highlight the potential of CRCGMMeta Predictor in identifying microbiome-mediated drug responses.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colon cancer is a life-threatening gastrointestinal malignancy in which Hedgehog (Hh) signaling plays a critical role, yet no Hh pathway inhibitor is clinically approved for its treatment. This study aimed to design and synthesize thiadiazole-based Hh pathway inhibitors and evaluate their anti-colon cancer activity and mechanism. A series of thiadiazole derivatives were synthesized from pyrazole boronic acid and 2,5-dibromothiadiazole via nucleophilic substitution, Suzuki-Miyaura coupling, and tert-butoxycarbonyl deprotection, with structures confirmed by The target compounds were structurally confirmed. SEZ13 exhibited the strongest Hedgehog inhibition, outperforming Vismodegib. BODIPY-cyclopamine assay, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations confirmed its binding to smoothened. SEZ13 dose-dependently inhibited HCT116 and HT-29 cell proliferation. At 30 μM, SEZ13 significantly suppressed migration and invasion, induced apoptosis, and caused G2/M arrest (P < 0.05). Mechanistically, SEZ13 significantly downregulated Gli1 and Patched-1 mRNA and Gli1 protein expression (P < 0.05). SEZ13, a novel thiadiazole derivative, binds smoothened and exerts anti-colon cancer activity by inhibiting the Hedgehog/Gli1 signaling pathway.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a malignant tumour with an extremely high global incidence rate; its development and progression are closely linked to fibroblasts within the tumour microenvironment (TME). In recent years, single-cell and spatial multi-omics technologies have revealed the high heterogeneity of fibroblasts in colorectal cancer and identified multiple subtypes with either oncogenic or tumour-suppressive functions. Within the TME, these fibroblast states have been associated with key processes in tumour initiation, progression, metastasis, and treatment resistance, although direct functional evidence for many of them remains to be established. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the origins, differentiation and activation trajectories, stage-associated distribution patterns, and spatial characteristics of fibroblasts, with a focus on newly identified functional states and their distributions across primary and metastatic CRC. Furthermore, given that the efficacy of current clinical treatments for fibroblasts remains less than satisfactory, there is still a need to develop effective targeted therapies for these newly identified subtypes in the future.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To investigate survival outcomes in frail, older patients with colorectal cancer who were deemed non-operable despite technically resectable tumors, compared to propensity score matched patients who underwent curative-intent surgery. This was a propensity score-matched retrospective cohort study. Overall survival was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. A univariate Cox proportional hazards model was applied to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and their corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CIs). From a total of 1667 patients, assessed at the Department of Surgery, Zealand University Hospital, Denmark, between January 1, 2020, and April 30, 2024, 67 were deemed non-operable and 805 patients underwent elective, curative intent surgery. After applying PSM, each study cohort included 36 patients. Both, before and after propensity score matching, surgery was significantly associated with better survival, HR: 11.73, 95% CI: 8.48-16.21, p < 0.01 and HR: 5.06, 95% CI: 2.57-9.95, p < 0.001, respectively. The results of the sensitivity analysis were consistent. In the propensity score-matched cohort, curative intent surgery was significantly associated with longer overall survival compared with patients who were deemed non-operable.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Tumor-adjacent mucosa is commonly used as a normal reference in colorectal cancer (CRC) transcriptomic studies, but its relationship with distant normal mucosa and tumor tissue remains unclear. Here, we performed bulk RNA sequencing of paired distant normal, adjacent, and tumor tissues from 25 patients with CRC and used these three tissue states to construct an ordered normal-adjacent-tumor (N-A-T) expression continuum. Although adjacent mucosa was globally closer to distant normal mucosa and showed no significant differential expression by pairwise analysis, a limma-based linear trend model identified widespread monotonic transcriptional changes along the N-A-T continuum. Tumor-directed genes were enriched in translation, RNA processing, cell-cycle activity, and proliferation-related pathways, whereas genes decreasing along this axis were associated with oxidative metabolism and epithelial homeostasis. A trend gene-based N-A-T score positioned adjacent mucosa between normal and tumor tissues in external bulk cohorts and was associated with proliferative and immune-low molecular states in CRC. Single-cell RNA-seq analysis localized this signal mainly to epithelial cells and associated higher scores with proliferative and stem-like epithelial states. In conclusion, CRC-adjacent mucosa is not fully equivalent to distant normal mucosa but carries coordinated tumor-directed transcriptional changes mainly associated with epithelial-cell programs.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
In patients with anorectal malformations (ARM), perineal wound complications following posterior sagittal anorectoplasty (PSARP) remain a challenge with an occurrence of 22%-43%. In adults, vacuum-assisted closure (VAC) aims to support wound healing after colorectal procedures. In children evidence is limited, suggesting a potential benefit of VAC therapy after PSARP. We aimed to evaluate the impact of VAC therapy on outcomes after PSARP in a multicenter comparative study. All consecutive patients who underwent PSARP from 01/2018-12/2025 in two participating pediatric surgical departments were included. Complications including postoperative perineal wound dehiscence were analyzed. The study was approved by the local ethics committee (approval number: 12354-BO-K-2026). 48 patients were included: 26 with and 22 without VAC therapy. Baseline characteristics, follow-up duration and the interval until first follow-up were comparable between cohorts respectively. Postoperative outcomes did not differ significantly between groups. Stool smearing occurred in none of the patients in the VAC cohort and in one patient in the non-VAC cohort (p > 0.99). No incontinence was observed in either cohort (p > 0.99). Perineal wound dehiscence occurred in two patients (8%) in the VAC and in one (5%) in the non-VAC cohort (p > 0.99). In our study, VAC therapy was associated with comparable rates of postoperative wound dehiscence after PSARP compared to the non-VAC cohort and to previous reports. Larger, prospective studies are required to confirm our findings.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To reassess pretreatment photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT)-derived normalized iodine concentration (NIC) in an expanded rectal-cancer cohort, using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-derived apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) as a within-cohort reference marker for histopathologic treatment response. This single-center retrospective study included 63 patients with rectal adenocarcinoma who underwent pretreatment pelvic MRI and contrast-enhanced PCCT, followed by neoadjuvant treatment and surgical resection. Dworak tumor regression grades 0-1 were classified as poor response (n = 22) and grades 2-4 as moderate/good response (n = 41). MRI and PCCT were performed a median of 3 days apart (IQR, 1-4.5). The previously reported NIC threshold of ≥ 0.36 was reassessed without re-optimization. Twenty-one of 63 patients overlapped with the preceding pilot cohort; therefore, the present study is an expanded reassessment rather than an independent external validation. Twenty-two patients showed poor response and 41 moderate/good response. ADC interobserver agreement was excellent (ICC, 0.959; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.90-0.98). In the 61 patients with paired numeric NIC measurements from both observers, NIC interobserver agreement was also excellent (ICC, 0.905; bootstrap 95% CI, 0.858-0.936). Mean ADC was lower in poor responders than in moderate/good responders (0.876 ± 0.186 vs. 1.035 ± 0.208 × 10⁻³ mm²/s; p = 0.003; AUC, 0.738; 95% CI, 0.608-0.867). NIC did not differ between groups (median, 0.313 vs. 0.370; p = 0.91; AUC, 0.509; 95% CI, 0.362-0.656). Applying the previously published NIC threshold ≥ 0.36 yielded sensitivity 53.7%, specificity 63.6%, and accuracy 57.1% for Dworak grades 2-4. Adding NIC to ADC did not improve model fit (likelihood-ratio p = 0.601). In this exploratory expanded cohort, lower pretreatment ADC was associated with Dworak grades 0-1. Single-phase portal-venous NIC measured with the described two-dimensional ROI approach did not reproduce the high performance reported in the pilot study and showed no evidence of improved model fit beyond ADC in this cohort. These findings require independent prospective validation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Fecal occult blood testing is a widely used diagnostic method for the early detection of colorectal cancer and the assessment of gastrointestinal pathologies in humans. For preclinical research purposes, we developed a cost-effective, non-invasive luminol-based chemiluminescent assay to detect fecal occult blood in murine feces that can function as a predictive tool, with sufficient sensitivity to correlate with disease severity. Fecal samples were collected and weighed, solubilized in a sodium hydroxide solution, then combined with luminol and hydrogen peroxide and immediately analyzed using a luminometer. Luminol reacts with the iron in hemoglobin to produce a measurable chemiluminescent signal; therefore, known hemoglobin concentrations from mouse blood, quantified using a hemoglobinometer, were used to generate a standard curve along with feces from naïve mice. The method was validated against standard Guaiac paper slide tests for accuracy. We demonstrated a strong correlation with disease severity metrics, including colonoscopy findings and tumor burden in multiple models of colon cancer, offering an accessible, non-invasive, and inexpensive alternative for routine monitoring of disease progression. The application of this technique can be broadened to other murine models of gastrointestinal pathologies, such as peptic ulcers, inflammatory bowel disease, Crohn's disease, and gastritis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Activating mutations in phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate 3-kinase catalytic subunit alpha (PIK3CA) and B-Raf proto-oncogene (BRAF) are hypothesized to confer primary resistance to anti-epidermal growth factor receptor (anti-EGFR) monoclonal antibodies in metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC). However, the clinical impact of these mutations in patients with rat sarcoma (RAS) wild-type tumors remains incompletely characterized. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the association of PIK3CA and BRAF mutations with clinical outcomes in RAS wild-type mCRC patients receiving first-line EGFR inhibitor therapy. A systematic literature search was conducted across PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Google Scholar, and OVID from inception through June 2019, following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. From 600 screened records, 10 studies comprising 1,478 patients with RAS wild-type mCRC were included. Pooled hazard ratios (HRs) for progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS), and risk differences (RDs) for objective response rate (ORR), were calculated using fixed- or random-effects models with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). PIK3CA mutations were associated with significantly worse PFS (HR, 1.38; 95% CI, 1.11-1.71; p = 0.004) and OS (HR, 1.58; 95% CI, 1.22-2.05; p < 0.001). BRAF mutations were similarly associated with worse PFS (HR, 1.68; 95% CI, 1.46-1.94; p < 0.001) and OS (HR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.09-1.49; p = 0.003). No significant difference in ORR was observed for either PIK3CA mutations (RD, -0.12; 95% CI, -0.38 to 0.15; p = 0.38) or BRAF mutations (RD, -0.12; 95% CI, -0.28 to 0.04; p = 0.15) compared with wild-type. These findings confirm that PIK3CA and BRAF mutations are negative prognostic biomarkers in RAS wild-type mCRC, associated with inferior PFS and OS but not ORR. Incorporating BRAF and PIK3CA mutation testing into pretreatment evaluation is supported, and alternative therapeutic strategies for mutation carriers are needed. Prospective validation in larger studies is warranted.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Anastomotic leak (AL) has a reported incidence of 3%-19% after colorectal resection. The aim of this Preferred Reporting Items of Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses (PRISMA) 2020 compliant systematic review is to determine whether intraoperative indocyanine green fluorescence angiography (ICG-FA) reduces clinically significant anastomotic leak and improves peri-operative outcomes compared with standard white-light assessment in adults undergoing colorectal resection with primary anastomosis. We searched MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), and Web of Science from inception to March 2026. Eligible study designs included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) enrolling adults undergoing elective colorectal resection with primary anastomosis and comparing intra-operative ICG-FA with standard white-light assessment. The primary outcome was "clinically relevant anastomotic leak" as defined by the International Study Group of Rectal Cancer. Six RCTs enrolling 4,366 randomised patients, of whom 4,221 were evaluable: FLAG (n=377), De Nardi et al. (n=240), EssentiAL (n=839), AVOID (n=931), ICG-COLORAL (n=1,136), and IntAct (n=698). EssentiAL was the only trial to demonstrate a statistically significant reduction in all-grade AL (7.6% (32/422) vs 11.8% (49/417); relative risk (RR) 0.645; p=0.041) and grade B/C AL (4.7% (20/422) vs 8.2% (34/417); p=0.044). AVOID, ICG-COLORAL, and IntAct did not meet their primary endpoints but consistently favoured left-sided resections in subgroup analyses. IntAct showed an absolute five percentage-point reduction in grade B/C AL (10% (36/343) vs 15% (54/355); adjusted odds ratio (OR) 0.667; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.419-1.060; p=0.087). No serious ICG-related adverse events were reported. Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) certainty of evidence for the primary outcome was moderate. Current RCT evidence does not support routine ICG-FA across all colorectal anastomoses. Leak rates are most consistently reduced for left-sided and low rectal resections where inferior mesenteric artery (IMA) ligation may compromise anastomotic perfusion.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Resistance to cetuximab is a major challenge in colorectal cancer (CRC). Here, we show that IPO5, an importin mediating RASAL2 nuclear import, contributes to cetuximab resistance. Screening six CRC cell lines revealed an inverse correlation between IPO5 expression and cetuximab sensitivity, with higher IPO5 levels in resistant (RKO and SW620) than sensitive (LoVo and Caco2) cells. IPO5 knockdown in resistant cells restored cetuximab sensitivity, induced apoptosis (upregulated active caspase-3/BAX and downregulated BCL-2), and suppressed proliferation and xenograft growth, whereas IPO5 overexpression in sensitive cells reduced sensitivity. Mechanistically, IPO5 facilitates RASAL2 nuclear translocation via its nuclear localization signal, depleting cytoplasmic RASAL2 and increasing GTP-bound RAS to sustain AKT and MAPK activation. Consistently, IPO5 and downstream Ras effectors were elevated in resistant LoVo-CR cells. Collectively, our findings identify the IPO5/RASAL2 axis as a key contributor to cetuximab resistance in CRC by disrupting the cytoplasmic localization of RASAL2 and activating the RAS/MAPK and PI3K/AKT pathways.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1) is the most common adult-onset muscular dystrophy and is increasingly recognized as a cancer predisposition syndrome, with 2- to 8.5-fold elevated risks of endometrial, ovarian, thyroid, and colorectal cancers. Evidence on the oncological management of DM1 patients-including perioperative care, chemotherapy tolerability, and cancer surveillance-remains scarce. A 56-year-old woman with DM1 developed four primary malignancies over 16 years: papillary thyroid carcinoma at age 40, breast carcinoma at age 49, and synchronous endometrial carcinoma and low-grade serous ovarian carcinoma at age 56. Progressive respiratory muscle weakness necessitated tracheostomy and nocturnal ventilation from age 49, and DM1 was diagnosed at age 50. Three general anesthesia surgeries were completed without complications under multidisciplinary DM1-tailored perioperative protocols. For FIGO stage IIIB ovarian carcinoma, four cycles of paclitaxel-carboplatin chemotherapy were administered without dose reduction. First-degree atrioventricular block and left ventricular function remained stable, and treatment was discontinued for Grade 2 nausea rather than a DM1-specific toxicity. Standard-intensity multimodal cancer treatment was feasible in this DM1 patient with appropriate perioperative and cardiac monitoring. DM1 should be recognized as a cancer predisposition syndrome, and individualized surveillance strategies analogous to those used in hereditary cancer syndromes warrant further investigation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC), is a highly prevalent malignant tumor worldwide, and early screening is key to improving its prognosis. Currently, CRC screening research is growing exponentially, but its core research hotspots, evolutionary trends, and interdisciplinary features are not clear. In this study, we used bibliometric analysis to analyze the distribution of literature, research hotspots, and cutting-edge developments in the field of CRC screening worldwide, and to provide a scientific basis for optimizing screening strategies. Publications on CRC screening from 2015 to 2024 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. VOSviewer (v1.6.20), RStudio (v4.4.1), and CiteSpace (v6.4.2) were used for bibliometric and visual analyses. The main analyses included publication trends, countries, authors, journals, references, and keywords. A total of 3245 publications were included in the analysis. Global publications on CRC screening showed a steady upward trend over the past decade, with an annual growth rate of 2.17%. The United States contributed the highest number of publications, and the University of North Carolina ranked as the most productive institution. GASTROENTEROLOGY and GUT were the most frequently cited journals in this field. Lansdorp‑Vogelaar I was among the most prolific authors. The most cited article was "CRC screening for average-risk adults: 2018 guideline update from the American Cancer Society." Keyword analysis showed that the research hotspots in this field included colonoscopy, biomarker, adenoma detection rate, artificial intelligence, etc. Current research in CRC screening focuses on traditional screening methods, population-related factors, and emerging technologies, particularly artificial intelligence. Stronger international collaboration and interdisciplinary studies are needed to advance the field.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal carcinoma (CRC) remains a major cause of cancer mortality in the United States (U.S.); however, contemporary long-term projections by demographic and geographic strata are limited. This study examined national colorectal cancer mortality trends from 1999 to 2025 and projected age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) through 2050. We conducted an ecological time-series analysis of U.S. adults aged ≥ 25 years using Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Wide-ranging Online Data for Epidemiologic Research Multiple Cause of Death data. CRC-related deaths were identified by any mention of International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision codes C18-C20 on the death certificate. AAMRs per 100,000 population were calculated overall and stratified by sex, age group, race and ethnicity, urbanization, census region, state, and place of death. Joinpoint regression was used to estimate the annual percent change and average annual percent change. A demographically optimized ensemble forecasting model was used to project AAMRs from 2026 to 2050. From 1999 to 2025, 1,674,393 CRC-related deaths were recorded. Overall, the AAMR declined from 38.11 in 1999 to 23.14 in 2025 (average annual percent change, -1.99%; 95% confidence interval, -2.13 to -1.85; P < .001), but recent rates have stabilized. The mean AAMR was higher among men than women (34.13 vs 23.43) and higher in nonmetropolitan than metropolitan areas (32.43 vs 28.49). Non-Hispanic Black adults had the highest racial and ethnic burdens (37.45). Adults aged 25 to 44 years showed a significant increase in mortality (annual percent change, 1.13%; 95% confidence interval, 0.93 to 1.33; P < .001). Most deaths occurred at home (41.15% of deaths). The overall AAMR was projected to continue declining slowly, from 23.02 in 2026 to 21.56 in 2050, at a slower pace than the 1999 to 2016 decline. U.S. CRC mortality has declined substantially and is projected to continue declining slowly through 2050, rather than resume its earlier faster decline, with persistent sex, racial, rural, age, and geographic disparities. Targeted strategies are needed to improve screening completion, diagnostic follow-up, rural access, equity, and early-onset colorectal cancer detection.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Endoscopic self-expandable metal stent (SEMS) placement is an established palliative treatment for malignant gastrointestinal (GI) obstruction, but data on its use in patients eligible for subsequent conversion therapy remain limited. We describe our single-center experience with SEMS placement in advanced and recurrent GI malignancies and report the proportions of patients who subsequently completed antitumor therapy and underwent R0 resection. We retrospectively reviewed 148 consecutive patients with advanced or recurrent GI malignancies who underwent SEMS placement for malignant obstruction or fistula at a single center between January 2019 and December 2022. Technical success, clinical success, fistula closure, adverse events, subsequent antitumor therapy, R0 resection, and overall survival were assessed. All analyses were descriptive and exploratory; no adjustment for confounding was performed. Gastrointestinal SEMSs were successfully placed in 146 patients (98.6%). The overall obstruction-relief rate was 95.7%, and the overall fistula-closure rate was 80%. No patient in this cohort required rescue gastrostomy or colostomy because of failed stent therapy during the study period. A total of 132 patients (94.3%) completed antitumor treatment after endoscopic metal stent placement (EMSP). R0 resection was performed in 8.89% of patients with esophageal malignancies, 10.10% of those with gastric malignancies, and 17.9% of those with colorectal malignancies. Median survival time (MST) was generally longer among patients who underwent conversion surgery than among those who did not. Comorbidities, anemia, and SEMS-related adverse events were also analyzed as factors associated with conversion therapy after SEMS placement; the respective P values were .039, <.001, and .012. In this retrospective single-center series, SEMS placement was technically feasible and relieved obstruction or closed fistulas in most patients with advanced or recurrent GI malignancies; a subset subsequently completed antitumor therapy and underwent R0 resection. These data support feasibility and demonstrate associations but cannot establish a survival benefit; prospective comparative studies are required.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Oxaliplatin, a platinum-based chemotherapeutic widely used in colorectal, hepatobiliary, and pancreatic malignancies, commonly causes a symmetric, cold-induced sensory neuropathy. Rarely, it has been linked to immune-mediated Guillain-Barré Syndrome (GBS), which can be misattributed to drug-induced sensory neuropathy and delay diagnosis. Distinguishing the two is critical because GBS can progress to respiratory failure and death. A 77-year-old woman with concurrent metastatic cholangiocarcinoma and colorectal carcinoma developed acute, symmetric, ascending motor weakness with clinically preserved sensation approximately 2 weeks after her last cycle of gemcitabine, oxaliplatin, leucovorin, and 5-fluorouracil (GOLF), rapidly progressing to an inability to ambulate. Neurological examination and cerebrospinal fluid analysis (albuminocytologic dissociation) were consistent with GBS, and nerve conduction studies demonstrated absent motor and sensory responses, indicating a severe axonal variant (AMSAN); sensory involvement was electrodiagnostic rather than clinical. An extensive infectious, autoimmune, and paraneoplastic workup was negative, supporting a diagnosis of presumed oxaliplatin-related GBS; a Naranjo score of 4 indicated a "possible" drug association. She received 5 sessions of therapeutic plasma exchange followed by 4 sessions of intravenous immunoglobulin. No meaningful neurological recovery occurred; she developed progressive respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation and died. Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for GBS in patients on platinum-based chemotherapy who develop abrupt, symmetric motor weakness after common causes have been ruled out. Because causality is difficult to establish, the association remains presumed; early recognition, prompt immunotherapy, and pharmacovigilance are essential to reduce mortality.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Natural orifice specimen extraction surgery (NOSES) has emerged as an advanced minimally invasive technique that eliminates abdominal wall incisions for specimen retrieval; nevertheless, comparative data on its efficacy relative to conventional minilaparotomy-assisted extraction in colorectal cancer (CRC) remain limited. This retrospective analysis was conducted on 126 patients who underwent laparoscopic CRC resection at our institution, allocated to either the NOSES group (transanal specimen extraction, n = 49) or the conventional group (minilaparotomy-assisted extraction, n = 77), comparing perioperative parameters, postoperative recovery indicators, complication rates, and pathological outcomes. The NOSES group demonstrated significantly shorter time to first flatus (2.3 ± 0.9 vs 2.9 ± 1.1 days, P = .002), time to first liquid diet (3.1 ± 1.0 vs 3.8 ± 1.3 days, P = .001), and postoperative hospital stay (8.4 ± 3.2 vs 10.1 ± 4.1 days, P = .014). Visual analog scale pain scores on postoperative day 1 were significantly lower in the NOSES group (3.2 ± 1.1 vs 4.5 ± 1.3, P < .001), with reduced additional analgesic requirements (22.4% vs 44.2%, P = .014). Overall complication rates were significantly lower in the NOSES group (12.2% vs 24.7%, P = .043), with wound infections occurring exclusively in the conventional group (0% vs 6.5%, P = .045). No significant differences were observed in operative time, estimated blood loss, anastomotic leakage, lymph node yield, or R0 resection rate (all P > .05). In conclusion, NOSES appears to be a safe and feasible alternative to conventional minilaparotomy-assisted specimen extraction in highly selected patients with CRC, offering advantages in postoperative pain control, gastrointestinal function recovery, and wound-related complication reduction without compromising oncological integrity.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Insomnia is closely associated with tumors and is recognized as a risk factor for cancer development. This two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) study investigated the potential causal link between genetically determined insomnia and various cancers, including brain, colorectal, esophageal, gastric, hepatic bile duct, liver, lung, malignant lymphoma, pancreatic, skin, and thyroid cancers. Summary statistics from genome-wide association studies for insomnia and eleven cancer types were examined. instrumental variables (IVs) were selected from single nucleotide polymorphisms that passed strict quality control for minimal linkage disequilibrium and genome-wide significance. All IVs demonstrated strong predictive power for insomnia, with F-statistics exceeding the conventional threshold of 10. The primary analysis was conducted using the inverse variance weighted method. Sensitivity analyses were performed using MR-Egger regression, weighted median, and weighted mode methods to test robustness, pleiotropy, and heterogeneity. MR analysis suggested potential causal associations between insomnia and increased risk of hepatic bile duct cancer (odds ratio [OR] = 4.458, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.074-18.493, P = .040), reduced risk of hepatic cancer (OR = 0.312, 95% CI: 0.100-0.973, P = .045), and reduced risk of skin cancers (OR = 0.599, 95% CI: 0.439-0.818, P = .001). However, after Bonferroni correction (adjusted threshold P < .0045), these associations did not retain statistical significance. No notable causal influence of these cancers on insomnia was observed. Sensitivity analyses showed no evidence of reverse causality or significant bias. These findings, though not retaining statistical significance after stringent multiple testing correction, provide suggestive evidence that genetically predicted insomnia may influence the risk of certain cancers, potentially through mechanisms involving genetic predisposition and biological pathways that modulate inflammation, immune function, and circadian rhythms. The study highlights the translational value of understanding insomnia's role in cancer risk, suggesting that clinicians should consider this association when managing patients with insomnia. Further research with larger sample sizes is warranted to validate these findings.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Pulmonary thromboembolism (PTE) is a severe and potentially fatal complication in patients with malignancy. Systemic inflammation plays an important role in both cancer progression and thrombogenesis. This study aimed to evaluate the association of systemic inflammatory indices with in-hospital mortality and clinical risk classification in patients with malignancy-associated PTE. This retrospective study included 75 adult patients diagnosed with both malignancy and PTE at a tertiary chest diseases center between February 2018 and June 2025. Demographic characteristics, cancer types, laboratory values at diagnosis, treatment details, and clinical outcomes were recorded. Neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio (LMR), lymphocyte-to-CRP ratio (LCRPR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), and systemic inflammation response index (SIRI) were calculated from blood samples obtained at diagnosis. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality, and the secondary outcome was the association between systemic inflammatory markers and ESC PTE clinical risk classification. The mean age was 69.5 ± 11.8 years, and 56% of patients were male. Lung (24%), colorectal (13.3%), and breast (9.3%) cancers were the most common malignancies. In-hospital mortality was 20%. Neutrophil count (P = .026), NLR (P = .032), and lactate (P = .027) were significantly higher in patients who died during hospitalization. ROC analysis identified an NLR cutoff value of 4.95, with a sensitivity of 86.7% and a specificity of 51.7%. Neutrophil count and SIRI were significantly higher in the intermediate-risk group (P = .036 and P = .049, respectively), whereas troponin was highest in the high-risk group (P < .001). Neutrophil count, NLR, and lactate levels were associated with in-hospital mortality in patients with malignancy-associated PTE. Neutrophil count and SIRI were also associated with ESC clinical risk classification. These findings should be considered exploratory and require validation in larger prospective studies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal dysplasia represents an early stage of colorectal carcinogenesis and is closely associated with chronic inflammation and altered microRNA (miRNA) expression. Probiotic strains such as Weizmannia coagulans (formerly Bacillus coagulans) and Saccharomyces boulardii possess anti-inflammatory properties and may influence host miRNA expression, suggesting their potential as prophylactic agents against inflammation-associated colorectal dysplasia. Mice received prophylactic oral administration of Weizmannia coagulans or Saccharomyces boulardii beginning one week before azoxymethane/dextran sulfate sodium (AOM/DSS) induction and continuing throughout the experimental period. Histopathological examination, TNF-α immunohistochemistry, serum pro-inflammatory cytokine measurements, and miRNA expression profiling using reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) were performed to evaluate the prophylactic effects of both probiotic strains. Prophylactic administration of both probiotic strains significantly attenuated early dysplastic alterations and inflammatory cell infiltration compared with the AOM/DSS group (p < 0.05). These histopathological improvements were accompanied by significantly lower serum levels of the pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-6 and IL-1β, together with reduced TNF-α immunoreactivity (p < 0.05). In addition, probiotic pretreatment attenuated the altered miRNA expression profile induced by AOM/DSS. Compared with the model group, expression of miR-122-5p, miR-29b-5p, and miR-15b-5p was significantly reduced, whereas miR-98-5p, miR-202-5p, miR-21-5p, and let-7i-5p showed increased expression and were associated with miRNA expression patterns that more closely resembled those of the control group (p < 0.01). Prophylactic administration of Weizmannia coagulans and Saccharomyces boulardii reduced inflammation-associated early dysplastic changes while preserving normal miRNA expression patterns in an AOM/DSS-induced murine model. These findings support the potential of probiotic prophylaxis as an early preventive strategy against colorectal dysplasia and provide a foundation for future studies investigating its clinical applicability.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To make informed choices in health-related discrete choice experiments (DCEs), respondents need to understand the choice scenarios, alternatives, attributes and attribute levels presented to them. Respondent populations are often highly diverse in knowledge and experience, leading to varying informational needs that make it challenging to design educational materials that sufficiently inform all respondents without disengaging others. At present, however, structured guidance on developing DCE educational materials is lacking. Drawing on the instructional design literature, this paper investigates whether theory-driven adaptations to educational materials improve respondent comprehension and engagement in health-related DCEs. Informed by three focus groups on DCE informational needs, we identified four design principles from the instructional design literature relevant to DCE educational materials: whole-task instruction, making inferences explicit, adapting information to respondents' prior knowledge and embedding self-check questions with corrective feedback. Educational materials for three existing DCEs (influenza vaccination, colorectal cancer screening and rheumatoid arthritis prevention) were redesigned to incorporate these principles. Panel respondents (N = 1754) were randomized to receive either the original or the adapted educational materials, and effects on comprehension, engagement, internal validity and choice consistency were assessed. Adapted materials increased time spent on educational content and were associated with small improvements in selected comprehension outcomes, though effects were often not statistically significant against the co-created comparator. Self-check questions revealed considerable comprehension gaps regardless of condition, underscoring that co-creation and pre-testing alone do not guarantee sufficient respondent comprehension. Educational materials also emerged as a meaningful source of selective dropout in all surveys, predominantly among respondents with lower education levels, posing a risk to sample representativeness that warrants attention in future research. Adapting DCE educational materials based on educational theory and instructional design principles offers a promising approach to improving respondent engagement and understanding. To enable cumulative learning, we further encourage researchers to report comprehension outcomes and publish educational materials as supplementary materials.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Early-onset locally advanced rectal cancer presents unique challenges in treatment and prognosis. This study aimed to develop and validate a prognostic nomogram for patients aged 18-50 years with locally advanced rectal cancer treated with neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy, addressing the lack of tailored prognostic tools for this growing patient population. Using the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database, we analyzed 2,853 patients who received neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy between 2010 and 2020. Patients were divided into training (n = 1,990) and validation (n = 863) cohorts. Cox proportional hazard regression models identified prognostic factors for overall survival (OS) and cancer-specific survival (CSS). Nomograms were constructed and validated using Harrell's C-index and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Independent predictors of poor OS and CSS included male sex, unmarried status (particularly divorced/separated/widowed), non-Hispanic black and American Indian/Alaskan native races, advanced T stage, increased positive regional nodes, and positive carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA). The nomogram demonstrated good discriminative ability in the validation cohort, with area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.767 and 0.742 for 3-year OS and CSS, respectively, and 0.705 and 0.697 for 5-year OS and CSS, respectively. The developed nomogram and identified prognostic factors provide valuable tools for individualized risk stratification and treatment optimization in young patients with locally advanced rectal cancer. These findings can aid in clinical decision-making and patient counseling. However, further external validation and prospective evaluations are necessary to confirm the clinical utility of this prognostic model in diverse healthcare settings.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Complete mesocolic excision (CME) for right-sided colon cancer is technically demanding due to substantial variability in mesenteric vascular anatomy. Patient-specific three-dimensional (3D) vascular reconstructions may improve preoperative planning by enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of anatomical analysis. This study assessed the impact of 3D reconstructions on anatomical accuracy and interpretation time compared with conventional CT. This retrospective, single-centre comparative study used a cross-over design. Portal-venous phase CT scans were analysed using either conventional CT interpretation or patient-specific 3D vascular reconstructions (Visible Patient®, Strasbourg, France). Readers with different levels of experience assessed right colonic arterial and venous anatomy. Anatomical accuracy and interpretation time were compared using mixed-effects models accounting for reader- and patient-related effects. Thirty patients and fourteen readers (seven junior and seven senior) were included, yielding 840 imaging assessments. Anatomical accuracy was significantly higher with 3D reconstructions (adjusted OR 2.05, 95% CI 1.76-2.40; P<0.001), independently of reader experience and reading sequence. Median interpretation time was significantly shorter with 3D reconstructions compared with conventional CT (150 s [110-232] vs. 335 s [203-500], P<0.0001). In multivariable analysis, 3D reconstructions remained independently associated with reduced interpretation time, with a stronger effect in junior (-60%) than senior readers (-35%). Patient-specific 3D vascular reconstructions improve both the accuracy and efficiency of preoperative anatomical assessment for right-sided colon surgery compared with conventional CT interpretation. These findings support their integration into preoperative planning for CME, with potential benefits for surgical standardisation and training.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) is a clinically important biomarker for cancer diagnosis and prognosis, particularly in colorectal cancer. This investigation introduces a simplified approach for the purification of native CEA antigen from the ascitic fluid of patients with colorectal cancer. Moreover, the technique allows the characterization of CEA though ensuring its structural and functional integrity is preserved. The CEA purification was achieved using perchloric acid precipitation, tangential flow filtration and sequential chromatography. The isolated CEA showed a relative molecular mass of ∼200 kDa and was analyzed using SDS-PAGE, size-exclusion FPLC and immunoblotting, confirming high purity comparable to reference form of native CEA protein. Peptide mass fingerprinting of trypsin-digested and deglycosylated CEA antigen identified it as CEACAM5_HUMAN (Uniprot ID: P06731). The proposed method demonstrates the adaptability for larger volume and practical approach for production of native form of CEA protein, also potential utility for future diagnostic applications, clinical research and bioanalytical studies.
