ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The association between serrated polyp detection rates, including proximal serrated polyp detection rate (PSPDR), and postcolonoscopy colorectal cancer (PCCRC) remains unestablished. We investigated PCCRC incidence and characteristics, and explored associations of PSPDR and adenoma detection rate (ADR) with PCCRC in colonoscopy- and fecal immunochemical test (FIT)-based screening within the Screening of Swedish Colons (SCREESCO) trial. Data from participants who underwent colonoscopy in the colonoscopy and FIT arms were analyzed. PCCRC, defined as colorectal cancer (CRC) diagnosed >6 months after a colonoscopy that did not detect CRC, was identified through linkage with cancer registries. Associations between PSPDR and PCCRC incidence were assessed using Cox models. Of 9982 and 5875 individuals in the colonoscopy and FIT arms, PCCRC was identified in 20 and 17 individuals, with 3-year PCCRC rates of 5.9% (3/51) and 3.5% (4/115), respectively. Compared with screening-detected CRC, PCCRC more often involved right-sided location and advanced stage. The 5-year cumulative incidence of PCCRC was 0.16% (95%CI 0.10%-0.27%) and 0.06% (95%CI 0.02%-0.15%) when colonoscopies were performed by endoscopists with low vs. high PSPDR (<10% vs. ≥10%), respectively. Among endoscopists with high ADR, 5-year PCCRC incidence was 0.13% (95%CI 0.04%-0.32%) vs. 0.06% (95%CI 0.02%-0.16%) for those with low vs. high PSPDR, respectively. Within this group, PCCRC incidence over 8 years decreased as PSPDR increased (hazard ratio per percentage-point increase, 0.90; 95%CI 0.82-1.00; P = 0.04). Despite the limited number of PCCRC events, this study suggests that PSPDR provides complementary information beyond ADR for identifying colonoscopies with higher PCCRC incidence.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Predictive models, as applied in computational pathology, are typically evaluated by accuracy, while their residuals are discarded as errors. In this paper we show that these residuals contain structured biological information. We introduce and validate a conditional discordance framework that uses foundation model prediction residuals to identify tissue regions where morphology and transcriptome diverge. The framework, applied to Xenium spatial transcriptomics data from 18 breast carcinoma sections across 2 cohorts, revealed spatially organized prediction errors with biological associations that varied across patients. In discovery, discordant regions showed higher EPCAM/KRT19 expression and lower expression of several stromal/macrophage markers, while cell mixture associations differed between patients. In two sections of P07, discordant regions enriched in tumor cells showed greater underprediction of transcription associated with EMT after composition adjustment, without a robust increase in observed program expression. Gene predictability is associated with spatial autocorrelation. Observed expression directions agreed across cohorts for 71 of 90 bridge genes; validation pathway profiles were more similar within patients, although the permutation test allowed only nine assignments (p=1/9). Application to four colorectal specimens supported broader use of the framework. The framework shows that prediction residuals carry biological information about microenvironmental heterogeneity, without identifying a universal EMT state.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Accurate polyp segmentation is a critical step in the early diagnosis of colorectal cancer. Existing methods commonly suffer from two limitations: insufficient exploitation of intra-layer channel subspaces, and the inability to explicitly handle highly ambiguous boundary pixels under reverse-attention paradigms. To address these issues, we propose FBB-HFNet, a hierarchical feature fusion network that integrates a grouped channel attention enhancement block (GCAEB) and a foreground-background-boundary attention block (FBBAB). The GCAEB partitions encoder features into parallel subspaces and applies independent channel attention to capture complementary channel-subspace cues. The FBBAB explicitly decomposes the predicted probability map into three confidence maps, corresponding to foreground, background, and boundary confusion, from which a deterministic estimator constructs a prototype for each region, and then adaptively aggregates context through a learnable regional prototype attention, effectively alleviating foreground-background confusion near polyp contours. Extensive experiments on five public benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed method achieves competitive or superior performance against current state-of-the-art methods.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) represents a major cause of cancer-associated morbidity and mortality worldwide, with significantly higher incidence and lethality in elderly individuals. Growing evidence implicates immunosenescence, the age-dependent functional decline of the immune system, as a key contributor to CRC initiation, progression, and therapeutic resistance. In this review, telomere attrition, impaired DNA repair, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and epigenetic remodeling are discussed as interconnected molecular processes that contribute to immunosenescence. These processes disrupt immune homeostasis and promote chronic inflammation. Moreover, functional alterations in macrophages, natural killer cells, neutrophils, and T lymphocytes further enable immune evasion and immunosuppressive niche formation. Furthermore, the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) orchestrates inflammaging and reprograms the CRC microenvironment via pro-inflammatory cytokines, chemokines, and growth factors. Gut-specific factors, including microbiota dysbiosis, intestinal barrier dysfunction, and microbial metabolites, further accelerate immune aging and tumorigenesis. In addition, metabolic reprogramming interacts bidirectionally with immunosenescence. By integrating molecular, cellular, microbial, and metabolic insights, this review offers a comprehensive understanding of immunosenescence in CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The epithelial cell adhesion molecule (EpCAM) is frequently overexpressed in colorectal cancer (CRC) and thus represents an attractive therapeutic target. However, the clinical efficacy of EpCAM-targeting antibodies has been limited by suboptimal binding properties and reliance on immune effector mechanisms. Here, we describe the development and characterization of anti-EpCAM #126, a fully human monoclonal antibody isolated from the OPAL phage-display library, and its corresponding antibody-drug conjugate (ADC). Anti-EpCAM #126 exhibited substantially higher binding affinity than adecatumumab, primarily owing to a markedly lower dissociation rate. High-density peptide microarray analysis and alanine-scanning mutagenesis identified NGSKLGRRAK (residues 74-83) within the EpCAM extracellular domain as the dominant epitope, with S76, R81, and K83 serving as key contact residues. Binding was conformation-dependent and markedly decreased following trypsin-mediated proteolytic cleavage of the epitope region. Anti-EpCAM #126 demonstrated robust staining of CRC xenograft and patient-derived tumor tissues and exhibited low cytokine release in human peripheral blood mononuclear cells and mouse models. Following the confirmation of efficient receptor-mediated internalization, anti-EpCAM #126 was conjugated to monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE) through a protease-cleavable valine-alanine linker, generating an ADC with a controlled average drug-to-antibody ratio of 4.31 while retaining nanomolar EpCAM-binding affinity. The resulting ADC exhibited potent cytotoxicity against EpCAM-expressing CRC cell lines and achieved 84.96% tumor growth inhibition in a patient-derived xenograft model at 10 mg/kg, whereas the unconjugated antibody showed no antitumor activity. These findings suggest that anti-EpCAM #126-MMAE is a high-affinity, epitope-specific ADC with promising preclinical efficacy against EpCAM-positive CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Postoperative skeletal muscle deterioration is associated with impaired recovery and adverse outcomes after colorectal cancer (CRC) surgery, but preoperative circulating markers of subsequent muscle loss remain insufficiently defined. We evaluated whether circulating musclin was associated with postoperative skeletal muscle status and longitudinal skeletal muscle index (SMI) change. This retrospective single-center study included 106 adults undergoing CRC surgery, of whom 95 had postoperative computed tomography (CT) data. Postoperative CT was obtained at a median of 198 days (IQR, 151-220; range, 73-685 days) after preoperative CT. CT-derived body composition was quantified at the third lumbar vertebra, and serum musclin and natriuretic peptides (NPs) were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. The primary outcome was postoperative SMI; greater than 5% SMI loss, percentage SMI change, and longitudinal musclin change were also evaluated. Higher preoperative musclin was associated with higher postoperative SMI in the fully adjusted model (B = 1.872; 95% CI, 0.765-2.979; p = 0.001). Greater than 5% SMI loss occurred in 27 of 95 patients, and higher preoperative musclin was associated with lower odds of this outcome (OR = 0.529; P = 0.038) and with a more favorable percentage SMI change (B = 3.941; P = 0.004). Absolute musclin change was positively associated with postoperative SMI in the baseline-adjusted analysis (B = 5.067; P < 0.001). Musclin-NP interaction terms were not significant. Preoperative circulating musclin was associated with postoperative skeletal muscle status and longitudinal SMI change after CRC surgery. These findings support further prospective evaluation of musclin as a candidate circulating marker of postoperative skeletal muscle vulnerability.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is characterized by marked epithelial heterogeneity and dynamic tumor-microenvironment interactions. However, epithelial states associated with progression across the normal-adenoma-carcinoma sequence remain incompletely defined. Single-cell RNA sequencing data from normal colorectal mucosa, adenoma, and tumor tissues were analyzed using inferCNV, Monocle, Slingshot, CytoTRACE, CellChat, and SCENIC. An OLFM4⁺ tumor cell risk score (OTRS) was constructed using Cox and LASSO regression, and TIMP1 function was evaluated in vitro. Eight major cell types and nine tumor epithelial subtypes were identified. C3 OLFM4⁺ cells showed elevated transcriptional activity, stemness, metabolic activity, and greater representation in carcinoma than adenoma tissues. Trajectory analyses positioned these cells in an early-to-intermediate transitional state. CellChat predicted prominent fibroblast-C3 OLFM4⁺ interactions, including a putative WNT2B-FZD/LRP axis, while SCENIC identified XBP1, NFIA, PPARG, HDAC2, and UBE2K as subtype-associated regulators. The C3 OLFM4⁺-derived OTRS stratified prognosis; high OTRS was associated with poorer survival, macrophage-enriched infiltration, higher stromal, immune, and TIDE scores, and differential predicted drug sensitivity. TIMP1 knockdown suppressed malignant behaviors in CRC cells. C3 OLFM4⁺ cells represent a stem-like, metabolically active tumor epithelial state associated with CRC progression, fibroblast-derived WNT signaling, immune-evasion-related features, and unfavorable prognosis. The OTRS model may support prognostic and therapeutic assessment, while TIMP1 contributes to malignant CRC cell behavior.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colonic diverticular disease is becoming increasingly common in Japan, paralleling population aging and changes in lifestyle and medication use. The predominance of right-sided diverticulosis in Asian populations, in contrast to the left-sided predominance in Western populations, influences clinical presentation and management. In Japan, diverticulitis has become a clinically important problem, and diverticular bleeding is currently the most frequent cause of acute lower gastrointestinal bleeding (LGIB). The Japanese Gastroenterological Association updated its clinical guidelines for diverticular bleeding and diverticulitis in 2026. Key domains including epidemiology, diagnostic and therapeutic strategies, and priority clinical and future research questions were addressed. Evidence was graded using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach, and recommendations were formulated via a modified Delphi process with external review. These guidelines aim to provide Japanese and Asian evidence-based consensus that complements Western guidelines. Recommendations for acute LGIB and diverticular bleeding are as follows: risk stratification with the Shock Index and Oakland and NOBLADS scores guides triage; pre-colonoscopy contrast-enhanced computed tomography is the widely used diagnostic modality; routine colonoscopy within 24 h is not suggested for all patients; endoscopic band ligation or direct clipping is suggested post-detection of stigmata of recent hemorrhage; and early oral refeeding is suggested. Recommendations for diverticulitis are as follows: post-resolution colonoscopy is suggested to exclude colorectal cancer; outpatient treatment and withholding of antibiotics are suggested in selected uncomplicated cases; and primary anastomosis may be favored over Hartmann's procedure in selected complicated cases.

Postpolypectomy surveillance intervals derived from colonoscopy findings and histopathology should be guideline-based, yet these are frequently not adhered to, contributing to under- and oversurveillance. This motivates a more structured and automated approach to improve adherence. We developed and evaluated an automated, implementable, guideline-aligned decision support tool that extracts colorectal polyp features from free-text colonoscopy and histopathology reports and produces auditable surveillance recommendations. We extracted paired colonoscopy and histopathology reports from a National Health Service (NHS) trust and designed a 4-stage prompting pipeline using open-weight large language models to separate multispecimen histopathology reports into individual containers ("pots"), align endoscopic findings with specimens, and normalize each pot into a structured schema. The surveillance intervals were then computed by a deterministic rule engine encoding guideline rules. We evaluated extraction performance on 100 procedures (215 pots), assessed surveillance recommendation performance on a same-site cohort (n=100), and performed external validation on a cohort from a second trust (n=100). A separate retrospective audit compared automated recommendations and observed routine scheduling against a clinician-derived reference based on full electronic health record review in 127 patients. Key extraction fields showed end-to-end accuracy (specimen type=0.995; location=0.981; diagnosis=0.981; excision completeness=0.949), with mean report-level pot comprehensiveness of 0.968 (SD 0.112). Overall surveillance recommendation accuracy was 0.96 (95% CI 0.90-0.98) at Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust (GSTT) and 0.93 (95% CI 0.86-0.97) at Sandwell and West Birmingham NHS Trust (SWB) and showed strong class-level performance (no follow-up This hybrid approach using open-weight large language models for structured extraction and guideline-encoded rules for decision-making can generate accurate, lightweight, and auditable postpolypectomy surveillance recommendations. Such a tool has the potential to improve safety netting and guideline adherence in NHS colonoscopy workflows.

We performed a retrospective analysis of 386 patients with one of the following cancers: breast, colorectal, non-small cell lung, melanoma, or renal cell carcinoma. In the pan-cancer cohort, landmark analysis at 3 months post-surgery revealed that patients with MRD-positivity had significantly inferior systemic DRFS compared to ctDNA-negative patients (HR: 23.7, p < 0.0001). Additionally, ∼30% improvement in 24-month systemic DRFS was observed among adjuvant-treated MRD-positive patients, whereas MRD-negative patients derived no clear benefit from adjuvant therapy. In the longitudinal setting, MRD positivity anytime post-definitive treatment surveillance significantly correlated with shorter systemic DRFS compared to serial MRD negativity (HR: 104.7, p < 0.0001). Tumor-specific analyses yielded similar findings. Notably, 62% (72/116) of patients had ctDNA detected in the ultra-sensitive range of < 100 ppm. Our findings underscore the robust clinical performance of the Signatera Genome assay for MRD detection across solid tumors. Its broad applicability and high specificity support its integration into clinical practice and prospective trials.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Robotic surgery offers potential advantages for the surgical management of rectal cancer; however, robust data on its use in locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) populations are limited. We aimed to evaluate the long-term oncological and perioperative outcomes of robotic surgery in a cohort of patients treated at a single tertiary referral cancer centre. In this retrospective study, 105 consecutive patients who underwent robotic surgery for rectal adenocarcinoma between July 2012 and May 2024 at a specialist UK centre were analysed. Patient demographics, tumour characteristics, perioperative outcomes (margin status, complications and conversion rate) and survival (disease-free survival [DFS] and overall survival [OS]) were assessed. The cohort was predominantly male (68.6%) with a median age of 63 (interquartile range 56-70) years. 89.5% of patients had LARC with 53.3% low rectal tumours and 13.3% requiring pelvic exenteration. Neoadjuvant therapy was used in 88.6%. An R0 resection was achieved in 86.7%. The conversion rate to open surgery was low at 0.9%. Clavien-Dindo Grade ≥ III complications occurred in 13.3%, with no 90-day mortality. After a mean follow-up of 53.7 months, the 5-year OS and DFS were 76% and 65%, respectively. Robotic surgery for LARC in a specialised referral setting is safe and feasible, achieving very low conversion rates and zero perioperative mortality. While the R1 and complication rate reflects the cohort's complexity, it is comparable to benchmarks for advanced pelvic malignancies. These findings endorse the robotic platform for treating challenging rectal cancers within a dedicated multidisciplinary framework.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Fluorogenic RNA aptamers have emerged as powerful molecular tools for cancer imaging, biosensing, and biomarker detection due to their high specificity, low background fluorescence, and genetic encodability. These short RNA molecules activate fluorescence upon binding specific fluorogens, enabling real-time visualization of intracellular targets and dynamic molecular processes in living systems. Recent advances in RNA structural engineering, fluorophore optimization, and biosensor integration have significantly expanded the translational applications of fluorogenic aptamers in oncology. This mini-review summarizes the structural principles, fluorescence activation mechanisms, and cancer-related applications of fluorogenic RNA aptamers and related nucleic acid biosensors. Foundational studies describing the architecture of fluorogenic aptamer families, including Spinach, Broccoli, Mango, Pepper, Squash, and Beetroot, are discussed with emphasis on G-quadruplex-mediated fluorogen stabilization and fluorescence enhancement. Furthermore, recent developments in CRISPR/Cas-assisted fluorogenic biosensors, dual-color RNA imaging systems, fluorogenic DNAzymes, and amplification-driven aptamer platforms are highlighted. Direct applications across multiple malignancies, including brain, breast, colorectal, liver, lung, prostate, and skin cancers, demonstrate the growing utility of these technologies for tumor-associated RNA detection, epigenetic biomarker analysis, molecular imaging, and therapeutic monitoring. In addition, advances in fluorescence brightness, structural stability, and multiplex imaging strategies have improved the sensitivity and adaptability of fluorogenic RNA systems for complex biological environments. Despite current limitations related to RNA stability, intracellular delivery, and tissue penetration, fluorogenic RNA aptamers represent highly promising tools for next-generation precision oncology. Continued integration with nanotechnology, live-cell imaging, artificial intelligence, and molecular diagnostics is expected to enhance further their clinical and translational potential in cancer research and personalized medicine.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, necessitating the identification of novel bioactive compounds with therapeutic potential. Trans-vaccenic acid (TVA), a primary ruminant-derived trans fatty acid, possesses diverse biological activities; however, its cellular effects in CRC and its association with miRNA expression and downstream targets remain to be fully characterized. In this study, HT-29 human CRC cells were exposed to increasing concentrations of TVA (0-800 µM). Cell viability was evaluated using the MTT assay, and apoptotic cell populations were quantified using Annexin V-FITC/PI flow cytometry alongside Hoechst 33,342 nuclear staining. The expression levels of apoptosis-, lipid metabolism-, and cell survival-related genes (BAX, CASP3, CASP8, CASP9, MCL1, BCL2, SCD1, and GPR34), as well as candidate miRNAs predicted via miRWalk 2.0, miRDB, and TargetScan, were analyzed by RT-qPCR and ELISA. TVA reduced HT-29 cell viability in a dose-dependent manner, with an IC₅₀ value of 251.13 µM at 24 h. Hoechst staining revealed apoptotic nuclear changes and apoptotic body formation, while Annexin V-FITC/PI flow cytometry confirmed a predominant increase in late apoptotic cells (p < 0.001). At the molecular level, TVA treatment significantly increased the expression of pro-apoptotic markers (BAX, CASP3, CASP8, and CASP9) and reduced anti-apoptotic (MCL1, BCL2), lipid homeostasis/tumor survival (SCD1), and oncogenic survival signaling (GPR34) markers (p < 0.05). Concurrently, TVA administration was associated with increased expression of candidate miRNAs (let-7e-5p, let-7b-5p, miR-519d-3p, miR-582-5p, and miR-381-3p; p < 0.05), accompanied by changes in the expression of their predicted target transcripts. TVA exerts cytotoxic and pro-apoptotic effects in HT-29 cells, accompanied by favorable shifts in lipid metabolism/survival gene expression and candidate miRNA profiles. While these correlative findings support the bioactive potential of TVA in CRC, further studies incorporating multiple cell lines and functional miRNA validation (e.g., mimic/inhibitor transfections) are required to establish direct mechanistic causality.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The clinical implementation of precision oncology remains challenged by intratumoral heterogeneity, complex tumor microenvironment interactions, and the limited predictive value of conventional preclinical models. 3D cancer spheroids have emerged as physiologically relevant platforms that closely mimic in vivo tumor architecture, cellular heterogeneity, hypoxic gradients, and treatment resistance mechanisms. This review highlights the growing role of cancer spheroids in drug panel testing and their application in personalized therapeutic decision-making across diverse malignancies, including breast, colorectal, ovarian, lung, head and neck, and brain cancers. Patient-derived spheroids and multicellular co-culture models preserve critical tumor-stroma and tumor-immune interactions, enabling clinically meaningful evaluation of chemotherapeutic agents, targeted therapies, immunotherapies, radiosensitizers, and combination treatment strategies. Drug panels assessed using spheroid platforms encompass platinum-based agents, EGFR and VEGF inhibitors, PARP inhibitors, immune checkpoint inhibitors, kinase inhibitors, antibody-drug conjugates, and emerging pathway-directed therapeutics. Accumulating evidence suggests that spheroid-based drug testing has the potential to recapitulate clinically relevant tumor characteristics and treatment responses and may serve as a useful preclinical approach for evaluating drug sensitivity, exploring resistance mechanisms, and assessing biomarker-associated responses within clinically relevant timeframes. Recent advances in high-throughput screening, microfluidic technologies, organ-on-chip systems, automated imaging, and artificial intelligence-driven analytics have further improved the scalability, reproducibility, and translational utility of these models. The review also discusses the current limitations, standardization challenges, and ethical considerations associated with spheroid-based drug testing. Collectively, personalized cancer spheroids represent a promising approach linking experimental oncology with precision medicine research, with potential applications in individualized drug testing and treatment optimization.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Histone deacetylase inhibitors (HDACi) have emerged as promising anticancer agents. This study aimed to investigate the antitumor efficacy and molecular mechanism of ITF2357 (Givinostat), a novel HDACi, in colorectal cancer (CRC). In vitro, CT26 cell viability, proliferation, colony formation, and cell cycle distribution were assessed. In vivo, a subcutaneous CT26 tumor model was established in female BALB/c mice to evaluate the antitumor effect of ITF2357. Multi-omics analysis (miRNA-seq, mRNA-seq, ATAC-seq) was performed to identify key regulatory molecules, followed by qRT-PCR, dual-luciferase reporter, and knockdown assays for mechanistic validation. ITF2357 significantly inhibited CT26 cell proliferation and induced G0/G1 phase arrest. In vivo, ITF2357 suppressed tumor growth without affecting body weight or liver and kidney tissues, suggesting no obvious systemic toxicity. Multi-omics analysis revealed that ITF2357 upregulated miR-1938, which directly targeted the 3'-UTR of ADAM12. ADAM12 knockdown phenocopied the anti-proliferative and cell cycle arrest effects of ITF2357. Clinically, high ADAM12 expression correlated with poor prognosis in CRC patients. ITF2357 exerts anti-CRC activity by upregulating miR-1938 to suppress ADAM12, leading to cell cycle arrest. These findings provide new mechanistic insights into the anti-CRC effects of ITF2357 and establish a foundation for exploring its therapeutic potential in CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Early cancer detection through screening can improve treatment outcomes. However, screening uptake remains lower among some communities, including Muslim women, which puts them at risk of late diagnosis and poor outcomes. In 2020, we worked with 10 Scottish Muslim women to co-design a peer-led, faith-based and culturally tailored intervention to encourage uptake of breast, bowel and cervical cancer screening. The intervention was delivered twice online and qualitatively evaluated. The study was subsequently funded as a feasibility trial, and the intervention was delivered a further 16 times, both online and face-to-face. This paper reports findings from a qualitative evaluation exploring participants' perspectives on the acceptability and implementation of the intervention. The intervention is a 2-h workshop comprising four components: (1) a peer-led cancer screening discussion, (2) a doctor-led health education session, (3) testimonials from Muslim women, and (4) an Islamic perspective delivered by a female religious scholar. In 2024, women participated in online or in-person workshops in North-East England and Scotland. After each workshop, women were invited to participate in focus groups or interviews to provide feedback on the workshop. Qualitative data collection and analysis were guided by the Theoretical Framework of Acceptability. Data were analysed using the Framework Analysis method. A convenience sample of 36 women was recruited. Participants described the workshop's content as comprehensive and providing new information. The workshop's informal atmosphere and use of different delivery methods enhanced information attainment. They appreciated the use of interpreters, who assisted non-English speakers. Bringing a medical and Islamic perspective together was novel to participants and made the workshop more impactful. Participants expressed more positive attitudes towards screening after the intervention. A peer-led, culturally-tailored and faith-based intervention for improving cancer screening uptake for Muslim women was deemed acceptable. However, more work is needed to assess the intervention's effectiveness and impact. The intervention was co-designed with 10 Muslim women. A public involvement group worked with the research team throughout the study; they provided their views on the intervention, recruitment, data collection and interpretation of findings. Some were trained as peer educators to help deliver the intervention. Two members of the community (FH and CS, who are also listed as authors) were also employed on the project as Community Recruitment Leads, facilitating participant recruitment and contributing to all stages of the research as valued members of the research team, ensuring the community's voice was embedded throughout.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
DNA methylation is an important epigenetic modification and has been widely used as a biomarker for disease diagnosis, particularly in cancer screening. However, conventional quantitative methylation-specific PCR (qMSP) often lacks single-CpG-site resolution because the methylation states of neighboring CpG sites within primer or probe binding regions can interfere with amplification efficiency. In this work, we report a novel Hairpin Competition qMSP (HC-qMSP) strategy for precise DNA methylation analysis at single-CpG-site resolution. In this method, degenerate bases were introduced at non-target CpG positions within the primer and probe binding regions to eliminate interference from adjacent CpG sites. Meanwhile, a specially designed hairpin primer was introduced so that the extension product forms a hairpin structure that competes with the reverse primer during amplification, enabling selective amplification of methylated templates while suppressing unmethylated sequences. Under optimized conditions, the HC-qMSP assay achieved a discrimination sensitivity down to 0.1%, and showed good linearity across a wide dynamic range. The method was further validated using colorectal cancer tissues and stool samples, successfully distinguishing cancer samples from normal controls. Owing to its simplicity, low cost, and compatibility with conventional real-time PCR platforms, HC-qMSP provides a promising approach for precise DNA methylation analysis and potential clinical diagnostic applications.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Copyright: © 2026 El-Deiry et al. This is an open access article distributed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY 4.0), which permits unrestricted use, distribution, and reproduction in any medium, provided the original author and source are credited. Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, with a complex molecular profile that impacts tumor behavior and treatment response. This case report discusses a 52-year-old female diagnosed with Stage IIIc colon cancer, exhibiting KRAS, TP53, IDH1, and APC mutations, as well as a tumor microenvironment with high PD-L1 expression and elevated VEGFR1 and VEGFR3. Despite surgical resection and adjuvant treatment which included FOLFOX, FOLFIRI with bevacizumab and local radiation, the patient’s disease was difficult to track due to small, non-FDG-avid lymph nodes in the aortocaval region and persistent circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA). Following a review by an international Molecular Tumor Board (MTB), maintenance therapy options were discussed, including the personalized combinations of regorafenib, sulindac, and metformin, or fruquintinib, sulindac, and metformin, based on the patient’s molecular alterations. Alternatively, 5-FU with or without bevacizumab was suggested. In the event of relapse, the MTB recommended the combination of regorafenib, sulindac, and metformin, with the addition of trametinib and ivosidenib. The combination of regorafenib, ipilimumab, and nivolumab (RIN) was also considered due to the patient’s high PD-L1 expression. Further clinical trial options, such as pan-RAF inhibitors, NK cell agonists, and TAS-102 with bevacizumab, were also discussed. Additionally, the potential combination of PD-1 and TGFβ inhibitors was explored. This case underscores the critical role of molecular profiling in tailoring personalized treatment strategies for advanced CRC, providing novel avenues for managing recurrent disease, even in the absence of measurable disease.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
We evaluated 10 years of QOPI implementation in Spain to characterize quality performance across successive stages of participation, assess sustainability over time, compare performance with contemporaneous QOPI benchmarks, identify persistent certification gaps, and examine quality performance across repeated certification and reassessment cycles. We conducted a longitudinal descriptive study of QOPI implementation in Spanish oncology practices between 2015 and 2025. Analyses included within-practice changes in QOPI quality measures among certified practices, comparing the last available pre-certification assessment with the first post-certification assessment, including disease-specific measures for breast, colorectal, and lung cancer; descriptive comparisons between first participation and post-certification assessments, benchmarking against the contemporaneous QOPI Aggregate, and findings from external certification and recertification surveys. Within-practice longitudinal analyses among certified practices showed higher post-certification performance in several patient-centered measures, including emotional well-being assessment (75.56% to 85.20%), infertility risk discussion (70.33% to 78.67%), appropriate pain management (83.57% to 89.15%), and pain assessment (83.56% to 89.50%). Certified practices maintained broadly high performance over time, although lower post-certification performance was observed in some chemotherapy and other documentation measures. Benchmarking showed a shift: pain assessment, emotional well-being assessment, appropriate pain management, and infertility counseling moved from below to above the contemporaneous QOPI Aggregate after certification. External surveys identified recurrent opportunities for improvement in treatment verification and patient information and education. A decade of QOPI implementation in Spain was associated with sustained high-quality performance, higher scores in selected patient-centered measures after certification, and the identification of persistent opportunities for improvement. Repeated measurement, benchmarking, certification, and reassessment may support organizational change and continuous quality improvement.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The incidence of early-onset colon cancer is increasing, and younger patients are often treated more intensively on the assumption of worse prognosis. To determine whether early-onset presentation is independently associated with prognosis, and to compare adjuvant chemotherapy use and effect between age groups. Retrospective cohort study with 1:3 propensity score matching and exact matching on stage. A single tertiary referral center. Patients who underwent curative resection for stage I to III colon cancer between 2012 and 2020. Early onset was defined as diagnosis before age 50. Curative resection with or without adjuvant chemotherapy. Recurrence-free survival was the primary outcome; overall survival and adjuvant chemotherapy use and effect were secondary. Of 5,032 patients, 749 (14.9%) had early-onset disease; 656 were matched to 1,968 late-onset patients. Five-year recurrence-free survival did not differ between the groups (88.0 vs 86.1%; p = 0.09), and early onset was not independently associated with recurrence or death after adjustment for tumor factors and adjuvant chemotherapy, both in the matched (adjusted hazard ratio 0.85; 95% confidence interval 0.66-1.10) and entire cohort (0.79; 0.62-1.00). Among early-onset patients, recurrence-free survival was independently associated with T4 classification, nodal category, and poor differentiation. Nonetheless, early-onset patients received adjuvant chemotherapy more often (60.2 vs 53.5%; p = 0.003), including in low-risk Stage II disease (37.7 vs 14.3%; p < 0.001). Retrospective single-center design with potential residual confounding; few early-onset patients did not receive chemotherapy. Early-onset presentation was not significantly associated with recurrence-free survival after multivariable adjustment in the matched cohort. Early-onset patients nonetheless received adjuvant chemotherapy more frequently and more intensively, including in low-risk Stage II disease. The observational design and the small number of untreated early-onset patients limit conclusions regarding age-specific chemotherapy benefit. See Video Abstract.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Condylomas are usually benign lesions associated with human papillomavirus (HPV) infection, but extensive disease can cause substantial morbidity. Immunosuppression can contribute to disease progression. A man presented with a two-year history of extensive condylomas involving the anal and perianal regions, penis, groin, suprapubic region, tongue and neck. Medical evaluation had been delayed due to health anxiety. Surgical treatment comprised excision of all lesions, split-thickness skin grafting, circumcision and a diverting colostomy. Histopathological examination revealed high-grade dysplasia, carcinoma in situ and squamous cell carcinoma in penile and anal lesions. HPV genotyping showed the highest viral titres for HPV types 82 and 6. Most countries offer HPV vaccines that provide protection against oncogenic HPV types as well as those associated with condylomas. In Norway, the HPV vaccine primarily targets the most common oncogenic HPV types. This case illustrates the potential severity of condylomas and the stigma and health burden associated with the condition. It also highlights possible limitations of current HPV vaccination practice in Norway.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colitis-associated colorectal cancer (CAC) develops in the setting of long-standing intestinal inflammation and remains a major complication of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Although effective control of inflammation may reduce cancer risk, approaches that specifically prevent the progression from chronic colitis to neoplasia remain limited. Disruption of the gut microbiota-metabolism-immunity axis is increasingly implicated in this process, as microbial dysbiosis and altered metabolite production can compromise epithelial barrier integrity, sustain inflammatory signaling, and disturb mucosal immune homeostasis. This review examines how active components derived from traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), particularly flavonoids, alkaloids, saponins, and polysaccharides, influence this interconnected network in CAC-related models. Rather than treating these constituents as a single group, we compare the mechanistic patterns and evidence base associated with each class. Flavonoids and alkaloids have been studied mainly in relation to inflammatory signaling and epithelial barrier protection, whereas saponins are more often linked to regulation of the immune microenvironment. Polysaccharides have been studied most frequently in relation to microbiota remodeling, short-chain fatty acid production, and mucosal immune balance. These distinctions are not absolute, and substantial overlap exists across component classes. Moreover, most evidence is derived from animal or cell-based studies, with marked variation in experimental models, compound characterizations, dosing, and outcome assessments. The microbiota-metabolism-immunity axis provides a coherent framework for interpreting the multi-level actions of TCM-derived components, but their causal mechanisms and clinical relevance to human CAC require further validation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death that has emerged as a potential vulnerability in cancer cells under therapeutic stress. However, the mechanisms by which colorectal cancer cells modulate ferroptosis susceptibility remain incompletely understood. In this study, we investigated the role of CWH43, a glycosylphosphatidylinositol-anchor biogenesis-related protein whose role in chemotherapy response has been unclear, in regulating redox balance and ferroptosis-associated vulnerability in colorectal cancer. Integrative analyses of clinical datasets, transcriptomic profiling, and functional experiments were performed using gain- and loss-of-function approaches in CRC cell models. We found that elevated CWH43 expression was associated with adverse clinical outcomes and reduced responsiveness to chemotherapy. Functionally, CWH43 attenuated ferroptosis-associated vulnerability by reducing intracellular reactive oxygen species and lipid peroxidation. Mechanistically, CWH43 promoted redox-adaptive programs involving activation of NRF2-dependent antioxidant signaling, upregulation of the cystine transporter SLC7A11, increased intracellular glutathione availability, and suppression of lipid peroxidation. Genetic or pharmacological disruption of SLC7A11 restored ferroptosis susceptibility and sensitized CWH43-overexpressing colorectal cancer cells to therapeutic stress, whereas ferrostatin-1 partially restored cell viability following erastin-containing treatments. Collectively, these findings identify CWH43 as a regulator of redox adaptation that modulates ferroptosis-associated vulnerability in colorectal cancer, providing insights into stress-adaptive survival mechanisms and chemotherapy resistance in cancer cells.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major global health burden, while conventional systemic therapies are limited by toxicity, drug resistance, suboptimal tumour exposure, and pharmacokinetic constraints. Recent advances in nanotechnology have produced diverse nanosystems including liposomes, dendrimers, polymeric nanoparticles, metallic nanoparticles, mesoporous silica systems, and other hybrid platforms that can improve drug solubility, stability, biodistribution, controlled release, and tumour-directed delivery. Plant-derived small molecules provide an additional source of structurally diverse anticancer candidates, but their clinical development is often constrained by poor aqueous solubility, rapid metabolism, limited bioavailability, and non-specific toxicity. This review critically examines recent progress in nanoscale delivery systems for CRC and evaluates their potential for delivering plant-derived and other bioactive small molecules. Particular emphasis is placed on passive and active targeting, physicochemical determinants of delivery, platform-specific advantages and limitations, preclinical evidence, and the barriers to clinical translation. The review also highlights the distinction between plant-derived and fungal-derived natural products and identifies opportunities for integrating natural products with responsive and ligand-functionalized nanocarriers.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Advances in gastrointestinal (GI) cancer care have produced a growing population of long-term survivors at risk of second primary malignancies (SPMs). SPM definitions vary across studies, and SPMs remain underrepresented in cancer forecasting and prediction tools for GI cancer survivors. We conducted a narrative review across major GI cancer subtypes, summarizing site-specific SPM risk, key etiological pathways, and available prediction tools. Approximately one in ten colorectal cancer (CRC) survivors develops an SPM at ten years (pooled SIR ~1.15), a figure specific to CRC that does not generalize to other GI sites. Gastric cancer survivors carry excess risk of thyroid (O/E 2.00), esophageal, small intestinal, and pancreatic (O/E 1.60) malignancy, amplified by radiotherapy. Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma survivors show markedly elevated risk of upper aerodigestive tract tumors, consistent with field cancerization. Lynch syndrome (~16% second CRC risk at 10 years) and familial adenomatous polyposis (near-100% lifetime CRC risk without colectomy) confer some of the highest lifetime risks of metachronous GI malignancy reported to date. Most forecasting frameworks treat cancer incidence as a single event and do not adequately capture survivor-specific transitions, competing mortality, or germline susceptibility. GI cancer survivors form a distinct group whose risk is often overlooked. Harmonizing SPM definitions, extending multistate and competing-risk modeling, and integrating hereditary-risk stratification are near-term priorities for individualized surveillance.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Nasopharyngeal angiofibroma (NA) is generally benign, but recurrent disease and rare malignant transformation remain clinically relevant beyond adolescence. We examined adult clinical presentations, records of malignant transformation, and age-related differences in stage distribution. We retrospectively reviewed 289 surgically treated patients from January 2006 through June 2026. Radkowski stage distributions were compared between patients aged > 30 and ≤30 years using exact tests. Detailed clinical records were reviewed for 16 adults, and whole-genome sequencing (WGS) annotation summaries were examined for one tumor-blood pair. Twenty-five patients (8.7%) were older than 30 years; stage was available for 287 patients. In the detailed adult subgroup, a prior pathology-slide record described focal malignant transformation with a Ki-67 index of approximately 50% in one recurrent tumor. Two other patients had database transformation entries without accompanying pathological documentation. Four recurrences and three deaths were recorded, all in stage IIIB disease. Three men had colorectal or rectal cancer histories. Low-, intermediate-, and advanced-stage tumors accounted for 36.0%, 36.0%, and 28.0% of adult cases, compared with 17.6%, 57.3%, and 25.2% of younger cases ( Adult NA included recurrent stage IIIB disease and a documented record of focal malignant transformation. Stage distributions differed between age groups. These clinical observations support pathological reassessment of recurrent tumors. The single-case genomic findings remain descriptive annotations.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Computed tomography (CT) informs preoperative staging in colon cancer, yet its diagnostic accuracy for lymph node involvement relative to pathological staging remains uncertain. We examined nodal concordance and multicentre variation in Poland. This retrospective diagnostic accuracy study included adults who underwent upfront resection for nonmetastatic colon cancer at five centres between January 2022 and August 2025. All underwent preoperative CT; recorded cN categories were dichotomised as cN0 versus cN+ (any positive cN category), and pathological pN was the reference. We estimated accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, and kappa with 95% confidence intervals. A centre-adjusted exploratory analysis examined the association between cT3-4 and occult pN+ among cN0 patients. Of 662 otherwise eligible patients, 590 had evaluable cN and pN. CT and pathology agreed in 386 (65.4%; 95% CI, 61.5-69.2; κ = 0.276; 95% CI, 0.199-0.353). Occult pN+ occurred in 73 of 335 cN0 patients (21.8%; 95% CI, 17.7-26.5); 131 of 255 cN+ patients were pN0 (51.4%; 95% CI, 45.3-57.4). Sensitivity was 62.9% and specificity 66.7%. Centre-level cN/pN completeness ranged from 73.5% to 100%. cT3-4 was associated with occult pN+ after centre adjustment (OR, 3.10; 95% CI, 1.71-5.62). Sensitivity analyses were materially consistent. Routine CT nodal classification showed limited concordance with pathology. The cT3-4 association is exploratory and does not establish a prediction or treatment selection rule; cN alone should not determine treatment.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Patients with primary sclerosing cholangitis-associated ulcerative colitis (PSC-UC) have an elevated risk of colorectal cancer compared with ulcerative colitis (UC), but the molecular mechanisms linking chronic inflammation to epithelial cell fate remain unclear. The present study investigated disease- and region-specific molecular patterns involving miRNAs and associated PI3K/AKT, STAT3, and NF-κB signalling pathways. miR-21, miR-181a, miR-181b, and key pathway components were analysed in paired ascending and sigmoid colon biopsies from patients with PSC, PSC-UC, UC, and controls. Functional effects were examined in HT-29 and NCM460D cells, and circulating miRNAs, including miR-155, were assessed. UC was characterised by marked miR-181a upregulation and PI3K/AKT activation, whereas PSC-UC showed reduced PDCD4, divergent p65 regulation, and altered miR-181a/miR-181b coordination. In NCM460D cells, miR-181a and miR-181b reduced viability, promoted apoptosis, impaired cell-cycle progression, and decreased PDCD4, p-AKT, and p-STAT3; miR-181b additionally reduced CYLD. Serum miR-155 was elevated in PSC-UC compared with UC and showed the strongest individual discriminatory capacity. Random forest analysis and an exploratory multivariable serum miRNA profile showed discriminatory potential. These findings support disease- and region-specific molecular patterns involving miRNAs and associated signalling pathways linked to epithelial cell-fate responses in PSC-UC and highlight molecular differences between PSC-UC and conventional UC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Pelvic autonomic nerve injury is a major cause of postoperative bowel dysfunction, yet effective strategies for restoring damaged pelvic ganglia remain lacking. Here, we demonstrate that extracellular vesicles derived from human pluripotent stem cell-derived sacral neural crest cells (Sacral NC-EVs) promote pelvic neuroregeneration by suppressing oxidative stress-induced pyroptosis. In a rat model of major pelvic ganglion (MPG) injury, local administration of Sacral NC-EVs improved gastrointestinal motility and partially restored rectal neural innervation and epithelial barrier integrity. Mechanistic analyses showed that MPG injury increased oxidative stress and activated the NLRP3-caspase-1-GSDMD pyroptosis pathway, whereas Sacral NC-EVs attenuated both responses. Comparisons across EV sources showed that Sacral NC-EVs more effectively suppressed oxidative stress and pyroptosis and increased PGP9.5-positive and ChAT-positive neuronal areas than mesenchymal stem cell-derived EVs and vagal neural crest-derived EVs. Proteomic and functional analyses implicated EV-associated annexin A1 (ANXA1) as one contributor to the antioxidant and anti-pyroptotic effects of Sacral NC-EVs through FPR2 signaling. Collectively, our findings support Sacral NC-EVs as a promising cell-free strategy for pelvic neural repair by targeting the oxidative stress-pyroptosis axis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Prior abdominal surgery (PAS) is common in patients undergoing robotic colorectal cancer (CRC) resection. Most studies have evaluated PAS as a binary exposure, leaving unclear which specific PAS characteristics are associated with technically relevant adhesions, adhesiolysis, and operative efficiency in robotic surgery. This retrospective cohort study included 746 consecutive patients who underwent robotic CRC resection at a single institution between January 2018 and December 2025; 200 patients (26.8%) had a history of PAS. Among patients with PAS, associations between detailed PAS characteristics and intraoperative adhesion phenotype or adhesiolysis were assessed using multivariable regression analyses. Short-term outcomes between PAS and non-PAS patients were compared after 1:1 propensity score matching using age, sex, body mass index, American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status, preoperative treatment, primary tumor site, and clinical T stage. In the PAS cohort, adhesions were observed in 46.0 and 36.0% required adhesiolysis. Cancer-related PAS (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 3.78, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.36-11.4; p = 0.01) and prior open surgery (aOR 6.06, 95% CI 2.47-16.9; p < 0.01) independently predicted abdominal wall adhesions. Among adhesion-positive PAS patients, middle (aOR 15.2, 95% CI 1.34-172.9; p = 0.02) and lower abdominal PAS (aOR 12.2, 95% CI 3.05-48.9; p < 0.01) independently predicted adhesiolysis. After matching, operative time, console time, blood loss, conversion, and severe complications were comparable between groups. Mean differences were small for operative time (16.2 min, 95% CI -8.5 to 40.9), console time (10.6 min, 95% CI -7.6 to 28.8), and blood loss (12.9 mL, 95% CI -7.4 to 33.2). Specific PAS characteristics, rather than PAS presence alone, were associated with technically relevant adhesions and adhesiolysis in robotic CRC resection. Despite increased technical burden, short-term outcomes remained comparable, supporting a more individualized interpretation of prior surgical history in robotic colorectal surgery.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Peristomal bulging and external stoma prolapse are the most common long-term complications following stoma formation. This systematic review aims to describe available evidence on the incidence of parastomal hernia, subcutaneous prolapse and external stomal prolapse following open versus minimally invasive intestinal resections with definitive stoma formation. In this systematic review and meta-analysis, a literature search was performed to include studies published in the last 15 years on intestinal resections with a definitive ileostomy or colostomy formation and a follow-up of more than 12 months, reporting on PSH and/or subcutaneous prolapse and/or external stoma prolapse after laparoscopic or robotic, and open surgery. The incidence of PSH after open versus minimally invasive surgery was the primary outcome, and secondary outcomes included other stoma-related complications such as subcutaneous stoma prolapse and external stoma prolapse, and outcomes. In total six studies (one randomised controlled trial and five observational studies) on 1480 patients with a definitive stoma were included (731 open, 749 laparoscopic). All studies reported PSH as an outcome, no study reported the incidence of subcutaneous prolapse and one study reported on external stoma prolapse. There was consistent trend toward higher PSH rates following laparoscopic resections, both in clinically (RR 1.89 (95% CI 1.39-2.58)) and radiologically (RR 1.70 (95% CI 0.89-3.28)) assessed hernias. Minimally invasive intestinal resection may be associated with a higher incidence of PSH than open surgery, but the certainty of the evidence is very low. Subcutaneous prolapse is seldom recognised as a distinct form of stoma herniation. Clear differentiation is essential, as these conditions differ in their underlying mechanisms and management. PROSPERO CRD420251026395.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Whether technical difficulty influences outcomes after transanal total mesorectal excision (TaTME) for middle and low rectal cancer remains unclear. This study evaluated the association between technical difficulty and patient outcomes. This multicenter retrospective cohort study included 210 consecutive patients with middle and low rectal cancer who underwent TaTME at three centers in China. A five-item technical difficulty score was constructed using male sex, body mass index ≥ 25 kg/m Overall, 130 patients were classified into the low technical difficulty group and 80 into the high technical difficulty group. The high technical difficulty group had a longer operative time (249.0 ± 60.0 vs. 220.3 ± 50.1 min, P < 0.001), but major short-term outcomes did not differ significantly. The 3-year DFS and OS rates were 80.2% and 89.0%, respectively. Forty postoperative recurrences were recorded, mainly distant metastases, with most occurring within 2 years. Overall recurrence (17.7% vs. 21.2%, P = 0.588) and local recurrence (3.8% vs. 2.5%, P = 0.711) were comparable between groups. High technical difficulty was not independently associated with DFS (HR 1.06, 95% CI 0.57-2.00, P = 0.849) or OS (HR 1.21, 95% CI 0.52-2.81, P = 0.664). Technical difficulty in TaTME was mainly reflected by prolonged operative time and was not significantly associated with increased local recurrence or reduced 3-year DFS/OS. Early surveillance for systemic recurrence remains important.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Bacteria are increasingly recognized as contributors to cancer, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear for most species. Here, we find that Gemella morbillorum (Gm) is enriched in feces and tumor tissues from patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) and reveal a multi-step host-pathogen mechanism that promotes colorectal tumorigenesis. In mouse models of CRC, Gm suppresses IL-22 production by type 3 innate lymphoid cells (ILC3s), impairing intestinal barrier function and facilitating bacterial translocation to early neoplastic lesions. At the tumor site, Gm utilizes an ANXA2-dependent, clathrin-mediated pathway to invade CRC cells. Gm induces profound lipid remodeling, characterized by the accumulation of oxidation-prone fatty acids and enhanced lipid peroxidation, which contributes to invasion-dependent DNA damage. Inhibition of lipid peroxidation attenuates Gm-induced DNA damage, functionally linking lipid oxidative stress to genotoxicity. Together, these findings identify Gm as a candidate onco-pathogen in CRC that uses multiple mechanisms to disarm the intestinal barrier and trigger genotoxicity.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cetuximab (CET), a monoclonal antibody targeting the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), serves as a cornerstone therapeutic option for advanced colorectal cancer (CRC). However, patients with KRAS-mutant CRC present inherent resistance to CET, which directly compromises its clinical efficacy and therapeutic benefits. Zuojin Wan (ZJW), a classic traditional Chinese medicine formula consisting of Coptis chinensis Franch. and Evodia rutaecarpa (Juss.) Benth., has been documented to exert potent antitumor activity; nevertheless, its potential role in reversing CET resistance in KRAS-mutated CRC and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly defined. This study aimed to investigate the efficacy of ZJW in overcoming CET resistance in KRAS-mutated CRC and further characterize its key molecular targets and regulatory mechanisms. In vitro experiments were conducted using two KRAS-mutated CRC cell lines, HCT116 and SW620. The synergistic antiproliferative effect of ZJW combined with CET was assessed via CCK-8 assay and colony formation assay. Ferroptosis induction mediated by the combination treatment was verified by measuring lipid peroxidation, glutathione (GSH) depletion, ferrous ion (Fe2+) accumulation, and observing characteristic mitochondrial morphological alterations using transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels were detected to evaluate intracellular oxidative stress. Transcriptome sequencing, Western blot analysis and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) were performed to explore the underlying molecular mechanisms, while plasmid transfection and quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) were carried out for functional validation. A nude mouse subcutaneous xenograft model was established to evaluate the antitumor efficacy of the combined treatment in vivo, and immunohistochemical (IHC) staining was performed to detect the expression of relevant proteins. The primary bioactive components of ZJW were identified by mass spectrometry, and network pharmacology analysis was performed to predict the potential interactions between these active components and CRC-related signaling pathways. ZJW synergistically augmented the CET-mediated suppression of KRAS-mutated CRC cell proliferation and triggered significant ferroptosis, as evidenced by elevated lipid peroxidation, reduced GSH levels, increased Fe2+ accumulation, shrunken mitochondria with condensed cristae, and markedly enhanced intracellular oxidative stress. Combination treatment with ZJW and CET significantly downregulated the expression of core proteins involved in the parallel NRF2-GCH1/CoQ and DHODH/CoQ antioxidant axes, thereby disrupting intracellular redox homeostasis. Silencing of NRF2 or DHODH facilitated ferroptosis and sensitized CRC cells to CET, whereas overexpression of these two molecules abolished the synergistic antitumor effect of ZJW plus CET. In the nude mouse xenograft model, the combined regimen notably suppressed tumor growth and decreased tumor weight, and modulated the expression of ferroptosis-associated markers (NRF2, DHODH) and the lipid peroxidation indicator 4-HNE in tumor tissues. Mass spectrometry identified the major bioactive constituents of ZJW, and network pharmacology analysis predicted their potential involvement in multiple CRC-related pathways, including antioxidant defense and ferroptosis regulation. ZJW reverses CET resistance in KRAS-mutated CRC by inhibiting the parallel NRF2-GCH1/CoQ and DHODH/CoQ antioxidant axes to induce ferroptosis. This study provides a solid scientific basis for the clinical translation of ZJW as an adjuvant therapeutic strategy to boost the efficacy of CET in CRC treatment.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Chronic diarrhea (CD) severely affects patients' quality of life and is linked to ulcerative colitis, inflammatory bowel disease, and colorectal cancer. Gut microbiota dysbiosis plays a crucial role in intestinal health, with Lactobacillus reuteri emerging as a key regulator. However, its role in chronic diarrhea remains unclear. In this study, we observed macaques with spontaneous diarrhea and investigated microbial and metabolic changes. We also developed a chronic diarrhea mouse model using dextran sulfate sodium. CD group of both models revealed a significant reduction of L. reuteri. L. reuteri transplantation alleviates intestinal injury in CD by secreting D-lactate and modulates macrophage polarization. L. reuteri-derived D-lactate binds to IARS2 in intestinal epithelial macrophages, reducing mitochondrial IARS2 activation and suppressing cGAS-STING pathway activation. This preserves mitochondrial function while decreasing M1 macrophage polarization. Our research revealed the significance of microbiota dysbiosis in CD with both non-human primate and murine model, and highlighted the critical role of L. reuteri, which is conducted with D-lactate-mediated modulation of macrophage function and offered new insights into probiotic therapy for CD.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Tumor-associated myeloid alterations extend beyond the local microenvironment and involve systemic changes in myeloid development and circulating monocytes. However, how these systemic changes are coordinated with macrophage reprogramming during colorectal tumorigenesis remains unclear. Here, we identified coordinated HIF-1α-associated changes across the monocyte-macrophage compartment in advanced adenoma and early colorectal cancer. Circulating HIF-1α⁺ monocytes were prominently altered in advanced adenoma, whereas colorectal tissues accumulated CXCL8⁺HIF-1α⁺ macrophages with enhanced glycolytic programs. In tumor-bearing mice, common monocyte progenitors and mature monocytes expanded together with HIF-1α⁺ myeloid cells, and macrophages acquired heightened HIF-1α responsiveness to tumor-derived signals. Functional perturbation further demonstrated that macrophage HIF-1α promoted tumor-cell survival, proliferation, and invasion. These findings define the systemic monocytic remodeling and HIF-1α-associated protumor macrophage activity as coordinated features of the myeloid response during colorectal tumorigenesis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) represents a major malignancy of the gastrointestinal tract with substantial global morbidity and mortality. Mounting evidence underscores the pivotal role of chronic psychological stress in the pathogenesis of gastrointestinal cancers. Psychological stress-related genes have been implicated in modulating tumor progression and represent promising prognostic biomarkers. Nevertheless, their precise prognostic significance in CRC remains incompletely characterized. We initially identified prognostic genes through univariate Cox regression analysis of The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) dataset. An optimal prognostic signature was subsequently constructed using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression and multivariate Cox analysis. Predictive accuracy was assessed via Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, and calibration curves. Furthermore, immune microenvironment characterization and chemotherapeutic response profiling were performed across risk-stratified subgroups to elucidate underlying biological mechanisms. Of 374 psychological stress-related genes examined, 62 demonstrated significant associations with overall survival (OS). The resulting 11-gene signature achieved area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.711, 0.768, and 0.800 for 1-, 3-, and 5-year OS prediction in the TCGA training cohort, respectively. External validation in three GEO cohorts showed attenuated but reproducible prognostic stratification, with AUCs ranging from approximately 0.56 to 0.63. High-risk patients exhibited significantly reduced survival probability. Computational analyses suggested a higher estimated M2 macrophage fraction and reduced predicted sensitivity to oxaliplatin. We developed and externally evaluated an 11-gene transcriptomic signature related to stress-associated tumor biology in CRC. The signature stratified survival in retrospective cohorts, although external discrimination was moderate. This signature should be regarded as an exploratory research tool rather than a clinically validated assay. Computational analyses generated hypotheses regarding immune contexture and oxaliplatin sensitivity, and UBP1 emerged as a candidate tumor-suppressive regulator. Prospective multicenter validation and mechanistic studies are required before clinical application.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
In this work, YK-2168 was selected as the lead compound for the development of a series of highly selective CDK9 inhibitors due to its unique 1H-pyrrolo[2,3-b]pyridine scaffold, which acts as an optimal backbone for targeting the kinase hinge region. The optimized compound B3 exhibited potent inhibitory activities at both enzymatic and cellular levels with satisfactory selectivity. Mechanistic studies revealed that compound B3 induces apoptosis in the HCT116 cells by suppressing the phosphorylation of RNA polymerase II at Ser2 site, which further results in the downregulates the expression of apoptosis-related gene and protein (Mcl-1) and triggers the cleavage of caspase 3 and PARP. Pharmacokinetic studies and in vivo experiments demonstrated that intravenous injection of compound B3 could achieve prominent therapeutic efficacy with a high safety profile. In general, these findings indicate that compound B3 is a promising candidate for CRC treatment.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Gastrodin is a natural compound with anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antitumor activities; however, its therapeutic role and molecular mechanisms in colorectal cancer (CRC) remain unclear. In this study, we explored the anti-CRC mechanisms of gastrodin through integrated bioinformatics and experimental validation. The potential targets of gastrodin were obtained from public databases. Transcriptomic data of CRC were retrieved from TCGA and GEO datasets, and the differentially expressed genes were screened. The CRC-related genes were subjected to gene-set variation analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and the core genes were identified by the LASSO regression, support vector machine, and random forest algorithms, followed by SHAP analysis. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), immune infiltration analysis, consensus clustering, molecular docking, and in vitro experiments were further performed. A total of 628 potential gastrodin targets and 15 overlapping CRC-related genes were identified. Five core hub genes, including NFE2L3, UBE2S, CA9, CCNB1, and CFD, were screened, among which NFE2L3 showed the highest SHAP importance score. The scRNA-seq data indicated cell-type-specific expression patterns of these genes in CRC tissues. Immune infiltration analysis further suggested that gastrodin may regulate the CRC immune microenvironment by regulating the activated B cells, activated CD4⁺ T cells, and other immune cells. Molecular docking revealed favorable binding affinity between gastrodin and the five core proteins. Moreover, NFE2L3 was highly expressed in CRC tissues and cell lines, and its knockdown significantly inhibited the proliferation, migration, and invasion of the tumor cells. Gastrodin may suppress CRC progression by targeting key genes, particularly NFE2L3, and modulating the tumor immune microenvironment. Furthermore, our study has identified the potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets for CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Automated colorectal segmentation provides a quantitative basis for the preoperative assessment of acute malignant colorectal obstruction. However, existing public datasets predominantly focus on conventional anatomical structures, lacking representation of colorectal cancer-related anatomical phenotypes. This study aims to establish a dedicated dataset for colorectal segmentation in acute malignant colorectal obstruction and provide a benchmark for evaluating segmentation models. A total of 86 eligible cases were retrospectively included to construct AMCOD, with the colorectum annotated into proximal, obstructed, and distal segments. Experiments were conducted to establish a segmentation benchmark on AMCOD, assess the contribution of the three-region supervision strategy through ablation analysis, and evaluate cross-dataset transferability with two public colorectal datasets. Benchmark experiments revealed differences across the three annotated colorectal regions, with the obstructed segment consistently showing the lowest segmentation performance across the evaluated models. Ablation analysis showed that three-region supervision improved obstructed-segment segmentation compared with obstruction-only supervision. Cross-dataset evaluation further showed that the AMCOD-trained model retained colorectal segmentation capability on both evaluated external datasets. This work provides a dataset resource for acute malignant colorectal obstruction segmentation and establishes a benchmark for evaluating segmentation methods under obstruction-related anatomical conditions. To facilitate further research and community development, the proposed dataset is made publicly available at https://github.com/FZU312lab/AMCOD.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
IntroductionReal-time artificial intelligence (AI) decision-support systems are increasingly proposed for use in endoscopic and minimally invasive surgery although how best to present such information intraoperatively is unclear. This study explored surgeon perspectives regarding the user-interface, interpretation and workflow integration of a prototype AI system (CLASSICA-OR) for real-time endoscopic cancer characterization during surgery.MethodsSurgeons specialising in minimally invasive gastrointestinal surgery were asked for their first impressions in their evaluation of the CLASSICA-OR system within a high-fidelity surgical simulation environment. For this, participants viewed prerecorded colonoscopic imagery of significant rectal neoplasia while the AI analysis was applied in real-time to the video. Commentary and responses to semi-structured interview were recorded audiovisually for transcription and analysis using qualitative thematic analysis supported by NVivo (Lumivero).ResultsEighteen surgeons participated, generating rich qualitative data. Four major themes emerged: (1) AI was viewed as a valuable but evolving decision-support tool; (2) institutional culture, governance and commercial realities were recognised as important determinants of adoption; (3) real-time perfusion-based lesion characterisation (foundational to CLASSICA-OR) was considered promising but with specific challenges; and (4) clarity, usability, transparency and workflow compatibility are surgeon priorities in decision-support displays. Participants emphasised minimised cognitive load, preserved surgeon autonomy, clear communication of uncertainty and seamless workflow integration. Preferences differed between simplified binary outputs and more detailed numerical displays supporting the need for adaptable interfaces.ConclusionsSurgeons perceive real-time intraoperative AI decision support as promising but requiring thoughtful user-centred design. They articulate practical development and implementation insights for intraoperative AI systems.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Ultra-processed foods (UPF) account for >50% of energy intake by US adults. UPF intake can include dietary components linked to lower colorectal cancer (CRC) risk, such as whole grain and dairy products, and others linked to higher CRC risk, such as processed meats, potentially explaining the heterogeneity of evidence for an association between UPF and CRC risk. Our goal was to estimate the associations of UPF and established CRC-related dietary factors, by UPF and non-UPF source, with CRC incidence in a large cohort study. US adults, aged 50-71, who enrolled in the NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study in 1995-96, self-reported dietary intake using a food frequency questionnaire (FFQ). Median UPF intake was 293 g/1000 kcal/day or 43% of daily energy intake. We assigned disaggregated FFQ items to Nova classification and categorized UPF intake (g/1000 kcal/day) into sex-specific quintiles. Participants who were cancer-free at baseline (N = 461,682) were followed for cancer incidence through 2018, and 10,075 colorectal adenocarcinoma cases were diagnosed. We used multivariable-adjusted Cox proportional hazards regression models, adjusted for demographic, lifestyle, and health-related factors, including age, sex, race/ethnicity, education, physical activity, smoking, and alcohol drinking, to estimate associations for UPF and related dietary components with CRC incidence. UPF intake was not associated with CRC incidence (hazard ratio 5th versus 1st quintile 0.97; 95% confidence interval [0.91-1.03]; ptrend = 0.55). Whole grain, fiber, dairy, and calcium intakes from UPF sources were inversely but meat intake from UPF sources was positively associated with CRC incidence. The main limitations of the study relate to its observational design and include potential residual confounding and exposure misclassification owing to systematic or random error in self-reported dietary data. Total UPF intake was not associated with incident CRC in this cohort of older, US adults. This may be explained, in part, by opposing associations of some UPF with CRC risk. Our findings support current dietary guidance to consume whole grains, fiber, dairy, and calcium and avoid processed meat for CRC prevention.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Data on quality of life (QOL) after total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) are important for counseling patients on the benefits of watch-and-wait (WW) vs total mesorectal excision (TME) for rectal cancer. A thorough understanding of both options and their long-term impact on bowel, urinary, sexual function, and other QOL domains remains limited. To examine the association of organ preservation with QOL and functional outcomes among patients with rectal cancer treated in 2 phase 2 clinical trials. This unplanned, post hoc, cohort study used data from the CAO/ARO/AIO-12 and CAO/ARO/AIO-16 trials, recruiting participants from June 15, 2015, through October 7, 2020, from 19 centers in Germany. Included patients had cT3 to cT4 or node-positive rectal adenocarcinoma. Total neoadjuvant treatment included chemoradiation therapy combined with induction or consolidation chemotherapy. The statistical analysis was performed from March 6 to December 23, 2025. The association of WW with functional outcomes and QOL was assessed using prospectively recorded EORTC QLQ-C30, EORTC QLQ-CR29, and Wexner score questionnaires. Differences in QOL scores were estimated using adjusted longitudinal and cross-sectional analyses with a predefined clinically meaningful difference of at least 5 points. Baseline questionnaires were available from 346 of 385 eligible patients (89.9%; median [range] age, 60 [19-80] years; 257 male [67%]), while available QOL questionnaires decreased over time to 185 (48.1%) at 5 years. Using the longitudinal analytic approach, statistically significant and clinically meaningful differences in favor of WW were noted for fecal incontinence (-21.2 [95% CI, -30.0 to -12.3]; P < .001); stool frequency (-19.8 [95% CI, -27.6 to -11.9]; P < .001); embarrassment (-17.0 [95% CI, -27.4 to -6.6]; P = .002); flatulence (-15.2 [95% CI, -24.4 to -6.0]; P < .001), buttock pain (-11.9 [95% CI, -20.8 to -3.0]; P = .01); social (9.7 [95% CI, 1.1-18.3]; P = .03), physical (10.2 [95% CI, 4.1-16.3]; P = .002), and role (13.9 [95% CI, 4.9-22.9]; P = .003) functioning; and global health status (9.2 [95% CI, 3.2-15.2]; P = .004). These clinically meaningful differences were detectable in both the intended organ preservation and disease-free groups. Patients with sustained clinical complete response at 3 years (n = 29) vs those with pathologic complete response or matched baseline characteristics favored WW for fecal incontinence (-24.0 and -11.6, respectively), stool frequency (-34.6 and -19.1), sore skin (-18.0 and -18.1), buttock pain (-14.7 and -17.6), embarrassment (-41.1 and -20.5), role functioning (19.1 and 10.9), and social functioning (20.0 and 8.4). In the absence of prospective randomized trials, this study provides evidence suggesting long-term clinically meaningful benefits for organ preservation regarding QOL, especially for most gastrointestinal subscales, social functioning, and global health status, over a 5-year period among patients with rectal cancer. As treatment options for patients with rectal cancer now routinely include WW in cases of clinical complete response after TNT, patient-reported QOL measures have become paramount for informed shared decision-making. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifiers: NCT02363374 and NCT03561142.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Metastasis-associated in colon cancer 1 (MACC1) is an established regulator of colorectal cancer (CRC) progression and metastatic competence, but its proposed role in the tumour microenvironment is less certain. We performed a critical claim-level audit of original studies, classifying evidence by cancer-type match, manipulated cellular compartment, direct MACC1 perturbation, functional recipient cell endpoint, and immune context. The audit identifies convergent CRC evidence for tumour cell-intrinsic functions and inflammatory regulation of tumour cell MACC1. It also supports MACC1-dependent extracellular vesicle communication between CRC cells. By contrast, direct immune or stromal causality in CRC is not yet demonstrated: the available macrophage result is pharmacologically conditioned, functional immune and fibroblast mechanisms come from other cancers, and CRC immune associations are mainly computational. We define the conclusions permitted by each evidence class, specify clinical guardrails for prognostic and treatment-predictive claims, and propose two experiments that could establish or falsify cell-specific microenvironmental functions.
