ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor BHLHE40 (also known as BHLHB2, DEC1, STRA13) functions as a critical molecular rheostat in cancer biology, exhibiting context-dependent roles that contribute to tumor plasticity. This review synthesizes current knowledge of BHLHE40, with emphasis on its structural features, including DNA binding, dimerization, and regulatory domains, as well as its integration of key physiological signals, such as circadian rhythm regulation, hypoxic adaptation, cellular senescence, and immune modulation. Pancancer analyses indicate that BHLHE40 expression is dysregulated across multiple tumor types. Elevated expression is associated with poor prognosis in cancers such as glioblastoma, acute myeloid leukemia, and ovarian cancer, whereas it correlates with favorable outcomes in breast and kidney cancers. Notably, the functional role of BHLHE40 is highly tissue-dependent. It promotes tumor progression in hepatocellular carcinoma, gastric cancer, colorectal cancer, and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma by enhancing proliferation, invasion, migration, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), and therapeutic resistance. In contrast, BHLHE40 exhibits tumor-suppressive effects in prostate cancer by inducing cellular senescence, and in endometrial cancer by inhibiting EMT. The tumor microenvironment plays a pivotal role in modulating BHLHE40 activity, with factors such as hypoxia, cytokine signaling, and immune cell interactions shaping its oncogenic or tumor-suppressive functions. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Li-Fraumeni syndrome (LFS), caused by germline pathogenic variants in TP53, predisposes affected individuals to multiple early-onset malignancies. Although the risk of colorectal cancer (CRC) is increasingly recognized, evidence regarding colonoscopic surveillance remains limited. We present a series of seven genetically confirmed patients with LFS who underwent colonoscopic surveillance at our institution. All patients were women with a history of multiple primary malignancies. Adenomas were identified at the initial colonoscopy in two patients. Among the remaining five patients with negative baseline examinations, four subsequently had colorectal neoplastic lesions detected within 2-3 years. Overall, colorectal neoplasia was detected in five patients, including three advanced adenomas and one CRC diagnosed at 32 years of age. A serrated lesion was observed in one patient. The median age at first detection of colorectal neoplasia was 32.5 years. This case series demonstrates that colorectal neoplasia may be detected at a young age in patients with LFS, including within a relatively short interval after a negative colonoscopic examination. These findings underscore the importance of careful and regular colonoscopic surveillance in this high-risk population.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed microsatellite instability-high or mismatch repair-deficient metastatic colorectal cancer, but clinically relevant progression still occurs and treatment after progression remains undefined. We performed a clinically oriented narrative review, updated August 8, 2026, and separated direct prospective evidence, retrospective post-ICI evidence, extrapolation from general metastatic colorectal cancer trials, case-level evidence, and biological rationale. In the absence of prospective post-dual-ICI sequencing studies, we propose an evidence-informed conceptual framework. Apparent early progression should prompt confirmation of MSI/MMR status and exclusion of pseudoprogression before classification as early global progression, late systemic progression, or oligoprogression. BRAF V600E is common in MSI-H/dMMR metastatic colorectal cancer and is not an absolute predictor of ICI failure, but it is a major treatment-defining branch after progression. Repeat tissue biopsy or circulating tumor DNA profiling should be selective, used when findings can alter management and without delaying urgent therapy. ctDNA-based molecular residual disease is prognostic after curative-intent colorectal cancer resection, including metastasectomy, but is not validated to direct treatment of radiographically evident post-ICI progression. Oligoprogression warrants multidisciplinary consideration of local therapy, while ICI rechallenge remains investigational. Most recommendations are retrospective or extrapolated; transparent evidence boundaries and prospective post-dual-ICI studies are essential.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Chronic colitis is a major risk factor for colorectal cancer (CRC), particularly for colitis-associated colorectal cancer (CAC), where persistent inflammation drives the transition from mucosal injury to malignant transformation. Accumulating evidence indicates that gut microbiota dysbiosis, epithelial barrier disruption, microbial translocation, chronic immune activation, and aberrant inflammatory signaling collectively contribute to CAC initiation and progression. Sustained inflammation promotes oxidative stress, DNA damage, genetic/epigenetic alterations, and tumor microenvironment remodeling, ultimately facilitating tumor development and immune evasion. These processes form an interconnected pathogenic network linking microbial, inflammatory, genetic, immune, and stromal alterations. This review comprehensively summarizes the key drivers and molecular mechanisms of CAC, covering microbiota and barrier dysfunction, inflammatory signaling, oxidative stress and DNA damage, genetic and epigenetic alterations, and tumor microenvironment remodeling and immune dysregulation. We further review recent advances in diagnostic biomarkers, disease monitoring, chemoprevention, targeted therapies, and emerging interventions, including the potential utility of specific chemokine axes as biomarkers and therapeutic targets. Particular emphasis is placed on the translational challenges of linking mechanistic insights to diagnostic and therapeutic advances, including biomarker validation, stage-specific interventions, and patient stratification across disease progression. By integrating these interconnected mechanisms and therapeutic strategies, this review provides a comprehensive framework for understanding CAC pathogenesis and identifies opportunities for precision prevention, early detection, and multimodal treatment.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
3-Methyladenine (3-MA), an early autophagy inhibitor, blocks autophagosome formation mainly by inhibiting class III phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) vacuolar protein sorting 34, while its concurrent inhibition of class I PI3K can produce opposing effects on autophagic flux depending on nutrient status. This Review examines the context-dependent roles of 3-MA across cancer types. When autophagy serves a pro-survival function, 3-MA-mediated inhibition tends to attenuate this protective response, thereby potentiating the cytotoxicity of chemotherapeutics, targeted drugs, and natural compounds, and helping to overcome acquired resistance. However, in some settings-such as colorectal cancer without therapeutic pressure-autophagy suppression may instead promote epithelial-mesenchymal transition and metastasis. The pharmacokinetic shortcomings and off-target effects of 3-MA have motivated the design of nanocarriers for tumor-specific co-delivery, aiming to improve bioavailability and avoid paradoxical autophagy induction. Ultimately, the lasting contribution of 3-MA may be its utility as a mechanistic probe that uncovers key autophagy regulatory nodes, paving the way for next-generation selective modulators and biomarker-driven strategies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Women with Lynch syndrome are at increased risk of endometrial cancer. Gynecological surveillance is advised, but also prophylactic hysterectomy is an option. This study aimed to gain more insight in tumorigenesis in Lynch carriers to be able to personalize prophylactic hysterectomy timing. To this aim endometrial cancer surveillance in Lynch syndrome carriers was assessed using data from the Dutch Lynch syndrome database linked to the Dutch National Pathology Databank (PALGA). Eligible participants were Lynch syndrome carriers under surveillance, who underwent hysterectomy and had ≥ 1 endometrial biopsy within five years prior to surgery. Pathology reports, describing the histopathological features of the samples, were collected and, if available, samples were revised by a specialized pathologist. Additionally loss of expression of ARID1A, PTEN, PAX2, and mismatch repair (MMR) proteins was studied. Pathology reports from 32 Lynch syndrome carriers were analyzed: 16 had normal endometrium at hysterectomy, five had hyperplasia without atypia, six had endometrial intra-epithelial neoplasia (EIN), and five had endometrial cancer. Prior to hysterectomy, hyperplasia with or without atypia or endometrial cancer was reported in 3% of biopsies in the histopathological normal group, 26% in endometrial hyperplasia without atypia group, 26% in the EIN group, and 36% in the endometrial cancer group. Upon revision, combined neoplastic development of tissue and loss of protein expression were observed in 12% of the normal group, 36% of endometrial hyperplasia without atypia, 36% of EIN, and 50% of endometrial cancer group. So, increasing tissue disorganization and loss of protein expression appeared to correlate with progression to (pre)malignancy. However, no specific marker or consistent pattern emerged that could guide clinical decisions on prophylactic hysterectomy for individual patients. These findings highlight the complexity of endometrial cancer development in Lynch syndrome and underscore the need for further research to improve surveillance strategies and optimize timing of prophylactic surgery.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Comorbidity is usually summarised as a count or index, which treats different combinations of conditions equally. Whether distinct comorbidity patterns have different implications for management decisions in cancer is unclear. We applied latent class analysis (LCA) to identify comorbidity patterns and examined their associations with performance status and cancer treatment in individuals with breast or colorectal cancer. Data from two Malaysian cohorts comprising adults with breast or colorectal cancer were analysed. Comorbidities, verified against medical records, were grouped into 20 categories. LCA was used to identify comorbidity patterns. Outcomes included ECOG performance status (0-1 vs ≥ 2) and receipt of treatment (surgery, chemotherapy, radiotherapy, immunotherapy, anti-HER2, CDK4/6 inhibitors, hormone therapy). Among 1117 individuals, 695 (62.2%) had ≥ 1 comorbidity. Hypertension, dyslipidaemia, diabetes and obesity were most prevalent. LCA identified three classes: low (n = 723), cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) (n = 368) and multisystem (n = 26). All in the multisystem group and half in the CKM group had modified Charlson Comorbidity Index ≥ 3. The CKM group was older than the low-comorbidity group (62 vs 51 years) but did not differ in performance or treatment status. The multisystem group however had poorer performance status (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 4.04, 95%CI = 1.50-10.84), lower odds of receiving chemotherapy (aOR = 0.10, 95%CI = 0.04-0.25) and anti-HER2 therapy (aOR = 0.14, 95%CI = 0.02-0.86). Comorbidity patterns revealed differences that counts alone would have missed. The CKM class had similar performance status and treatment receipt to the low-comorbidity class despite cardiovascular and renal comorbidity, highlighting risks not reflected by performance status. The multisystem class requires validation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Fluoropyrimidine cardiotoxicity is uncommon but may cause life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias. A 43-year-old man with stage IIIB colon cancer developed chest discomfort and out-of-hospital ventricular fibrillation arrest approximately 72 hours after his first folinic acid (leucovorin), fluorouracil (5-FU), and oxaliplatin (FOLFOX) cycle. Electrocardiography showed anterior ST-segment elevations, but coronary angiography demonstrated nonobstructive left and right coronary arteries. Echocardiography showed a left ventricular ejection fraction of 25% to 30%, which improved to approximately 50% on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging without myocardial edema or late gadolinium enhancement. FOLFOX was discontinued, guideline-directed medical therapy was initiated, and an extravascular implantable cardioverter-defibrillator was placed for secondary prevention. This case highlights a rare, severe presentation of fluoropyrimidine cardiotoxicity after the first treatment cycle despite no prior cardiac history. Ventricular fibrillation may occur early during FOLFOX therapy. Prompt recognition and multidisciplinary cardio-oncology management are essential.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
We describe hospitalization rates in adolescent and young adult (AYA) cancer survivors 2-5 years (Y2-Y5) from diagnosis. Observational study of AYA cancer survivors diagnosed 2006-2020 was conducted in two healthcare systems [Kaiser Permanente Southern California (n=7889) and Northern California (n=7338)] and two states [California (47,302) and Utah (n=7935)]. Hospitalizations were ascertained from electronic health records and statewide administrative records and stratified by whether pregnancy-related. Hospitalization rates were calculated by cohort. We estimated patient factors associated with hospitalizations using a Poisson model. Most AYA survivors were women (~64% of all cohorts), mean age ~31 years at diagnosis, and non-Hispanic white (range 35.1-81.2%) or Hispanic (range 14.3-40.6%). Overall, 21-24% of AYA survivors experienced >1 hospitalization. Unadjusted hospitalization rates declined from Y2 [range 155.1-243.4 per 1000 person-years (PY)] to Y5 (range 105.8-132.0 PY) (p-trend<0.0001 in all cohorts). Factors associated with increased non-pregnancy related hospitalizations were [range of relative risks (RR)]: non-Hispanic Black race/ethnicity (RR 1.46-1.66 vs non-Hispanic white); public insurance (RR 1.57-1.93 vs commercial/military); receipt of chemotherapy (RR 1.51-1.81), and cancer type-breast (RR 1.69-1.97), cervical (RR 2.30-3.31), colorectal (2.76-3.66), acute lymphoblastic leukemia (RR 2.89-5.19), acute myeloid leukemia (2.11-5.05), and sarcoma (RR 2.70-4.96) (vs thyroid). While hospitalizations decline as time from diagnosis elapses across health system settings and states, nearly 1 in 5 AYA cancer survivors experience hospitalization in early survivorship. Hospitalization rates remain elevated in some AYA patient subgroups in early survivorship, highlighting the need to identify AYAs at risk to mitigate unanticipated hospitalizations and costs.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
While pathological and magnetic resonance imaging-based tumor regression grading systems are widely utilized following neoadjuvant therapy for rectal cancer, existing endoscopic approaches rely on qualitative assessment without quantitative weighting of individual features. Although individual endoscopic features associated with response have been described, no weighted scoring system exists to integrate these features into an objective assessment tool. This lack of a statistically weighted grading framework leads to subjective clinical impressions and significant interobserver variability in documentation and interpretation, limiting standardized patient selection for organ preservation strategies. To develop a quantitative, point-based endoscopic tumor Regression Grading system to standardize post-neoadjuvant therapy endoscopic assessment and predict pathological complete response. Retrospective cohort study. Single tertiary care center. Patients with locally advanced rectal cancer treated with total neoadjuvant therapy and surgical resection between 2018 and 2025 who had complete pre- and post-total neoadjuvant therapy endoscopic documentation were included. Two experienced colorectal surgeons independently evaluated endoscopic images in blinded fashion, scoring predefined endoscopic features. A statistically weighted, point-based scoring algorithm was developed, with quantitative point values assigned proportional to the strength of association with American Joint Committee on Cancer pathological response. The system incorporated mucosal healing features (whitening, telangiectasia, scarring, erythema), adverse features (ulceration, necrosis), mass regression levels, and stricture characteristics, classifying patients into 3 tiers: Endoscopic Tumor Regression Grading 1 (complete), Endoscopic Tumor Regression Grading 2 (near complete), or Endoscopic Tumor Regression Grading 3 (partial/incomplete). Predictive performance of the Endoscopic Tumor Regression Grading system for pathological complete response, 3-tier risk stratification, and interobserver reliability, evaluated using diagnostic performance metrics and receiver operating characteristic analysis. Seventy-six patients (mean age 58 ± 12 years; 58% male) were eligible. The 2 endoscopists demonstrated excellent interobserver agreement for the overall response assessment (weighted κ = 0.9) with 88.2% exact agreement. Univariate analysis identified whitening of the mucosa as the strongest predictor of complete response (odds ratio 47), followed by telangiectasia (odds ratio 23), scarring (odds ratio 16), and erythema (odds ratio 16). Ulceration and necrosis were powerful negative predictors (odds ratio 0.03 each). Each incremental level of mass regression (from no regression to < 50% to 50-99% to 100% regression) increased the odds of complete response 9.6-fold (all p < 0.01). The Endoscopic Tumor Regression Grading system demonstrated strong discrimination for predicting pathological complete response (area under the curve 0.85, 95% confidence interval 0.76-0.93) with a sensitivity of 83.3%, specificity of 76.1%, and accuracy of 78.9%. The Endoscopic Tumor Regression Grading 1 category identified patients with 69.4% pathological complete response probability, while Endoscopic Tumor Regression Grading was associated with 85.7% probability of pathological partial or incomplete response. Retrospective single-center pilot study requiring external validation. The Endoscopic Tumor Regression Grading system is the first statistically weighted, point-based scoring algorithm for endoscopic response assessment following neoadjuvant therapy. By quantitatively integrating multiple concurrent endoscopic features weighted by their predictive strength, this system addresses the limitations of qualitative grading, provides objective 3-tier risk stratification, and facilitates standardized patient selection for organ preservation strategies. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) represents a promising tool for dynamic molecular profiling in metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC), enabling monitoring of clonal tumor evolution and the detection of mechanisms of acquired resistance during treatment. The relevance of ctDNA has increased, particularly in the context of anti-EGFR therapy, where the emergence of RAS gene mutations constitutes a key resistance mechanism. The aim of this study was to evaluate the clinical utility of reassessing mutational status using ctDNA prior to rechallenge with anti-EGFR therapy in later treatment lines in patients with mCRC. A total of 17 patients with confirmed RAS and BRAF wild-type status in tumor tissue before initiation of first-line therapy were included in the analysis. All patients received anti-EGFR monoclonal antibody-based therapy in the first line and subsequently underwent ctDNA analysis from peripheral blood prior to initiation of third-line treatment using the Idylla™ qPCR platform. RAS gene mutations were detected in ctDNA in 4 patients, while 13 patients retained a wild-type status. Patients without detectable mutations achieved longer progression-free survival in the third-line setting compared with patients harboring RAS mutations. Overall survival from the start of third-line therapy was also prolonged in the wild-type ctDNA group. These findings suggest that the absence of resistant RAS clones in ctDNA may predict greater clinical benefit from anti-EGFR rechallenge. Liquid biopsy-based retesting may therefore represent an important tool for treatment individualization in later lines of mCRC therapy. This study also illustrates the translational potential of ctDNA analysis, linking dynamic molecular characterization of tumor evolution with clinically relevant treatment decision-making and the implementation of personalized oncology approaches.

To evaluate the association between preoperative neoadjuvant therapy and short-term outcomes of transanal total mesorectal excision for rectal cancer. We retrospectively analyzed patients who underwent transanal total mesorectal excision at 26 Japanese institutions between 2012 and 2019. Patients who received neoadjuvant therapy were matched 1:1 with patients who did not. Perioperative, postoperative, and pathological outcomes were compared. After matching, 294 patients (147 per group) were analyzed. Operative time was longer in the neoadjuvant therapy group than in the non-neoadjuvant therapy group (median, 510.0 vs. 382.0 min), with an adjusted mean difference of 129.25 min (95% CI, 87.90-170.59; Neoadjuvant therapy was associated with longer operative time during transanal total mesorectal excision, whereas no statistically significant association with severe postoperative morbidity was detected. Sensitivity analyses likewise did not identify a statistically significant association, supporting the technical feasibility of transanal total mesorectal excision after neoadjuvant therapy in experienced centers.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Coagulation activation is common in cancer, but its link to treatment durability is unclear. We investigated whether early-treatment coagulation activation correlated with radiographic progression during vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)/vascular endothelial growth factor receptor (VEGFR) inhibitor therapy. This single-center, retrospective, multicancer cohort study developed a coagulation activation score (0-2) based on the last available D-dimer (>500 ng/mL) and fibrinogen (>4.0 g/L) measurements taken within 100 days after baseline. Multivariable Cox models calculated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for subsequent radiographic time to progression among patients who were progression-free at the 100-day landmark. Of 1400 eligible patients, 1089 had evaluable early-treatment measurements, and 909 were included in the landmark analysis. Compared to a score of 0, adjusted HRs were 1.29 (95% CI 1.02-1.62) for score 1 and 1.51 (95% CI 1.07-2.12) for score 2. Score 2 also correlated with lower odds of durable clinical benefit (adjusted odds ratio 0.56, 95% CI 0.38-0.84), while objective response and best tumor shrinkage did not show a consistent gradient. These associations remained significant in time-dependent and timing-restricted analyses. Exploratory subgroup analyses revealed the strongest association in colorectal cancer patients treated with bevacizumab (score 2 vs. 0: HR 2.23, 95% CI 1.21-4.11); however, no association was observed in lung cancer patients treated with bevacizumab. No significant interaction with documented immune checkpoint inhibitor exposure was detected. The score did not enhance discrimination beyond clinical variables and baseline coagulation markers. Early-treatment coagulation activation was associated with reduced treatment durability during VEGF/VEGFR inhibition. Prospective validation in specific cancer-drug contexts is necessary.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the leading causes of cancer death worldwide, with outcomes depending on the stages at diagnosis. Genomic and transcriptomic classifications are largely inferential because the genotype-phenotype relationship is non-linear and is influenced by post-translational regulation, protein turnover, and the tumor microenvironment (TME). Proteomics measures this functional layer directly. This review surveys proteomic technologies for CRC emphasizing mass spectrometry, affinity- and aptamer- based multiplex platforms, post-translational modification proteomics, spatial proteomics, AI-driven structural and predictive analysis, and multi-omics integration. Each platform is evaluated based on clinical questions, the supporting evidence and the barriers to implementation. Literature was drawn primarily from PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus (2020-2026), emphasizing advanced and translational applications. Alongside approved blood cfDNA and stool-RNA molecular tests, proteomics is a functional complementary technology that may improve biological interpretation, assay triage and treatment response prediction, although prospective clinical utility remains to be established. The decisive barriers are standardized biospecimens, validation evidence, clinical utility data and interoperable public data sharing. (169 words).

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Socioeconomic and racial or ethnic inequalities affect colorectal cancer (CRC) across the care continuum. Although increasingly documented, whether current interventions effectively reduce these inequalities remains uncertain. To review socioeconomic and racial or ethnic inequalities in CRC incidence, screening and diagnosis, treatment, surveillance and survival and assess interventions designed to reduce them. We conducted a narrative review of adult studies published in English between January 2000 and March 2026. MEDLINE, EMBASE, PubMed, and ISI Web of Knowledge were searched for studies addressing socioeconomic or racial and ethnic disparities in CRC, using a saturation approach. Socioeconomic disadvantage and belonging to some racial or ethnic minority groups were associated with higher CRC incidence within high-income countries, lower screening participation, later diagnosis, less timely or guideline-concordant treatment, poorer surveillance and worse survival. In the USA, five-year survival was 60.6% among Black patients versus 66.7% among White patients, with little improvement in this gap over several decades. Inequalities at successive stages may contribute to cumulative disadvantage. Intervention evidence was markedly uneven across the continuum. Mailed stool-test outreach and patient navigation increased screening among underserved populations, whereas evidence for interventions specifically reducing inequalities in treatment, surveillance, and broader survivorship was sparse. Improving overall CRC prevention and care cannot be assumed to reduce inequalities. The major evidence gap has shifted from documenting disparities towards demonstrating how to reduce them, particularly beyond screening. Equity should become an explicit outcome of CRC research, implementation, healthcare quality assessment and clinical guidelines.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
RAS pathway mutations occur in ~ 40% of colorectal cancers (CRCs), with KRAS- and BRAF- mutant tumors exhibiting distinct mutational, transcriptional, and epigenetic landscapes. Advances in next-generation sequencing enable integrated analyses of multi-omics data, providing insight into their regulatory relationships. To define the molecular programs driven by RAS pathway mutations, we generated isogenic CRC cell models and profiled chromatin accessibility using ATAC-seq. We performed ATAC-seq in isogenic HCT116 and RKO models. Mutation-associated changes in genes, regulatory elements, and signaling pathways were identified, together with inferred transcription factor (TF) binding activity. Clinical datasets were analyzed to assess whether features identified in the cell models were recapitulated in patient tumors and whether they were associated with clinical outcomes. Isogenic CRC models segregated by RAS pathway mutation status at both epigenetic and transcriptomic levels. Mutation alterations modulated WNT signaling, accompanied by changes in RUNX2 and TCF7L2 expression and binding activity. Comparison between the HCT116 and RKO models identified 85 genes, eight of which displayed reproducible expression patterns across three independent clinical cohorts. TCF7L2 were associated with RAS pathway mutations in patient tumors, with elevated expression level predicting worse overall survival independent of cofactors. We identified RAS pathway mutation-driven regulatory reprogramming with convergent effects on WNT signaling. TCF7L2 emerged as a key TF, with elevated expression in BRAF-mutant tumors independently associated with poor clinical outcomes. These findings highlight a clinically relevant epigenetic mechanism linking RAS pathway mutations to CRC cell survival maintenance.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Diverting ileostomy is routinely used to protect the anastomosis after laparoscopic low anterior resection (LAR) for rectal cancer, but it exposes most patients to stoma-related morbidity even though only a minority develop a true anastomotic leak. This trial evaluated whether a postoperative C-reactive protein (CRP) and computed tomography (CT) guided selective ileostomy strategy could reduce the rate of ileostomy formation compared with routine diversion. In this RCT, 200 patients with stage II or III middle or lower third rectal cancer undergoing laparoscopic LAR were randomized 1:1 to a CRP/CT-guided selective ileostomy group (n = 100) or a routine diverting ileostomy group (n = 100). In the CRP/CT group, serum CRP was measured daily from postoperative day 1; a threshold of 114 mg/L on day 3 or a rise greater than 15 mg/L per day triggered confirmatory contrast-enhanced CT, with ileostomy formed only if findings were suspicious for leak. The primary outcome was the stoma-free status throughout the 12-month follow-up. Baseline demographic and tumor characteristics were similar between groups (all p > 0.05). Ileostomy formation was markedly lower in the CRP/CT group than the routine group (22.0% vs. 100.0%, p < 0.001). Anastomotic leak rates did not differ (0% vs. 1.0%, p = 1.000), nor did overall complication rates (31.0% vs. 32.0%, p = 0.879). Operative time (148.4 ± 14.0 vs. 166.6 ± 13.1 min, p < 0.001) and intraoperative blood loss (168.9 ± 28.2 vs. 197.3 ± 39.7 mL, p < 0.001) were significantly lower in the CRP/CT group. Stoma-related complications were far less frequent with the selective strategy (3.0% vs. 30.0%, p < 0.001). The CRP/CT group reported significantly better global health status, physical functioning, and emotional functioning scores (all p < 0.001). A postoperative CRP/CT-guided selective ileostomy strategy reduces the need for diverting ileostomy after laparoscopic low anterior resection for rectal cancer while improving operative outcomes and quality of life; however, confirmed leakage was infrequent in both groups. This approach may serve as an alternative to routine diversion in appropriately monitored surgical units. This trial was retrospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: NCT07722533) on July 17, 2026.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) has demonstrated limited efficacy in microsatellite stable (MSS) colorectal cancer (CRC). The fibroblast growth factor receptor (FGFR) signaling pathway contributes to tumor immune evasion, yet its role in CRC remains insufficiently understood. We investigated the immunomodulatory effects of FGFR inhibition in combination with PD-1 blockade in murine CRC models. In vitro co-culture systems were used to evaluate T cell activation upon FGFR3 blockade. RNA sequencing and bioinformatics analyses, including The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) dataset evaluation, were conducted to elucidate molecular mechanisms and clinical relevance. Combined FGFR inhibition and PD-1 blockade significantly reduced T cell exhaustion and promoted macrophage repolarization toward an antitumor phenotype. Transcriptomic profiling revealed upregulation of immune-related pathways and activation of immune-stimulatory genes. In vitro, FGFR3-specific monoclonal antibody treatment enhanced IFNg release following PD-1 blockade. Moreover, analysis of TCGA data demonstrated that high FGFR3 expression correlates with worse prognosis in CRC patients. Our findings suggest that FGFR pathway inhibition may enhance the efficacy of immune checkpoint blockade and provide a rationale for further investigation of FGFR-targeted combination strategies in MSS CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Two key factors required for pre-mRNA 3' end processing, CPSF73 and PCF11, are linked to poor cancer prognosis, yet their oncogenic roles remain unclear due to their dual function in transcription termination. Using a colorectal cancer (CRC) progression model, we show that primary tumor cells depend on high CPSF73 and PCF11 levels, whereas metastatic cells are less sensitive. This dependency is not explained by alternative polyadenylation (APA) or transcription-replication conflicts. Instead, we identify an uncoupling of 3' cleavage and transcription termination during CRC progression. Primary tumor cells exhibit a global shift toward proximal termination alongside distal APA usage, while metastatic cells partially revert to normal termination patterns and favor proximal APA. Notably, the distance between 3' cleavage and termination is nearly halved in primary tumor cells compared with normal cells and becomes particularly short in oncogenes. Reduced cleavage-termination distance correlates with increased gene expression both within and across cell states. These findings identify a previously unrecognized link between transcription termination architecture and gene expression regulation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
We identified areas of controversy in the management of patients with diverticular disease to develop key questions addressing the management of symptomatic uncomplicated diverticular disease (SUDD), uncomplicated diverticulitis, and complicated diverticulitis. We performed a systematic review to identify randomized trials and cohort studies addressing our key questions. Informed by an updated evidence synthesis, an international, multidisciplinary panel of gastrointestinal surgeons, gastroenterologists, patient partners, and methodologists applied the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) evidence-to-decision framework during panel consensus meetings to derive recommendations for the management of patients with diverticular disease. The systematic review identified 27 studies representing very low to moderate certainty evidence. The panel made the following recommendations: 1. In patients with SUDD, we suggest rifaximin or mesalamine over standard supportive care (conditional recommendation); 2. In patients with uncomplicated diverticulitis, we suggest no routine antibiotics (conditional recommendation); 3. In patients with persistent symptoms following an episode of recurrent uncomplicated diverticulitis, we suggest elective resection over observation (conditional recommendation); 4. In patients who have recovered from a first episode of uncomplicated diverticulitis, we suggest no routine follow-up colonoscopy (conditional recommendation); 5. In patients who have recovered from a first episode of diverticulitis complicated by an abscess, we suggest elective resection over surveillance (conditional recommendation). The panel judged that a significant proportion of patients would place a high value in reducing the risk of recurrence at 1 year but also acknowledged the lack of evidence addressing prioritized outcomes including 30-day major complications, need for emergency surgery, stoma-free survival at 1 year, and quality of life at 1 year. Given that patient values and preferences may vary, clinicians are encouraged to apply patient-centered decision-making and discuss the alternatives. This clinical practice guideline update provides evidence-informed recommendations to support patients and clinicians in the management of diverticular disease.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The prevalence of colorectal cancer in young adults is increasing worldwide but there is limited data from Latin American countries. In Mexico, the burden and clinical profile of colorectal adenocarcinoma in young patients are not well characterized. Our study aimed to estimate the prevalence of colorectal adenocarcinoma and describe its clinical characteristics, in young adult patients in Mexico. The PubMed and Web of Science databases were systematically searched from database inception to September 2024. The prevalence of colorectal adenocarcinoma in young adults in Mexico was evaluated, comparing the clinical characteristics of early-onset and late-onset cases. A pooled meta-analysis was carried out, using random effects models. Heterogeneity was assessed through the I² statistic, meta-regression, and subgroup analyses. The risk of bias was evaluated using the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist for Studies Reporting Prevalence Data. The pooled prevalence of colorectal adenocarcinoma in young adults was 10% (95% CI 6-15 %) in patients ≤40 years of age and 19% (95% CI 18-21 %) in those under 50 years of age. Meta-regression indicated a growing trend in the under 40 age group over time and the predominating clinical factors were male sex (52%), rectal involvement (44%), stage IV disease at diagnosis (32%), and a greater number of poorly differentiated tumors. Colorectal adenocarcinoma in young adults is an emerging public health concern in Mexico that requires specific strategies targeting prevention and early detection.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The first objective was to present fertility outcomes following surgery for deep endometriosis with colorectal involvement at an expert endometriosis center, and to compare conventional laparoscopy with robotic-assisted laparoscopy. Secondary objectives included an analysis of pregnancy and obstetric outcomes. We conducted a retrospective, monocentric cohort study involving patients who underwent surgery for endometriosis between February 2019 and January 2023, with colorectal resection and wishing to become pregnant either before surgery or in the immediate postoperative period. Among the 72 patients wishing to conceive, 23/34 patients (68%) in the robotic-assisted laparoscopy group achieved pregnancy, compared to 25/38 patients (66%) in the conventional laparoscopy group (not significant (NS)). Spontaneous pregnancies occurred in 11/23 patients (48%) and 9/25 patients (36%), respectively (NS). Among those who achieved pregnancy, 18/23 patients (78.3%) in the robotic-assisted laparoscopy group and 21/25 patients (84%) in the conventional laparoscopy group had at least one live birth (NS). Our findings suggest that surgery for deep endometriosis with colorectal involvement, whether performed via robotic-assisted or conventional laparoscopy, yields similar postoperative fertility outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
One of the uncertainty factors in estimating radiation-induced cancer risk is temporal changes in baseline cancer and all-cause mortality rates, which reflect advances in medical and diagnostic technologies, increased diagnostic frequency, and improvements in lifestyle, hygiene standards, and public health. Assessments of radiation-induced cancer risk have generally been performed using constant baseline data and therefore do not consider the effects of temporal changes in these data. To determine the effect of changes in baseline data on risk estimation, we calculated lifetime attributable risks (LARs) for individuals from six countries and different regions under two conditions: using constant baseline data and using baseline data that changed over time . The LARs were calculated for all solid cancers, oesophagus cancer, stomach cancer, colon cancer, lung cancer, and breast cancer. The LARs calculated using changing baseline data were comparable to those calculated using constant baseline data in 2021, and were, on average, approximately 1.7-fold higher (ranging from 0.8-to 4fold) than those calculated using constant baseline data in 1955. Furthermore, comparison of the effects of baseline data changes with that of other uncertainty factors indicated that the effect of baseline changes was greater than that of the minimum latency period but smaller than those of the fitting parameter of the risk models and the dose and dose-rate effectiveness factor.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Perturbation of microbial-derived bile acid (BA) metabolism is strongly linked to the pathogenesis of intestinal diseases, including inflammatory bowel disease, enteric infections, and colorectal cancer. Recent advances in artificial intelligence-assisted pipelines have enabled the identification of BA modification reactions, which have uncovered novel targets and the mechanisms contributing to intestinal diseases. In this review, we summarize recent studies on microbial enzymatic pathways and modifications of BAs, and their roles in promoting or preventing intestinal diseases. The mechanisms altering gut microbiota populations and microbial BA metabolic landscapes that influence intestinal diseases are further examined along with how microbial-derived BAs modulate intestinal immune responses. Based on these advances, we suggest different dietary patterns that reshape the gut microbiota community and BAs to prevent intestinal diseases. We further discuss current challenges in basic and translational research on microbial BA modifications in intestinal homeostasis and propose future directions to drive progress in this field.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) treatment remains limited by gastrointestinal toxicity, heterogeneous therapeutic responses, and treatment resistance. The gut microbiota has emerged as a modifiable factor implicated in these outcomes, particularly chemotherapy-induced toxicity. Probiotics, prebiotics, and synbiotics have been investigated as adjunctive strategies to mitigate chemotherapy-related harm. However, whether the field is ready to extend its focus toward oncologic endpoints, including treatment response, recurrence, and survival, remains unclear. We conducted a scoping review following the Arksey and O'Malley framework and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidance. PubMed, EBSCOhost, Scopus, and CENTRAL were searched through 18 February 2026 for studies evaluating probiotic, prebiotic, or synbiotic interventions in adults with CRC receiving systemic therapy. Primary clinical studies and systematic reviews were eligible. Outcomes included treatment-related toxicity, microbial composition, inflammatory and immune markers, and oncologic endpoints. Of 114 records screened, 16 studies were included, comprising 9 primary studies and 7 systematic reviews. Most studies evaluated probiotic-only regimens in patients receiving fluoropyrimidine- or oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy. The most consistent benefit was a reduction in chemotherapy-induced gastrointestinal toxicity, particularly diarrhea, mucositis, and nausea, along with improved treatment tolerance. Effects on microbial diversity, systemic inflammation, and immune parameters were inconsistent. Only 2 trials directly addressed oncologic outcomes: one reported significantly higher 6-, 12-, and 24-month survival in the probiotic arm, whereas another identified a microbiota-based classifier that predicted treatment response, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.95. However, neither trial comprehensively reported conventional oncologic endpoints such as objective response rate or progression-free survival. In addition, strain, dose, and timing varied widely across studies. Microbiota modulation is a plausible and well-tolerated adjunctive strategy in CRC. However, current evidence remains largely anchored to toxicity mitigation, while oncologic endpoints remain underexamined. The field appears ready to move beyond a supportive-care framework and prospectively test whether microbiota-targeted adjuncts influence treatment response, recurrence, and survival. Probiotics, prebiotics, and synbiotics should not be treated as interchangeable interventions. Advancing this research agenda will require adequately powered, strain-specific trials with prespecified oncologic endpoints, embedded microbiome and biomarker readouts, and harmonized reporting.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Living donor liver transplantation (LDLT) should not only be evaluated as an alternative graft source in transplant oncology; it should also be evaluated as a disease-specific intervention on access and oncologic time. By removing dependence on deceased-donor availability, LDLT can convert an uncertain wait into a planned operation-but that temporal advantage is not biologically neutral, and its consequences differ sharply by tumor type. In hepatocellular carcinoma, an abbreviated wait can reduce waitlist dropout but may also shorten the interval during which aggressive biology would otherwise declare itself; contemporary biology-based selection has reduced this concern in selected cohorts. In perihilar cholangiocarcinoma, LDLT solves organ scarcity, but the neoadjuvant and staging protocol-not the graft-must remain the actual selection mechanism, and irradiated recipient anatomy adds a distinct technical burden. In intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, LDLT remains investigational, justified only by durable response to systemic therapy in small, prospectively protocolized cohorts. In neuroendocrine liver metastases, direct living-donor evidence is too sparse to support a confident recommendation in either direction. In colorectal liver metastases, LDLT can be framed as a timing technology: transplantation is scheduled once sustained chemotherapy response suggests a temporarily favorable biological state, on the premise that an unpredictable wait might otherwise close that window. This narrative review deliberately isolates the living-donor evidence within each of these five diseases rather than treating LDLT as one intervention, and proposes a common framework-the oncologic clock, the strength of pre-transplant biological selection, and the donor risk that expected recipient benefit can justify-for interpreting it. We further argue that transplant benefit over the best nontransplant alternative, rather than post-transplant survival, should anchor these judgments; that left-lobe and two-stage (RAPID-type) grafting strategies offer a means to reduce donor risk; and that the appropriate metrics depend on whether LDLT operates within a deceased-donor-predominant or a living-donor-predominant health-care system. Across all five diseases, graft source itself appears to matter less than who is selected and when; the central task for the next generation of studies is to report outcomes from evaluation and donor exposure forward, not from transplantation alone.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cytoreductive surgery (CRS) and oxaliplatin-based hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC) is controversial in patients with colorectal peritoneal metastases, particularly in those who have received prior systemic oxaliplatin. In the Netherlands, upfront CRS-HIPEC remains the preferred treatment. The aim was to compare the survival of patients with colorectal peritoneal metastases treated with CRS and mitomycin C versus oxaliplatin-based HIPEC. This was a retrospective, single-center cohort study of consecutive patients with colorectal peritoneal metastases who underwent macroscopic complete CRS-HIPEC between 2010 and 2023. Main outcomes were differences in disease-free, peritoneal disease-free, distant disease-free, and overall survival. Of 366 patients included, 153 and 213 underwent mitomycin C-based and oxaliplatin-based HIPEC, respectively. Most patients (68.6%) underwent upfront CRS-HIPEC. Median follow-up was 58.7 months (range, 24.8 - 175.1) and median overall survival was 43.3 months (95% CI, 36.5 - 49.9). In multivariable analyses, oxaliplatin-based HIPEC was associated with worse peritoneal disease-free survival compared to mitomycin C-based HIPEC (median 11.3 vs. 14.9 months; HR 1.44, 95% CI, 1.09 - 1.90; P = .010). No difference was observed in disease-free, distant disease-free, and overall survival. Among patients treated with oxaliplatin-based HIPEC, prior systemic oxaliplatin exposure was associated with worse peritoneal disease-free survival (median 8.7 vs. 13.1 months; HR 1.59, 95% CI, 1.10 - 2.31; P = .014) and overall survival (median 35.7 vs. 50.6 months; HR 1.55, 95% CI, 1.07 - 2.23; P = .020) compared to no prior oxaliplatin exposure. Oxaliplatin-based HIPEC was associated with a higher risk of peritoneal recurrence, particularly in patients previously treated with systemic oxaliplatin. Mitomycin C-based HIPEC is a better choice in this subgroup.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The integration of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) into neoadjuvant strategies is increasingly being studied in locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC), to improve complete response (CR), organ preservation, and potentially overall survival (OS). However, the clinical impact of conventional PD-1 blockade still remains limited in proficient mismatch repair/microsatellite-stable (pMMR/MSS) disease, suggesting that its simple addition to standard neoadjuvant therapy may be insufficient. By contrast, deficient mismatch repair/microsatellite instability-high (dMMR/MSI-H) rectal cancer displays marked sensitivity to PD-1 blockade, enabling non-operative management in a substantial proportion of patients, although primary resistance and incomplete responses are increasingly recognized. In this review, we critically discuss the available randomized evidence and the biological determinants of response to neoadjuvant immunotherapy, with particular focus on pMMR/MSS disease. We examine the role of pre-existing antitumor immunity and potential biomarkers such as PD-L1 and Immunoscore, as well as how radiotherapy integration, novel ICIs, and immune-sensitizing strategies may enhance ICI efficacy. Finally, we also address emerging challenges in dMMR/MSI-H rectal cancer and potential strategies to overcome resistance. Moving from empiric ICI addition toward biologically informed and rationally designed immune-based strategies may represent the next step to maximize complete response and organ preservation in rectal cancer.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Accurate assessment of lymph node metastasis (LNM) is critical for prognostic stratification and treatment selection in colorectal cancer (CRC), yet imaging and routine pathology can yield false-negative/false-positive results. We propose DeepLNM, a multi-center foundation model for LNM prediction in CRC, evaluated with retrospective, external, prospective, and user study evidence. A multimodal dataset was assembled from three hospitals, with matched hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained whole-slide images (WSI), CT scans, and text. DeepLNM achieved a mean AUC of 0.922 in the internal cohort and AUCs of 0.872 and 0.848 in two external cohorts. In a prospective cohort from a registered clinical trial (NCT07239063), DeepLNM remained robust (AUC = 0.845). In a user study, DeepLNM improved diagnostic accuracy, especially for junior pathologists (95.0%-97.3%), while reducing diagnostic time and increasing confidence. To explore the model's generalizability, it was further validated in a gastric cancer cohort, achieving an AUC of 0.793. Finally, DeepLNM identified histopathological features associated with LNM, addressing the "black-box" concern of deep learning. Together, these results position DeepLNM as a clinically preliminarily validated multimodal model for predicting LNM status in CRC, potentially facilitating the clinical translation of AI pathology.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Reliable circulating biomarkers for chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) remain lacking. Phosphorylated neurofilament-heavy chain (pNF-H) is an axon-oriented biomarker of neuroaxonal injury, but its clinical relevance in oxaliplatin-induced peripheral neuropathy has not been established. We evaluated the feasibility and longitudinal behavior of plasma pNF-H in patients receiving oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy. This prospective multi-institutional exploratory study included patients with unresectable or recurrent colorectal cancer receiving CapeOX plus bevacizumab as part of the NYX study, a randomised trial of ninjin'yoeito (NYT; TJ-108, Tsumura & Co., Tokyo, Japan), a twelve-ingredient Kampo herbal extract, at 9.0 g/day for 24 weeks in the NYT arm. Plasma samples were collected at baseline, at clinically assessed CIPN onset (follow-up 1), and at the time of neuropathy resolution, at cycle 9, or at discontinuation, whichever came first (follow-up 2). Plasma pNF-H concentrations were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. CIPN was assessed using CTCAE version 5.0. Thirty patients with evaluable plasma samples were included. Plasma pNF-H levels showed substantial inter-individual variability without a consistent temporal pattern. Compared with baseline and CIPN onset, plasma pNF-H levels at follow-up 2 were modestly but significantly increased. However, plasma pNF-H levels were not associated with the onset, severity, or persistence of clinically assessed CIPN. Although longitudinal plasma pNF-H measurement was technically feasible, pNF-H did not function as a clinically meaningful biomarker for oxaliplatin-induced peripheral neuropathy. These findings may reflect a pathophysiological mismatch between dorsal root ganglion neuronal cell body injury and the axon-oriented biological specificity of pNF-H.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Lynch syndrome, a prevalent hereditary cancer predisposition, is frequently caused by pathogenic variants in the MutL homolog 1 (MLH1) mismatch repair gene. However, a significant proportion of MLH1 missense variants remain classified as variants of uncertain significance (VUS), creating clinical ambiguity. Functional validation assays in vertebrate models are crucial to assess the pathogenicity of these VUS. We previously reported the rare MLH1 NM_000249.4:c.335A>G (p.His112Arg) variant in individuals with cancer histories within the Qatar Genome Program. To assess its functional impact, we established the MLH1 p.His112Arg variant in the human colorectal cancer cell line, COLO205, using CRISPR-Cas9 technology. Isogenic wild-type (WT) and variant-carrying cells were xenotransplanted into the zebrafish. Tumor growth was quantified via fluorescence microscopy at 24 and 72 h post-injection. Zebrafish xenografted with MLH1 p.His112Arg cells exhibited a significant increase in tumor area compared to WT. This accelerated growth was associated with a significant upregulation of the proliferation marker MKI67 in variant-carrying tumors, while cyclin D1 (CCND1) and proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA) (key regulators of cell cycle progression and DNA replication, respectively) expression remained unchanged, despite a tendency for increased expression. Furthermore, our functional characterization of the MLH1 p.His112Arg variant in COLO205 cells showed an enhanced proliferation capacity compared to the WT cell line, as well as increased cell viability and decreased apoptotic susceptibility when subjected to methylation-induced DNA damage. The MLH1 p.His112Arg variant confers a tumor-promoting phenotype in an in vivo zebrafish model, providing functional evidence that supports its reclassification from VUS to likely pathogenic.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer is now the leading cause of cancer-related deaths for people under the age of 50. As an initial step of the Early-Onset Colorectal Cancer Awareness Campaign, the purpose of this study was to survey a large sample of members of the public age 20 to 44 to determine their baseline levels of early-onset colorectal cancer understanding as well as their comfort discussing early-onset colorectal cancer and the associated symptoms. This was an online survey conducted in December 2025, before the launch of the Early-Onset Colorectal Cancer Awareness Campaign, to establish baseline measures. Baseline demographics were collected, including age, gender, race/ethnicity, region, and survey language. Survey measures were developed based on the Health Belief Model, focus group findings, and subject matter expert review. Participants aged 20 to 44 were recruited from a respondent panel maintained by a market-research vendor, and recruitment was stopped after meeting a quota of 1,000 respondents. Healthcare providers were excluded. A total of 1,000 respondents were included with even distribution of age and sex. The survey was taken in Spanish by 27%. Overall awareness of colorectal cancer (CRC) and early-onset colorectal cancer was low (41 and 24%, respectively). Knowledge of family history was low for colorectal cancer (22%) as well as colorectal polyps (17%). Twenty-nine percent of respondents had not heard of any symptoms of colorectal cancer while 36% identified rectal bleeding and 29% identified changes in stool habits as symptoms of colorectal cancer. Only 22% of respondents had looked for information on colorectal cancer within the last year. Female respondents felt less comfortable than their male counterparts discussing early-onset colorectal cancer with a healthcare provider (55 vs 67%, p = 0.017) or with their friends and family (56% vs 67%, p = 0.025). When asked about potential reasons to avoid or postpone a colonoscopy, respondents reported concerns about cost (69%), risk of complications (68%), fear of a cancer diagnosis (68%), and mistrust of the health care system (57%). The limitations of the study include the use of an opt-in survey, as this requires a self-selected group of respondents with potential differences in health literacy, digital engagement, and survey-taking behavior from the public. Currently, people under the age of 45 have a low overall understanding of early-onset colorectal cancer, and most are unaware of their own family history of colorectal cancer and colon polyps. Several important roadblocks to gaining information and/or seeking care for early-onset colorectal cancer were also identified. These findings will be used to inform future efforts of the Early-Onset Colorectal Cancer Awareness Campaign. See Video Abstract.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The clinical efficacy of currently available third- and later-line treatment regimens for patients with metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) remains suboptimal. This study was designed to investigate fruquintinib plus TAS-102 regimen in this patient population. This study was a prospective, multi-center, single-arm phase II trial. A total of 50 patients with mCRC who had experienced treatment failure to at least two standard therapies were enrolled. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS) and secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), objective response rate (ORR), disease control rate (DCR), and safety. Survival outcomes were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. With a median follow-up duration of 25.1 months, the median PFS was 6.07 months (95% CI: 4.07-7.87) and the median OS was 14.10 months (95% CI: 9.84-23.28). The ORR was 10.0% (95% CI: 3.3-21.8), with a DCR of 66.0% (95% CI: 51.2-78.8). All the patients experienced treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs), with 68.0% reporting grade ≥ 3 TRAEs. No serious adverse events (AEs), deaths, or new safety concerns were reported. In conclusion, fruquintinib combined with TAS-102 showed preliminary anti-tumor activity with a manageable safety profile in patients with refractory mCRC, which highlights its potential as a viable later-line therapeutic option.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer is still a leading cause of cancer morbidity and mortality in the world. This is a reflection of the limitations of current chemotherapy and the need for additional therapeutic strategies. Phytochemicals from plants have been of great interest recently because they can affect several pathways involved in cancer. In this review, we combine bibliometric mapping with a narrative synthesis to discuss the changing nature of phytochemical research in colorectal cancer. A total of 1029 records from Web of Science, covering January 2000 to December 2025, were analyzed using VOSviewer, Bibliometrix, and CiteSpace. The trend of publications is steadily increasing, particularly since 2020. Keyword mapping revealed some common themes, particularly apoptosis, flavonoids, curcumin, quercetin, network pharmacology, nanoparticles, and ferroptosis. The literature shows a transition from early screening studies to more in-depth mechanistic and translational studies. From the bibliometric findings, five areas are identified that might influence the future development of the field. These areas include modulation of multiple signaling pathways, regulated cell death, interactions between the gut microbiome and immune system, overcoming chemoresistance, and innovative delivery systems to enhance bioavailability. Taken together, these findings suggest that phytochemicals act as multi-target compounds rather than single cytotoxic agents with promising potential in combination therapies for colorectal cancer. Materials and delivery research accounts for a rising share of this corpus, increasing from 0.0% of records published between 2000 and 2011 to 16.0% of those published between 2020 and 2025, and nanoparticles emerge as a major keyword cluster although no materials term appears in the search string. The review therefore treats biomaterial design as a component of the field rather than as an adjunct to it, covering polymeric, lipid, inorganic, biomimetic and stimuli-responsive platforms against a common set of performance criteria.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
As biomarkers separated by the arbitrary 5-tumor-cell cutoff at the tumor invasive front, tumor budding (TB) and poorly differentiated clusters (PDC) are recognized as high-risk factors for lymph node metastasis (LNM) in pT1 colorectal cancer (CRC). Nonetheless, relevant findings remain inconsistent. Furthermore, the association between the tumor invasive front biomarker and D3 LNM in pT1 CRC remains unknown. To identify a biomarker that captures the full morphologic spectrum and eliminates the need for such cutoffs at the tumor invasive front for predicting LNM, particularly D3 LNM, in pT1 CRC, we defined peritumoral malignant cellular foci (PMCF) as nonglandular foci composed of ≥1 tumor cell at the tumor invasive front. After enrolling 2611 endoscopically or surgically resected pT1 CRC patients from 6 high-volume Chinese institutions, we found that neither TB nor PDC exhibited a consistent independent association with LNM across the training and validation cohorts. In contrast, PMCF emerged as an independent risk factor with superior risk stratification of LNM in both cohorts (P<0.05). The association between PMCF and LNM remained significant in subgroup analyses stratified by age, sex, tumor location, and BMI (P<0.05). Moreover, PMCF correlated with a greater number of metastatic lymph nodes and exhibited a stronger association with D3 LNM than with D1 and D2 LNM (P<0.05). In conclusion, PMCF not only suggests additional radical surgery after endoscopic resection in pT1 CRC, but may also indicate D3 lymph node dissection. PMCF provides an evidence-based rationale to optimize surgical decision-making in pT1 CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Low-dose aspirin use is associated with reduced CRC incidence and CRC-related mortality. A similar association with P2Y12 inhibitor use remains uncertain. We investigated whether the use of P2Y12 inhibitors was associated with CRC incidence and CRC-related mortality among individuals diagnosed with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). From the ESPRESSO cohort, we identified 334,882 patients diagnosed with ASCVD between 2006 and 2021. We identified patients who initiated P2Y12 inhibitors ≥ 84 consecutive Defined Daily Doses (cDDDs). We estimated the risk of incident CRC and CRC mortality according to P2Y12 inhibitor use using Cox proportional-hazards regression models adjusting for potential confounders including comorbidities and regular aspirin use. We documented 4,015 incident CRC cases and 2,610 CRC-related deaths during a median follow-up of 5.1 years (IRQ, 2.1-9.0 years). We did not observe an association between P2Y12 inhibitor use and CRC incidence. In contrast, a longer duration of P2Y12 inhibitor use was associated with lower CRC-related mortality. Compared to non-users, multivariable-adjusted hazard ratio (HR) for CRC mortality were 0.73 (95% CI, 0.60-0.89) in patients with 336-671 cDDDs of P2Y12 inhibitor and 0.81 (95% CI, 0.68-0.97) in those with ≥672 cDDDs. Among patients with incident CRC diagnosis, subsequent initiation of P2Y12 inhibitor after CRC diagnosis was associated with significantly lower CRC mortality (HR 0.42; 95% CI, 0.29-0.60). P2Y12 inhibitor use was not associated with risk of incident CRC but was significantly inversely associated with CRC mortality, which appeared to be due to improved survival among individuals who initiate P2Y12 inhibitors after CRC diagnosis. These findings merit further study given the observational nature of the analysis and potential for residual confounding.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The Karolinska Liver Metastases (KaroLiver) cohort was established to investigate associations between clinical characteristics and histopathological features in patients treated with curative intent for colorectal cancer liver metastases (CRLM). The cohort combines whole-slide digital histopathology images with detailed oncological, surgical, radiological and survival data, enabling comprehensive analyses of treatment trajectories, clinical outcomes and metastatic tumour biology. KaroLiver is a retrospective observational cohort comprising all consecutive patients who received curative-intent, liver-directed treatment for CRLM at Karolinska University Hospital in Stockholm, Sweden. The hospital is the regional referral centre for hepatopancreatobiliary (HPB) surgery, serving the population of approximately 2.5 million people in the Stockholm-Gotland healthcare region. Patient enrolment is continuously updated in accordance with amended ethical approvals and evolving scientific questions. The cohort currently comprises 811 patients who underwent 1204 liver interventions between February 2012 and January 2022. Detailed clinical, oncological, surgical, pathological, molecular, recurrence and survival data are collected. Median overall survival (OS) in the current cohort is 51.0 months (95% CI 46.2 to 57.1 months), and median recurrence-free survival (RFS) is 10.4 months (95% CI 9.2 to 11.9 months). The 5-year OS rate is 44.9% (95% CI 41.2% to 48.8%). Studies using the cohort have so far identified a liver injury-derived stromal capsule in a subset of metastases associated with improved survival. The cohort has also enabled the identification of histopathological markers of tumour biology, sex-based differences in treatment and survival, and associations between post-hepatectomy liver failure and oncological outcomes. Current research priorities include advanced histology-based prognostic scoring, sex differences in recurrence and retreatment, tumour biology and outcomes in early-onset versus average-onset CRLM, as well as CT-based and MRI-based radiomics, all integrated within KaroLiver’s histopathological framework. Data sharing is supported, given that regulatory requirements are met. Retrospective accrual and outcome updates will continue for current and future studies, subject to the required approvals.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
This retrospective analysis compares postoperative length of stay in patients undergoing colorectal surgery who received naloxegol or alvimopan as part of an Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) protocol. This is a systemwide retrospective cohort. The community health system switched from alvimopan to naloxegol as the peripherally acting mu-opioid receptor antagonist (PAMORA) agent used in the colorectal ERAS protocol in December 2024. Adult patients who underwent colorectal surgery and received one PAMORA dose for surgical discharge dates between May 2024 and August 2025 were included. There was no difference in median length of stay (alvimopan 3.2 days [2.2-6.2] versus naloxegol 3.3 days [2.2-5.9], p = 0.881). Median bowel function return was achieved sooner in patients receiving alvimopan (1.4 days [1.1-2.1] versus 1.7 [1.2-2.4], p = 0.015), however all-cause 30-day readmission rates were higher in the alvimopan group (15.2% versus 8.2%, p = 0.021). Patients in the alvimopan group were more likely to receive a dose prior to the procedure than naloxegol (89.1% versus 76.4%, p < 0.001). A subgroup analysis of those patients revealed there was no difference in median length of stay, median bowel function return, or incidence of postoperative ileus, with higher readmission rates in the alvimopan group (p = 0.005). The average PAMORA cost per admission who received alvimopan was approximately 16 times more expensive than naloxegol. Switching from alvimopan to naloxegol in colorectal ERAS protocols is a potential cost-saving initiative for formulary management that was associated with similar observed length of stay and postoperative ileus rates.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
ShenqiYichang decoction (SQYCD) is a traditional Chinese formula indicated for colorectal cancer (CRC). Studies have shown that SQYCD potentiates antitumor immunity and enhances the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). This study aimed to investigate the mechanism of SQYCD in enhancing ICIs efficacy against microsatellite stability (MSS) CRC. An in vivo CT26 tumor-bearing mouse model was established. The antitumor efficacy of SQYCD alone and in combination with ICIs was evaluated, and Treg infiltration was detected by immunofluorescence. Network pharmacology and bioinformatics were used to screen potential targets of SQYCD for MSS CRC. In vitro, MSS CRC cell lines were used for CCK-8 to assess cell proliferation. A CT26-Treg co-culture system was used to analyze Treg proportion by flow cytometry. Western blot, qRT-PCR, ELISA, and Co-IP assays were used to assess the IDO1/Kyn/p-AKT axis and IDO1-PI3K interactions. UPLC-Q-TOF/MS and molecular docking were subsequently employed to identify the key absorbed components involved in the IDO1-PI3K pathway regulated by SQYCD. In vivo, SQYCD alone did not affect the proliferation of MSS CRC cells but inhibited Treg infiltration. When combined with ICIs, SQYCD enhanced the efficacy of ICIs, significantly inhibiting tumor cell proliferation and further reducing Treg infiltration. Network pharmacology and bioinformatics analysis suggested IDO1 as a potential target of SQYCD in MSS CRC. In vitro, SQYCD-containing serum did not reduce MSS CRC cell proliferation but decreased Treg proportion in the CT26-Treg co-culture system. SQYCD also promoted IL-2 levels while downregulating IL-10 and TGF-β levels. Mechanistically, SQYCD suppressed the IDO1/Kyn pathway and p-AKT expression. Additionally, components of SQYCD significantly reduced the IDO1-PI3K interaction. LC-MS and molecular docking results suggested that esculetin, glycitin, and hydroxygenkwanin may be the active components of SQYCD that reduce the IDO1-PI3K interaction. SQYCD reduces Treg infiltration by inhibiting both the IDO1/Kyn/p-AKT and the IDO1-PI3K interaction, consequently enhancing the efficacy of ICIs.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Ulcerative colitis is a chronic inflammatory disorder characterized by diffuse mucosal inflammation confined to the colon and rectum. Long pepper is a widely used condiment for stews and barbecues and is known for its potential nutritional and medicinal value. Piperlongumine (PPL), the major active component of long pepper, represents a promising anti-inflammatory agent. However, the precise mechanism by which PPL regulates colitis remains unclear and requires further elucidation. In this study, we found that PPL interfered with NLRP3 inflammasome assembly in mouse and human macrophages and inhibited inflammasome-mediated pyroptosis. Mechanistic exploration revealed that PPL impaired NLRP3-ASC complex assembly and subsequent inflammasome activation largely by promoting β-catenin proteasomal degradation and reducing β-catenin abundance, with a minor contribution from a β-catenin-independent pathway. Most importantly, PPL alleviated pathological features of dextran sulfate sodium-induced colitis, including colorectal shortening, body weight loss, occult blood, and decreased neutrophil infiltration. In summary, PPL is a food-derived ingredient with anti-inflammatory properties that ameliorates colitis by suppressing NLRP3 inflammasome activation and pyroptosis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Antiapoptotic buffering in solid tumors is generally mediated by both BCLXL and MCL1, so that BH3 mimetic drugs targeting only one have limited efficacy. To identify agents that may sensitize tumors to BH3 mimetics targeting BCLXL, we screened prostate cancer cells against a panel of mitochondria-targeted drugs in combination with navitoclax, a BH3 mimetic targeting BCL2 and BCLXL. Homoharringtonine (HHT) in combination with navitoclax and as a single agent emerged as a potent inducer of apoptosis. HHT has been identified as an inhibitor of protein translation, and proteomic analysis showed broad suppression of translation-related pathways, while immunoblotting demonstrated rapid decreases in short-lived proteins, including MCL1. HHT dose response and time course studies showed marked declines in MCL1 within 2 hours that were associated with apoptosis in response to BCLXL inhibition with navitoclax or A1331852. Further cell viability assays showed synergy between HHT and BCLXL inhibitors in multiple prostate, lung, and colorectal cancer cell lines. HHT monotherapy in vivo caused tumor regression in two prostate cancer xenograft models. Analysis of tumor tissue taken at 4 hours after dosing showed decreases in MCL1 and MYC, indicating that HHT levels obtainable in vivo are adequate to deplete short-lived proteins and potentially sensitize to BH3 mimetics targeting BCLXL. These findings support further exploration of HHT as a single agent in solid tumors and establish a rationale for investigating safer, tumor-selective approaches to combine HHT-mediated translational inhibition with BCLXL targeting.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cellular inhibitor of apoptosis proteins 1 and 2 (cIAP1 and cIAP2), encoded by BIRC2 and BIRC3, respectively, are important regulators of cellular survival and apoptosis. These proteins contribute to cancer cell survival by suppressing apoptotic signaling. While individual knockouts of BIRC2 or BIRC3 in cancer cells have been investigated, the consequences of simultaneously targeting both paralogs remain poorly understood. Thus, a single-gRNA CRISPR/eCas9 strategy was developed in which one gRNA targeting a shared sequence in BIRC2 and BIRC3 was used to simultaneously disrupt both genes in human colorectal cancer HCT-116 cells, and the resulting cellular and transcriptomic effects were compared with those of the individual knockouts. Individual and dual-targeting CRISPR/eCas9 constructs were experimentally validated by immunofluorescence analysis, RT-PCR, and RT-qPCR, while fluorescence microscopy and T7EI analysis were used to evaluate single-cell-derived clones. Apoptosis was evaluated using flow cytometry, and RNA sequencing was performed for differentially expressed gene (DEG) analysis. The single-gRNA dual-targeting strategy resulted in concurrent loss of cIAP1 and cIAP2 expression and produced a stronger reduction in cell survival and induction of apoptosis than targeting either gene individually. In addition, the expression levels of TNFRSF25, TRAF2, TNFSF15, and MIR663AHG were significantly upregulated following simultaneous BIRC2/BIRC3 targeting. RNA-seq analysis provided detailed insight into the molecular alterations associated with concurrent cIAP1 and cIAP2 depletion. Overall, these findings demonstrate the technical feasibility of targeting two highly homologous genes with a single gRNA and reveal that simultaneous disruption of cIAP1 and cIAP2 produces biological effects that are more pronounced than those observed following individual targeting.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Transposable elements (TEs) are broadly reactivated in tumors, but their repetitive nature has limited transcript-level characterization. Here, we systematically investigate the TE-derived splicing landscape across pan-cancer samples and define a splice-resolved subset of TE-derived transcripts, termed TEtrans, with tumor enrichment and gene independence. TEtrans initiate within TEs, spliced within or between TE loci, and are composed predominantly of TE sequences. Their expression was associated with stemness and inflammation regulators in a context-dependent manner. Functional analyses identify an endogenous retrovirus-derived TEtrans that promotes colorectal cancer growth by enhancing topoisomerase I-mediated DNA relaxation. A subset of TEtrans encodes shared tumor antigens that elicit antigen-specific cytotoxic T cell responses, while a murine TEtrans-like transcript mediates antigen-dependent tumor control in vivo. Collectively, TEtrans represent a splice-resolved source of TE-derived oncogenic drivers and actionable tumor antigens, broadening the scope of TE reactivation in cancer.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
We compared baseline characteristics, outcomes and patterns of failure between patients undergoing cytoreductive surgery and hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (CRS/HIPEC) for peritoneal disseminations from appendiceal (MACA) or colorectal mucinous adenocarcinoma (MCRC), in order to assess clinical and prognostical differences. Colorectal origin was associated with lower peritoneal cancer index (PCI) (P < 0.001), lower rates of signet-ring cells histology (P = 0.016), T4a/b primaries (P < 0.001), negative nodes (P < 0.001), synchronous metastases (P < 0.001), microsatellite stability (P = 0.009), wild-type KRAS (P < 0.001) and BRAF (P < 0.001), but not wild-type NRAS (P = 0.999), incomplete cytoreduction (P = 0.014), and perioperative systemic anticancer treatments (s-ACT) (P < 0.001). Median follow-up was 70.5 months (95% confidence interval [CI] = 45.8-92.3) for MACA, and 40.2 months (95%CI = 35.4-55.2) for MCRC. Five-year overall survival was 58.9% (95%CI = 51.3-67.5) for MACA, and 35.4% (95%CI = 27.1-46.2) for MCRC (P < 0.001). Appendiceal origin correlated with better prognosis at multivariate analysis (hazard-ratio 2.52; 95%CI = 1.50-4.25; P < 0.001). Five-year cumulative incidence of distant relapses was higher for MCRC: 42.6% (95%CI = 30.8-52.4) vs. 28.1% (95%CI = 19.7-35.7) (P = 0.032). Incidence of peritoneal relapse was not different (P = 0.706). PCI correlated with survival in MCRC (P < 0.001), but not in MACA. Perioperative s-ACT correlated with worse prognosis in MACA (P = 0.024), but not in MCRC (P = 0.920). Peritoneal disseminations from MACA are associated with distinct clinical-biological features, better prognosis and lower incidence of systemic relapses, suggesting that MCRC and MACA are different entities. MACA should not be excluded from CRS/HIPEC based only on higher PCI. The role of s-ACT remain unclear.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cancer incidence is rising among young adults in several high-income countries, yet comprehensive data from Southern Europe, particularly Portugal, remain limited. We characterized temporal trends in cancer incidence among young adults (20-49 years) in Portugal between 2001 and 2022, comparing them with older adults (≥50 years).
