Age-standardized incidence rates (ASIR) per 100,000 inhabitants were calculated using the European Standard Population. Temporal trends were analysed using joinpoint regression, estimating annual percentage changes (APC) and average annual percentage changes (AAPC) by sex, age group, and cancer type. Cancer cases increased from 36,604 in 2001 to 60,926 in 2022. Young adults accounted for 13.0% of all cases. Among young women, ASIR increased by 31.6% (from 156.2 to 205.6; AAPC: +1.48%), driven largely by breast cancer (+50.0%), thyroid (+94.1%), melanoma (+84.1%), and lung cancer (+78.7%). In contrast, young men showed stable overall ASIR (AAPC: -0.05%), with a biphasic pattern of increase (2001-2010) followed by decline (2010-2022). However, young men experienced substantial rises in colorectal (+56.6%), thyroid (+185.1%), and melanoma (+70.1%) incidence, alongside declines in stomach (-67.0%), oesophageal (-56.8%), and lung (-45.8%) cancers. Older adults demonstrated significant ASIR increases driven by trends before 2011, with subsequent stabilization or decline. Cancer incidence among young Portuguese adults is increasing, particularly among women, with sex-specific and site-specific patterns. While declines in tobacco-related cancers reflect successful prevention efforts, rising rates of breast, colorectal, thyroid, and melanoma in young adults signal the need for enhanced targeted prevention strategies and continued etiological research.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The Brazilian Cerrado harbors 12,180 cataloged angiosperm species; 7395 (60.7%) are endemic to Brazil, and its flora has been used in traditional medicine for generations. Regardless, the antitumor potential of these species has been investigated in a fragmented manner. To compile and analyze experimental evidence on the antitumor effects of preparations derived from Cerrado plant species in vitro and in vivo models. Searches were conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and Scopus, without date restrictions and limited to publications in English. The methodological quality of included studies was assessed using an adapted risk-of-bias assessment tool. Sixty-two studies were included; 55 employed in vitro models and 12 employed in vivo models, five of which combined both approaches. The studies encompassed a broad range of malignancies, including melanoma, leukemias, glioblastoma, and breast, prostate, and colorectal cancers, and evaluated crude extracts, fractions, and isolated compounds from >40 species. The most frequently documented antitumor effects were cell viability reduction, apoptosis induction via the intrinsic mitochondrial pathway, cell cycle arrest, and matrix metalloproteinase inhibition. Annona crassiflora, Campomanesia adamantium, Stryphnodendron adstringens, and Tapirira guianensis were each reported in three or more independent studies (most frequently investigated species). Relevant methodological limitations, including a widespread absence of tumor selectivity data, pharmacokinetic profiles, and experimental blinding, were revealed. No clinical trials evaluating Cerrado plant species as oncological interventions were identified. The Cerrado flora represents a relevant source of compounds with preclinical antitumor activity, but essential translational data remain absent. PROSPERO database (CRD420261372222). Available from https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261372222.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The clinical translation of small extracellular vesicle-derived microRNAs (sEV-miRNAs) for early colorectal cancer (CRC) diagnosis is often limited by their low abundance and complexity of biological fluids. Herein, we developed an ultrasensitive electrochemical platform based on multifunctional DNA nanoflower-assisted catalytic hairpin assembly (NF-CHA) for sEV-miRNAs detection. The NF acts as a localized scaffold to accelerate CHA kinetics and load abundant signal reporter. As a result, the NF-CHA strategy enables the platform achieving a limit of detection of 23.65 aM. To improve diagnostic performance, we employed different sEV-miRNAs combination and machine learning (ML) algorithms, achieving an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.996 for distinguishing early-stage CRC from healthy donors in clinical samples. Therefore, the electrochemical platform holds a great promise as a robust tool for CRC early diagnosis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, necessitating novel therapeutic strategies. Ferroptosis, an iron‑dependent, lipid-peroxidation-driven form of cell death, has emerged as a potential tumor‑suppressive mechanism. Artemether, a derivative of Artemisia annua L., exhibits antitumor activity in various cancers, but its role in CRC and its link to ferroptosis remain unclear. Using an HCT116 xenograft model and CRC cell cultures, we evaluated artemether's effects on viability, migration, invasion, and histopathology. Inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β, IL-18, IL-1, caspase-1) were measured. Ferroptosis was assessed by flow cytometry, electron microscopy, and biochemical markers (GSH, MDA, ROS). Mechanistic studies included network pharmacology, molecular docking, SP600125 treatment, JNK1 siRNA knockdown, ferrostatin-1 rescue, western blotting, and qRT-PCR. Network pharmacology identified JNK1 as a core target of artemether in CRC. In vivo, artemether dose-dependently suppressed tumor growth, with efficacy comparable to that of oxaliplatin. In vitro, artemether inhibited CRC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion. Concurrently, artemether reduced multiple pro-inflammatory cytokines in serum and cell supernatants, indicating suppression of systemic and local inflammation. Mechanistically, artemether activated the JNK1/FOXO1/GPX4 pathway, leading to Fe²⁺ accumulation, a ROS burst, and lipid peroxidation, thereby inducing ferroptosis. These effects were reversed by the JNK inhibitor SP600125 and JNK1 knockdown. Furthermore, the ferroptosis inhibitor ferrostatin-1 significantly rescued artemether-induced cell death and lipid peroxidation, confirming ferroptosis as the primary mode of cell death. Artemether inhibits CRC and alleviates tumor-associated inflammation by inducing JNK1/FOXO1/GPX4-mediated ferroptosis, validated pharmacologically and genetically, highlighting its potential as an immunomodulatory anticancer agent.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is molecularly, cellularly and spatially heterogeneous, and current staging systems and biomarkers incompletely explain prognosis and treatment response. This study integrated transcriptomics, machine learning, single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics and in vitro experiments to prioritize candidate CRC-associated markers and characterize their potential biological and clinical relevance. GSE44861 and GSE44076 from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) and The Cancer Genome Atlas Colon Adenocarcinoma (TCGA-COAD) were used for differential expression, consensus differentially expressed gene (DEG) identification and functional enrichment analyses. Four machine-learning algorithms were applied for feature selection. Candidate genes were prioritized by differential expression, model importance and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) performance. GSE231559 single-cell data and spatial transcriptomics characterized the cellular source, pseudotime dynamics and spatial distribution of the core gene. TCGA-COAD assessed prognosis, pathways and computationally predicted drug sensitivity. Western blotting, Transwell and MTT assays were used for experimental validation, and public immunohistochemistry images from the Human Protein Atlas were used as supplementary protein-expression evidence. We identified 544 consensus DEGs enriched in leukocyte migration, chemotaxis, extracellular matrix organization, cytokine activity and metabolic pathways. Six genes were jointly selected: CLDN1, CDH3, KRT24, MMP7, NEBL and SCGN. CLDN1 was markedly upregulated and showed the highest tumour-versus-normal discrimination among the six candidates in the TCGA-COAD cohort. Single-cell and spatial analyses showed that CLDN1 was mainly expressed in CRC epithelial cells, displayed increasing expression across the inferred pseudotime ordering, and was enriched in malignant and mixed regions. In the TCGA-COAD cohort, high CLDN1 expression was associated with poorer overall survival and pathways involving the cell cycle, proteasome, autophagy, Hippo, ErbB and CRC. CLDN1 manipulation altered CRC-cell invasion and in vitro response to Nutlin-3a (-). These findings support CLDN1 as a candidate CRC-associated marker linked to malignant epithelial-cell states, tumour-associated spatial heterogeneity, invasive phenotype and Nutlin-3a (-) response. Further independent and prospective validation is required to determine its clinical diagnostic, prognostic and treatment-response relevance.

Three-dimensional (3D) modelling has demonstrated value in endoscopic training by creating models that improve recognition of colorectal polyp morphology. Building on our previously published research, we aimed to explore how a research-derived 3D printed colon model could function as an alternative visual communication tool to raise public awareness of colorectal cancer (CRC), screening, and interdisciplinary medical careers. A 3D colon model was modelled in ZBrush, and previously validated 3D digital polyp models were embedded within the colon lumen. The colon was segmented so that the model could be 3D printed in parts and connected with embedded magnets, allowing for the model to be broken down into parts to increase educational interactions. The model was 3D printed in thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) to permit flexibility. It was exhibited at the Museum of Liverpool during the British Science Festival 2025 as an interactive engagement artefact, and facilitated conversations around colorectal anatomy and polyp development, and cancer prevention and screening pathways. Its tactile and visual realism encouraged hands-on exploration and cross-generational engagement. We propose that the use of physical 3D printed colon and polyp models for clinical training can be used as powerful public health communication artefacts.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colonoscopy prevents colorectal cancer (CRC) but is invasive and resource intensive. Circulating microRNAs (miRNAs) may improve risk stratification of fecal immunochemical test (FIT)-positive individuals by identifying high-risk adenomas (HRAs). We evaluated the association of circulating miRNAs with HRAs and their contribution to risk prediction models (RPMs). We analyzed 398 FIT-positive participants from a Canadian screening cohort (160 HRAs; 238 controls). Plasma miRNAs were quantified using NanoString nCounter. Differential expression was assessed using two-tailed t-tests with Bonferroni correction, and LASSO regression identified predictive miRNAs. Five RPMs were developed (Baseline, Bonferroni, Bonferroni+Baseline, LASSO, LASSO+Baseline) and evaluated using AUCs, DeLong's test, calibration, bootstrap validation, and decision curve analysis. Eleven miRNAs were Bonferroni-significant, and LASSO retained 8 predictors. The Baseline model had an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.61, increasing to 0.80 with these miRNAs and 0.82 with baseline variables added; the LASSO+Baseline model achieved an AUC of 0.82 with good calibration. All miRNA-enhanced models outperformed Baseline (P<0.001) and showed greater net benefit on decision curve analysis. At a 20% threshold, the LASSO+Baseline model achieved 95.0% sensitivity and 56.7% PPV. Conclusions Circulating miRNAs substantially improved identification of HRAs among FIT-positive individuals with clinical utility. These data support further evaluation of miRNA-informed RPMs to refine CRC screening.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Bilobar colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) remain one of the most challenging scenarios in hepatobiliary surgery because complete oncologic resection often requires removal of extensive hepatic parenchyma while preserving an adequate future liver remnant (FLR). Over the past two decades, advances in systemic chemotherapy, minimally invasive liver surgery, liver-directed interventions, and multidisciplinary treatment planning have substantially expanded resectability, allowing an increasing number of patients previously considered unresectable to undergo curative-intent surgery. Contemporary management now focuses on selecting among complementary strategies that safely maximize resectability while preserving functional liver reserve. Within this evolving treatment algorithm, hepatic venous deprivation (HVD) hasemerged as an important strategy for FLR augmentation in appropriately selected patients requiring major hepatectomy.As functional assessment of the FLR continues to evolve beyond volumetric measurements alone, appropriate patient selection and individualized operative planning have become increasingly important. This case-based review describes the successful management of a 66-year-old woman with bilobar CRLM treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy, robotic first-stage parenchymal-sparing liver resection combined with synchronous sigmoid colectomy, HVD, and completion open extended right hepatectomy after adequate FLR hypertrophy. Using this case as a framework, we review the contemporary management of bilobar CRLM, current approaches to FLR augmentation, the rationale for selecting HVD over alternative strategies, evolving methods of functional liver assessment, and the role of minimally invasive staged hepatectomy within multidisciplinary oncological care.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Postoperative complications are drivers of healthcare costs following colon cancer surgery. We compared hospital costs between elective and emergency colon cancer resections according to complication severity. This retrospective cohort study included 520 patients undergoing colon cancer resection, of whom 431 underwent elective and 89 emergency surgery. Postoperative complications were graded according to the Clavien-Dindo classification. Hospital costs were analysed using a micro-costing approach. Adjusted costs were estimated using generalized linear models with gamma distribution and log link, adjusting for tumour stage, ASA classification, age and sex, with surgical technique in elective surgery. CD II-V occurred in 35% of elective and 56% of emergency patients. Emergency patients had higher ASA class, more advanced tumour stage and lower BMI (p < 0.05). Among patients with no or minor complications (CD 0-I), median costs were €9809 following elective surgery and €12,079 following emergency surgery. Among patients with complications, costs were higher in emergency versus elective surgery (€19,655 vs. €14,820; p = 0.004). Adjusted excess costs increased from CD 0-I to CD IV, whereas CD V did not follow this pattern. In adjusted analyses, complication severity remained associated with increased costs, with cost ratios of 3.21 in elective and 4.86 in emergency surgery for grade IV vs no or minor complications; however, the emergency estimate was based on six patients with CD IV complications and should be interpreted cautiously. Complication severity was independently associated with substantial cost increases after colon resection. Observed costs were generally higher and more variable following emergency surgery.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
This case report discusses the diagnosis and treatment of a 14-year-8-month-old male patient genetically diagnosed with Gardner syndrome (GS), systematically reviewing the disease's epidemiology, clinical manifestations, imaging advances, and management strategies. The patient presented with a post-influenza A chest wall mass and had prior resections of abdominal/scalp masses. Colonoscopy revealed > 20 adenomatous polyps. Imaging demonstrated multiple craniofacial osteomas and epidermoid cysts. Genetic testing identified a pathogenic APC gene mutation (NM_000038.6:c.4669_4670del (p.Ile1557*) heterozygous variant). GS, a familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP) subtype, has an estimated pediatric incidence of 1/8000-1/14,000. Its classic triad comprises colorectal polyps, osteomas, and soft tissue tumors. Recent studies indicate earlier malignant transformation of duodenal polyps in children versus adults, with desmoid tumor incidence reaching 10-20%. In imaging, low-dose CT, panoramic radiography, and contrast-enhanced MRI can improve early detection of bone lesions and soft tissue tumors. Genetic testing (APC/MUTYH) is the pediatric screening gold standard. Optimized chemoprevention (sulindac/celecoxib) and endoscopic monitoring have significantly improved prognoses. This case highlights the urgency of multidisciplinary management and genetic counseling for pediatric GS.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Conventional survival analyses cannot fully account for recurrence as an intermediate event that dynamically influences subsequent mortality. Multistate models (MSMs) enable explicit modeling of transitions between clinically relevant disease states; however, their application among patients undergoing resection for colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) remains limited. An international multi-institutional database was queried to identify patients undergoing curative-intent hepatectomy for CRLM between 1998 and 2023. A four-state MSM was constructed comprising alive and recurrence-free, alive with recurrence, colorectal cancer (CRC)-related death, and non-CRC-related death. Transition probabilities and transition-specific prognostic factors were evaluated RESULTS: Among 3002 patients, 1624 (54.1%) developed recurrence and 911 (56.1%) died, predominantly from CRC-related causes (92.8%). The probability of recurrence decreased substantially the longer patients remained recurrence-free after surgery, whereas recurrence markedly worsened subsequent prognosis. High tumor burden score was independently associated with transition to recurrence (hazard ratio [HR] 1.06 per unit; 95% confidence interval 1.03-1.08; p < 0.001) but not post-recurrence mortality, suggesting that the adverse prognostic impact of tumor burden was mediated primarily through recurrence. Adjuvant chemotherapy reduced recurrence (HR 0.76; p = 0.005) and CRC-related death from the recurrence-free state (HR 0.39; p = 0.002). MSMs provide a dynamic framework to characterize disease evolution after CRLM resection and represent recurrence as a clinically meaningful time-dependent intermediate state rather than a simple binary endpoint. Recurrence was the dominant determinant of long-term prognosis, supporting the role of MSMs for individualized prognostication and surveillance after hepatectomy for CRLM.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
This study conducted a retrospective disproportionality analysis of 50,031 adverse drug event (ADE) reports from the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) database spanning Q2 2009 to Q3 2025, in which golimumab was identified as the primary suspect drug. Four disproportionality algorithms were simultaneously applied: the reporting odds ratio (ROR), proportional reporting ratio (PRR), Bayesian confidence propagation neural network (BCPNN), and multi-item gamma Poisson shrinker (MGPS). A total of 397 positive signals were identified across 25 system organ classes (SOCs). The SOCs with concordant positive signals across all four algorithms were identified for infections and infestations and surgical and medical procedures. High-frequency signals included pneumonia, lower respiratory tract infection, influenza, nasopharyngitis, sinusitis and cellulitis. Comparison with the current prescribing information revealed several previously undocumented ADEs, including urinary tract infection, ear infection, flavivirus infection, Zika virus infection and Dengue fever. Twenty-nine positive malignancy signals absent from the prescribing information were identified, including basal cell carcinoma, colorectal cancer, cervical cancer and breast cancer. Time-to-onset analysis revealed that the risk of ADEs was the highest within the first few months of treatment initiation. Clinicians should rigorously monitor for infectious complications and malignancies when prescribing golimumab to ensure patient safety.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The long-term follow-up of workers with protracted exposure to low dose occupational ionizing radiation is important to understand the health effects and risks of radiation. This paper describes the creation and record linkage of the CANadian RADiation workers (CANRAD) cohort, including the work to resolve data issues and linkage challenges to outcome databases. The CANRAD cohort includes all workers with occupational exposure to ionizing radiation (1951-2018) in Canada's National Dose Registry (NDR) and three facility-based sub-cohorts: Eldorado uranium workers (1932-1980), Ontario uranium miners (1954-1996), and Atomic Energy of Canada Limited nuclear workers (1956-1985). The sub-cohorts were added to the NDR to update workers' employment histories and radiation exposures to 2018. Deterministic and probabilistic record linkage methods linked the CANRAD cohort to national population-based mortality (1950-2020), cancer incidence (1969-2019), and tax (1981-2020) data. Of 957,580 CANRAD workers, 883,150 (92.2%) successfully linked to Statistics Canada vital statistics databases. The analytical cohort includes 860,650 (89.9%) workers, including 427,920 (49.7%) females. At the end of follow-up, 751,520 (87.3%) of the cohort were alive and 94,410 (11.0%) were dead. Neoplasms and circulatory disease represented 63.8% (57,030) of all known causes of death (89,330). Prostate, breast, lung & bronchus, and colorectal cancer represented 49.9% (40,780) of first primary cancers (81,670). The mean cumulative effective dose was 17.1 mSv; but most cumulative doses were <10 mSv (∼85.0% of males and 98.1% of females). Females (350,510, 82.4%) dominated the medical sector. The CANRAD cohort is a large and valuable cohort of Canadian occupationally exposed radiation workers with employment histories, radiation exposures and long-term follow-up of tax, mortality, and cancer incidence. Analysis of this cohort will support the radiation protection framework.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) screening remains underused, in part because screening-related stressors can elicit fear, embarrassment, and other emotional barriers. Guided by the process model of emotion regulation, this study examined whether humor-based interventions engage cognitive reappraisal of CRC screening stressors and whether these reappraisal processes support screening intention. In a randomized experiment with 180 U.S. adults aged 45-75, participants received pre-crafted humor messages (PHM), completed self-generated humor tasks (SHT), or viewed an emotionally neutral control. Humorous and serious reappraisal were tested as parallel mediators, with health anxiety (HA) and cancer information overload (CIO) examined as moderators. Both PHM and SHT increased humorous reappraisal relative to control, and humorous reappraisal linked each intervention to stronger screening intention. Serious reappraisal did not mediate either intervention overall. Moderated mediation analyses showed that HA strengthened SHT's indirect effect through humorous reappraisal, whereas CIO strengthened SHT's indirect effect through serious reappraisal. The corresponding moderated pathways were not significant for PHM. These findings identify reappraisal as a pathway linking humor interventions with screening intention and suggest that self-generated humor may engage different reappraisal processes under heightened health-focused attention and information overload.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cancer survivors face an increased risk of second primary malignancies (SPMs). Understanding SPM incidence and risk factors is crucial for long-term survivorship care. This was a SEER-Medicare retrospective cohort study of breast, prostate, colon, or rectal cancer survivors diagnosed between 2003-2011 at age 66+ years who survived ≥5 years post-diagnosis. The primary outcome was a 'late' SPM, defined as invasive cancer occurring ≥5 years after initial diagnosis. Restricted mean survival time (RMST) regression was used to assess demographic, clinical, and treatment related factors associated with late SPMs. SPMs were categorized as hematologic, screen-detectable (breast, prostate, lung, colon, or rectal), or non-screen detectable solid tumors. Of 90,261 long-term survivors, 11.2% (10,116) developed at least one late SPM. The cumulative incidence of late SPMs over 8 years was highest in prostate cancer survivors. Non-screen detectable cancers composed the largest proportion (47.8%) of 10,220 total late SPMs. The most common late SPM site was lung in colon (14.9%), and rectal (16.1%) cancer survivors, urinary bladder in prostate (17.0%), and new-primary breast cancers in breast cancer survivors (36.5%). In RMST regression, significant associations with demographic, index cancer, treatment, and clinical characteristics and late SPMs ranged from 3.6 months shorter to 4.4 months longer time without late SPM during the 8 years assessed. Between 10-14% of older long-term cancer survivors developed a late SPM during 5-13 years after index cancer diagnosis. Over 40% of late SPMs were screen-detectable, highlighting the need for surveillance strategies beyond 5 years from index cancer diagnosis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most common cancer types affecting both men and women. MicroRNA-492 (miR-492) plays an important role in the development of various malignant tumors; however, its specific role and related mechanisms in CRC remain unclear. Therefore, we aimed to explore the relationship between miR-492 and the prognosis of patients with CRC, as well as the specific mechanisms involved in CRC development. The Gene Expression Omnibus and The Cancer Genome Atlas datasets were downloaded to analyze the relationship between the miR-492 expression level and the overall survival of patients with CRC. Forty-four pairs of primary CRC tissues and paired normal tissues were collected. The relationship between the miR-492 expression level and clinicopathological parameters of patients with CRC was analyzed using statistical methods. MiRNA quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) was used to detect miR-492 expression levels in CRC tissues and cell lines. 3-(4,5-Dimethylthiazol-2-yl)-2,5-diphenyl tetrazolium bromide and colony-formation assays were performed to assess cell growth and proliferation, respectively. Transwell assays were performed to analyze the migration and invasion potential of CRC cells. The interaction between miR-492 and 3' untranslated regions (3'-UTRs) of neuronal pentraxin 1 (NPTX1) was evaluated using a luciferase reporter assay. The expression of NPTX1 in CRC tissues and cells was detected by qRT-PCR. Low expression of miRNA-492 in CRC tissues is closely associated with patients' survival prognosis. miR-492 can recognize the 3'-UTR of NPTX1 mRNA and directly target and regulate NPTX1 expression, thereby promoting the growth, migration, and invasion of CRC cells. The ability of miR-492 to mediate the biological behavior of CRC by targeting NPTX1 is associated with poor prognosis and suggests that miR-492 is a potential therapeutic candidate for CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Complete mesocolic excision (CME) with central lymphadenectomy represents the oncologic standard for right colon cancer surgery. However, vascular anatomical variability particularly involving the superior mesenteric vessels and Henle's gastrocolic trunk may substantially increase operative complexity and hemorrhagic risk. This study aimed to evaluate mesenteric vascular variations systematically and to analyze their implications for the quality and safety of CME/D2 right hemicolectomy. A retrospective descriptive single-center study was conducted at a tertiary referral university hospital. A total of 250 consecutive patients who underwent oncologic right hemicolectomy for histologically confirmed adenocarcinoma of the right colon between January 2020 and January 2025 were included. Clinical, radiological, operative, pathological, and postoperative data were analyzed. Mesenteric vascular anatomy was evaluated using CT angiography (available in 51.2% of cases) and correlated with intraoperative observations. The study was reported according to the STROBE criteria. The mean patient age was 64.5 ± 11.2 years (range 28-89) with slight female predominance (55.2%). Complicated presentations (obstruction, perforation, hemorrhage) occurred in 31.2% of cases. CT angiography was available for 128/250 patients (51.2%); its incomplete use was primarily attributable to emergency/complicated presentations (41.0% of the 122 non-angiography cases), resource/protocol constraints (34.4%), and adequate standard CT for planning (24.6%). The ileocolic and middle colic arteries were invariably present. The right colic artery was absent in 35.2% of patients, with variable origins when present. Henle's trunk was identified in 59.2% of patients, with three distinct venous configurations characterized. Open surgery was performed in 67.2% of cases. No major intraoperative vascular injury was recorded. Adequate lymph node harvest (≥12 nodes) was achieved in all patients (mean 24.6 ± 6.8 nodes). Anastomotic leakage occurred in 2.4% and 30-day mortality in 0.8%. Mesenteric vascular variations are the rule rather than the exception during right colon cancer surgery. Preoperative CT angiography with vascular reconstruction appears to facilitate operative planning and anatomical orientation during CME/D2 lymphadenectomy. Standardized vascular-oriented dissection may improve oncologic quality while minimizing vascular complications.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Proteases are central to cancer pathobiology and attractive targets for noninvasive diagnosis. Diagnostic use of urinary proteases has developed along two methodologically distinct streams: measurement of protein abundance by immunoassay and increasingly by mass spectrometry, and direct measurement of enzymatic activity using peptide substrates. However, no common terminology unifies these approaches. This narrative review synthesizes evidence published between 2016 and 2026, concentrating on urine and, for the transferability of the methodology, on fecal water and serum. Saliva and seminal fluid are surveyed only to show that protease biomarkers there are measured by abundance alone. It adopts, from its existing use in nephrology, the term proteasuria as a unifying construct for the urinary protease diagnostic field, proposing a wider scope than the pathophysiological sense in which it was introduced. Two operational subtypes are defined: concentration-based and catalytic proteasuria. The distinction rests on the parameter measured rather than on the detection chemistry. Within the catalytic subtype single-enzyme detection using a selective substrate is distinguished from disease profiling using a multi-substrate panel. Evidence was identified by a PubMed search supplemented by citation and semantic search and screened by a single reviewer without protocol registration or formal risk-of-bias assessment. Concentration-based proteasuria is the clinically established stream, yet no urinary analyte has displaced cystoscopy, and approved assays remain insufficient as stand-alone rule-out or triage tests. The catalytic stream rests mainly on small single-center case-control studies reporting activity qualitatively; only one reports formal diagnostic performance, with a single elastase-specific substrate in 12 cases and 24 controls, and no head-to-head comparison with concentration-based assays has been published. Analytical validity is partial: substrate selectivity is established by combinatorial screening and confirmed with inhibitor and orthogonal controls, but precision, limits of quantification in urine and inter-laboratory reproducibility are not systematically reported, and no reference material or external quality-assessment scheme exists for this assay class. A largely independent exogenous stream of synthetic urinary biomarkers and activity-based nanosensors reports high accuracy, but all published diagnostic-accuracy data derive from animal models. On a translational-readiness scale the urinary catalytic stream is proof-of-concept, research-grade work, and any realistic target is therefore not cystoscopy but the margin at which established assays fail, principally low-grade noninvasive disease. The same reasoning identifies the detection of advanced adenoma, for which the fecal immunochemical test performs poorly, as the concrete benchmark for extending the framework to fecal protease profiling in colorectal cancer.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Available epidemiological evidence shows that many cancers share familial risks, and this is increasingly confirmed by data on shared pathogenic germline gene variants between cancers. We decided to harness the world's largest resource on familial cancer to assess discordant familial risks for female breast (BC), prostate (PC), colorectal (CRC), and lung (LC) cancers with any of 22 different cancers in first-degree relatives (proband cancers). Familial relative risk was calculated as standardized incidence ratio (SIR) when either one proband or 2 or more (2+) probands were found in a family to distinguish low- and high-risk associations. Discordant familial associations of BC were significant for 12 1-proband and 5 2+ proband cancers. For PC, the numbers were 11 and 4; for CRC, they were 8 and 4; and for LC, they were 15 and 5. The results with large case numbers showed that BC, CRC, and LC associated with each other, but the familial association between PC and LC was negative. Many known or novel associations with possible genetic causes were found, including lobular BC with stomach cancer, PC with kidney cancer, CRC with squamous cell skin and thyroid cancers, and LC with gallbladder and endocrine tumors, the most common of which were parathyroid adenomas. Also, LC associations with esophageal and cervical cancers were unlikely to be due to smoking alone and require additional explanations. In conclusion, 2/3 of discordant associations could suggest low-risk genetic and environmental causation and 1/3 high-risk genetic causation, both waiting for experimental proof.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Dialysis patients face a heightened risk of cancer, particularly kidney cancer. The global aging of dialysis patients suggests that managing cancer may become a critical factor in future healthcare. Given that the chronic uremic state is a cancer risk factor, dialysis patients may face an elevated risk for all cancers. However, the epidemiology of nonkidney cancers, such as colorectal cancer, remains to be fully elucidated. This was a retrospective cohort study targeting 74 dialysis facilities in Okinawa Prefecture, Japan. The subjects were patients who received dialysis for a minimum of 90 days between 2015 and 2019 and were diagnosed with cancer after initiating dialysis during this period. The cancer incidence ratio for the study population (21 655 person-years) was then compared with that of the general Okinawan population using standardized incidence ratios. A total of 404 cancer cases were collected from 56 facilities (76%). The standardized incidence ratios for all cancers was 1.36, with the risk of kidney cancer increasing with longer dialysis vintage. Patients with a dialysis vintage of less than 2 years showed an increased risk of colorectal and lung cancer. The risk of breast cancer was similar to that of the general population. The present study revealed that not all cancer risks were increased among patients receiving haemodialysis. Screening for colorectal and lung cancer in the first 2 years after commencement of dialysis may be important. Further research is needed to determine the efficacy of this approach for patients receiving dialysis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cancer is the leading cause of mortality worldwide. It encompasses a spectrum of malignancies that include lung, stomach, colon, prostate, liver, and skin cancers depending on the organ it affects. Epidemiological evidence indicates that regular consumption of cruciferous vegetables leads to a 10-20% reduction in the risk of lung, breast, and colorectal cancers and bioactive dietary constituents. The lipophilic character of phytochemicals facilitates membrane permeability and selective target engagement, underscoring their pharmacological relevance. Daily dietary intake introduces varying amounts of bioactive constituents that can act as preventive agents, thereby improving human health. In this review, we discuss the therapeutic potential of selected dietary natural products, focusing on cinnamaldehyde, eugenol, β-glucan, gingerol, shogaol, curcumin, and epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG). Strong scientific literature studies support the role of these compounds in targeting key molecular pathways, including the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway, caspase-3 activation, and Signal Transducer and Activator of Transcription (STAT) signaling. Bioavailability, dosing, and safety profiles remain challenges, particularly in ensuring that these factors do not hinder therapeutic efficacy. Analyzing the pharmacophoric features and discussing their potential for structural optimization leads to the development of clinical candidates in the market. Combination therapy of plant-derived bioactive compounds with anticancer drugs has improved patient outcomes in many studies, leading to the development of natural product-assisted therapeutics in the future.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Surgical strategies for colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) have progressively evolved toward parenchyma-sparing approaches, increasing the relevance of understanding the relationship between tumor biology and resection margin patterns. In parallel, KRAS and BRAF mutations have emerged as key determinants of tumor behavior in CRLM. The interaction between mutational status and surgical margin type, however, remains insufficiently characterized. This multicenter retrospective study included patients undergoing curative-intent liver resection for CRLM between 2016 and 2021 across 17 international HPB centers. Clinicopathological variables were compared according to mutational status and margin type. Among 1078 eligible patients, KRAS-mutated patients more frequently presented synchronous metastases, nodal involvement, and administration of perioperative chemotherapy compared with wild-type patients. Higher tumor burden was associated with both R1 parenchymal (R1P) and R1 vascular (R1V) resections. Within KRAS-mutated patients, synchronous disease and bilobar involvement were more frequently associated with R1P resections. KRAS/BRAF mutational status is associated with distinct clinicopathological patterns in patients undergoing liver resection for CRLM. Higher tumor burden and biologically aggressive disease features are more frequently associated with R1P and R1V resections, particularly among KRAS-mutated tumors.

Spatial heterogeneity in the colorectal cancer (CRC) tumor microenvironment (TME) is closely related to stromal organization and may influence treatment-related features. In this study, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomic data from CRC tissues to examine cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF)-dominant spatial domains. GPC1 and CHPF were enriched in stromal regions and showed higher expression in CRC tissues than in normal tissues. In the analyzed cohorts, higher GPC1 and CHPF expression was associated with advanced clinicopathological features and poorer survival outcomes in univariate analyses. Single-cell analyses showed that GPC1 and CHPF were mainly expressed in fibroblasts and were enriched in an ADAM12-associated fibroblast subset with myofibroblast-like features, extracellular matrix-related genes, and hypoxia/glycolysis-related signatures. Cell-cell communication analysis suggested that this fibroblast subset was linked to higher inferred WNT signaling. Drug-response and immunotherapy-related analyses further showed that GPC1 and CHPF expression was associated with transcriptomic patterns related to treatment response. In mucinous adenocarcinoma (MA), the ADAM12-associated fibroblast program showed stronger inferred MIF-related signaling and was associated with macrophage M2-like features. Spatial mapping and multiplex immunofluorescence supported partial colocalization of GPC1, CHPF, and ADAM12 in CAF-rich stromal regions. In CAFs, GPC1 or CHPF knockdown reduced ADAM12, CAF activation markers, and WNT/MIF-related proteins, while ADAM12 knockdown weakened macrophage M2-like marker expression in a co-culture model. These findings suggest that GPC1 and CHPF mark an ADAM12-associated CAF program linked to stromal remodeling and immune-related features in CRC, especially in MA, but further studies are needed to define its functional role.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Adequate distal margin (DM) achievement is essential in oncological rectal cancer surgery. In conventional transabdominal surgery, however, the intraluminal location of the distal tumor edge must be translated to an externally applied transection line; this potentially causes discrepancies between intended and achieved margins. This study aimed to evaluate the discrepancy between the planned intraoperative DM and the margin achieved in rectal cancer resection, identify factors associated with DM discrepancy, and evaluate the association between the transanal approach, specifically transanal total mesorectal excision, and DM accuracy. This retrospective cohort study included 171 consecutive patients who underwent curative-intent laparoscopic or robot-assisted low anterior resection (LAR) or intersphincteric resection between July 2019 and June 2025. The intended DM in operative records was compared with the pathological DM measured in formalin-fixed specimens. The primary outcome was the absolute DM discrepancy. As the distribution was skewed, adjusted median regression was performed using the transanal approach, intended DM, tumor distance from the anal verge, maximum tumor size, surgical platform, and surgical era as covariates. The median absolute DM discrepancy was 4.0 mm and was smaller with than without the transanal approach (3.0 vs. 6.0 mm; p < 0.001). After adjustment, transanal approach omission was associated with greater absolute DM discrepancy (β, 3.938 mm; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.848-6.027; p < 0.001). Greater maximum tumor size was also associated with greater discrepancy (β per 1-mm increase, 0.075 mm; 95% CI 0.040-0.110; p < 0.001). This association remained consistent in sensitivity analyses restricted to LAR and after exclusion of scar-based pathological DM measurements. The transanal approach was associated with a smaller discrepancy between intended and achieved DMs after adjustment for tumor characteristics, surgical platform, and surgical era. Assessing the distal tumor edge and intended transection line within the same transanal operative field may facilitate more precise DM control.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Robotic and endoscopic techniques continue to revolutionize minimally invasive surgery. Single-port (SP) robotic platforms mark a new era in minimally invasive colorectal surgery, combining single-incision/site access with full robotic articulation through a single access point. This manuscript, as a part of a four-part series, outlines specific technical considerations of the SP robotic platform including details of the platform, instrumentation, docking, and operative maneuvers. Subject matter experts from the SAGES Colorectal Committee SP Task Force performed a structured review of the currently FDA-approved SP robotic platform, assessing technical features, instrumentation, and workflow considerations for several key representative operations relevant to colorectal surgery. Three clinical areas of SP implementation included transanal robotic surgery, right colectomy, and low anterior resection (LAR). Task Force members (subject matter experts with early experience in SP robotic platforms) analyzed technical details, patient selection, and operative workflows. Representative procedural techniques were detailed with emphasis on instrumentation choice, docking strategies, and key operative steps specific to single-port colorectal surgery. The technical aspects of the SP platform include full robotic articulation through a single 25 mm port. A SP approach also enables triangulation and dexterity within confined spaces using three wristed instruments and a flexible 3-D camera. The current 360-degree boom rotation facilitates multi-quadrant manipulation without redocking. Current limitations may include continued reliance on bedside assistance for certain energy and stapling operative steps, although stapling capability has expanded with FDA clearance of an SP-compatible 45 mm stapler as of April 2025. Training of the entire operative team and gradual progression of case complexity is recommended as the surgeon implements this new technology into clinical practice. A SP robotic approach to minimally invasive colorectal surgical procedures is feasible for a range of colorectal surgery operations. In select procedures like SP TAMIS, SP right colectomy, and SP-LAR, the single-port platform appears to offer advantages related to reduced invasiveness and improved surgeon ergonomics compared to other minimally invasive approaches. Successful implementation requires structured training, careful patient selection, and adherence to evidence-based adoption principles.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cancer cachexia is a wasting syndrome with outsized impact on morbidity and mortality, yet its drivers and systemic consequences remain poorly defined. In this study, we repurposed longitudinal clinicogenomic data from 52,236 patients with cancer profiled by MSK-IMPACT (2010-2024) at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center to define episode-resolved trajectories of consensus-defined cachectic weight loss and linked these events to outcomes, serology and tumor genotypes. Cachectic episodes clustered near periods of disease progression and were associated with inferior outcomes in nearly all cancer types. Across diverse malignancies, cachectic weight loss episodes exhibited a consistent serologic signature characterized by lower albumin and hemoglobin and higher levels of liver enzymes. Numerous somatic tumor genotypes, including TP53 mutation across several diseases, were also associated with more frequent onset of cachectic episodes. Motivated by these observations, we developed a multivariate model to predict impending risk of cachectic weight loss in patients with lung, colorectal and prostate cancer, validated in an independent, external cohort from Dana-Farber Cancer Institute (n = 5,785). Routine clinicogenomic data are, therefore, a scalable resource for discovery in cancer cachexia.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
T cell immunoreceptor with Ig and ITIM domains (TIGIT) is a key inhibitory receptor on cytotoxic lymphocytes, yet the mechanisms governing its context-dependent upregulation in tumors remain poorly defined. Here, we identify tumor necrosis factor-α (TNFα) signaling as an upstream driver of TIGIT expression. Integrated analyses of patient transcriptomic datasets revealed a consistent positive association between TNFα pathway activity and TIGIT expression across multiple cancer types, with strong concordance in melanoma and prognostic relevance in kidney renal clear cell carcinoma. Mechanistically, TNFα directly induced TIGIT expression in natural killer cells via TNFR2 signaling, increasing chromatin accessibility at distal TIGIT enhancers and promoting NF-κB and AP-1 recruitment together with BRD4 and P300. Functionally, combined anti-TNFα and anti-TIGIT treatment suppressed tumor growth and prolonged survival more effectively than either monotherapy in murine melanoma and colon cancer models. These findings define a TNFα-TNFR2-enhancer axis controlling TIGIT expression and provide a mechanistic rationale for dual TNFα and TIGIT targeting in inflamed tumors.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To explore older adults’ experiences of adapting to physical, emotional and cognitive changes during the first month after colorectal cancer surgery. A qualitative descriptive study with an inductive approach was conducted in the Stockholm region, Sweden. Thirteen adults aged ≥60 years who had undergone planned colorectal cancer surgery participated in semi-structured interviews 1-month postoperatively. Data were analysed using thematic analysis following Braun and Clarke’s guidelines. Participants described recovery as a gradual and multifaceted process shaped by changes in their physical, cognitive and emotional capacities. Everyday activities required deliberate planning, pacing and continuous adjustment to fluctuating energy and function. These adaptations took place within a relational context, where support from family and healthcare professionals was experienced as both enabling and demanding. A heightened awareness of mortality emerged following the cancer diagnosis and remained present in daily life, influencing how participants prioritised and engaged in activities. Over time, participants navigated uncertainty through efforts to balance management and acceptance while striving to maintain autonomy and involvement in daily life. Recovery after colorectal cancer surgery in older adults is a dynamic and multidimensional process shaped by altered bodily capacity and awareness of mortality. Rehabilitation should extend beyond physical function to support everyday adaptation, autonomy and patients’ capacity to navigate uncertainty during the postoperative period. NCT05564195.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Immunotherapy for colorectal cancer (CRC) remains limited due to the inherently low tumor immunogenicity and the profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Herein, capitalizing on the metabolic traits and anatomical accessibility of CRC, we propose a broadly applicable oral strategy based on metabolically engineered bacteria (EcN-HlpA-CGL [EHC]) for CRC immunotherapy. Mechanistically, cystathionine γ-lyase expressed by EHC disrupts redox homeostasis, triggering ferroptosis in CRC cells and thereby enhancing tumor immunogenicity. Concurrently, the intrinsic adjuvant activity of the bacteria amplifies the cancer-immunity cycle driven by immunogenic cell death and remodels the immunosuppressive TME. In vivo studies demonstrate that this orally delivered engineered bacterial platform not only suppresses the growth of orthotopic CRC tumors but also inhibits metastatic progression, indicating the induction of a potent systemic immune response. Immune profiling confirms robust systemic and gut mucosal immune activation following oral administration. Collectively, this oral metabolically engineered bacterial platform is precisely tailored to the features of CRC and offers a safe and effective immunotherapeutic strategy for this malignancy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cancer stem cells (CSCs) play a central role in colon cancer progression and are major contributors to metastasis, recurrence, and therapeutic resistance. CPEB1 (Cytoplasmic Polyadenylation Element Binding Protein 1) is a tumor suppressor, but its role in CSC-associated signaling during colon cancer progression remains insufficiently understood. The potential modulation of CPEB1 by Icaritin, a prenylated flavonoid, particularly in a stage-dependent context, has not been comprehensively investigated. To investigate the effect of Icaritin on CPEB1 expression, CSC-associated markers, apoptosis, inflammatory cytokines, and stemness-related signaling pathways during the early- and late-stage of colon cancer progression using an in vivo AOM/DSS-induced colon cancer model. In our study, colon cancer was induced in BALB/c mice using azoxymethane (AOM) and dextran sulfate sodium (DSS) administered in cycles (three cycles to model early-stage disease; six cycles to model advanced-stage disease). Tumor stage was confirmed by histopathological analysis, while western blotting was performed for CPEB1, CSC markers (CD133, ALDH1A1, Nanog, Sox2, CD44), apoptosis markers (Bcl-2, caspase-3, Bax), and key signaling pathway proteins (β-catenin, c-Myc, Notch1, Hes1). Serum cytokines IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-10 were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Ki-67 immunohistochemical staining was performed to evaluate tumor proliferative activity. Advanced-stage tumors exhibited significantly lower baseline CPEB1 expression and significantly higher CSC marker expression compared with early-stage tumors. Treatment with Icaritin was associated with a marked increase in CPEB1 expression in advanced-stage tumors, accompanied by a greater reduction in CSC marker expression and more pronounced reductions in the expression of β-catenin, c-Myc, Notch1, and Hes1. Apoptotic activation was more pronounced in advanced-stage models (as indicated by increased cleaved caspase-3 and Bax expression and decreased Bcl-2 levels). Cytokine modulation was also more substantial in advanced-stage disease, where IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-1β were markedly reduced, and IL-10 was significantly increased. Furthermore, Ki-67-positive proliferative activity was significantly elevated in advanced-stage tumors and was markedly reduced following Icaritin treatment. Icaritin exhibits enhanced anti-inflammatory, pro-apoptotic, and CSC-associated molecular modulatory effects in advanced-stage colon cancer and is associated with upregulated CPEB1 expression and greater suppression of CSC-associated markers and reduced expression of proteins associated with stemness-related signaling pathways compared with early-stage disease. The observed association between increased CPEB1 expression and suppression of CSC-associated signaling pathways suggests a potential role of CPEB1 restoration in Icaritin-mediated antitumor responses; however, direct CPEB1-dependent regulatory mechanisms remain to be established. The observed reductions in CSC-associated markers represent molecular changes and do not establish direct inhibition of CSC self-renewal or functional activity. Further mechanistic and functional CSC studies are warranted to clarify the direct regulatory relationship between CPEB1 restoration and the antitumor effects of Icaritin in colorectal cancer progression.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Accurate preoperative prediction of lymph node metastasis (LNM) in colorectal cancer remains challenging using conventional CT assessment. This proof-of-concept study compared CT-based multi-station lymph-node radiomics with primary-tumor radiomics for patient-level preoperative prediction of LNM. This single-center retrospective study included patients with pathologically confirmed colorectal cancer who underwent preoperative contrast-enhanced CT and surgical resection. Patients were divided into training and validation cohorts. Radiomics features were extracted from the primary tumor and visible regional lymph nodes across multiple nodal stations. Three radiomics strategies were developed and compared: primary-tumor radiomics, multi-station lymph-node radiomics, and combined radiomics. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration analysis, decision curve analysis, and five-fold cross-validation. Pairwise AUCs were compared using the DeLong test. A clinical-radiomic model was further constructed by integrating the optimal radiomics strategy with preoperative clinical variables. In the validation cohort, the multi-station lymph-node radiomics model outperformed the primary-tumor radiomics model for predicting LNM (AUC, 0.864 versus 0.637; p = 0.0055). The combined radiomics model achieved an AUC of 0.840, without significant improvement over the lymph-node model (p = 0.2211). After integration with clinical variables, the clinical-radiomic model achieved an AUC of 0.879. CT-based multi-station lymph-node radiomics showed significantly higher validation performance than primary-tumor radiomics for patient-level preoperative LNM prediction in colorectal cancer. However, this single-center proof-of-concept model is not ready for direct clinical implementation and requires multicenter external validation before clinical translation. Question Can CT-based multi-station lymph-node radiomics improve preoperative nodal metastasis prediction beyond primary-tumor radiomics in patients with surgically treated colorectal cancer? Findings Multi-station lymph-node radiomics achieved higher validation performance than primary-tumor radiomics for patient-level prediction of pathological lymph-node metastasis in colorectal cancer. Relevance statement CT-based multi-station lymph-node radiomics may support individualized preoperative nodal risk stratification in colorectal cancer, but multicenter validation and prospective evaluation are required before clinical translation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
While current colorectal cancer (CRC) screening guidelines consider family history to determine starting age for screening, they inadequately incorporate other important unmodifiable risk factors, including polygenic risk score (PRS) and biological sex. In 353,118 average-risk UK Biobank participants, we used family history-stratified Cox models to estimate associations of sex and PRS with CRC incidence, metastasis, and CRC-specific mortality. We translated risk differences into risk-adapted initiation screening ages using both risk advancement period (RAP) and absolute 10-year cumulative risk. Men had a higher risk of CRC compared to women, with HRs of 1.41 (95% CI, 1.33-1.50) for those without family history and 1.42 (95% CI, 1.26-1.61) for those with family history. For each one-standard deviation (SD) increase in PRS, the risk was 1.49 times higher (95% CI, 1.45-1.53) in participants without a family history and 1.42 times higher (95% CI, 1.34-1.51) in those with a family history. The increase in PRS was associated with elevated risks of both metastatic CRC at diagnosis and CRC-specific mortality, indicating delayed diagnosis in high-PRS individuals and highlighting the potential benefit of earlier screening. Consequently, risk-adapted initiation ages ranged from before 40 years for men with a family history in the high-PRS group to after 60 years for women without a family history in the low-PRS group. Our findings demonstrate that the integration of PRS, biological sex, and family history identifies substantial heterogeneity in CRC risk and risk-adapted screening initiation ages.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The resistance of colorectal cancer (CRC) to PD-1 blockade has positioned it as a critical focus of global research efforts. The gut microbiota is a key regulator of anti-tumor immunity, but research on bacteria that are clearly associated with primary resistance to PD-1 blockade in colorectal cancer remains incomplete. In this study, C57BL/6 mice were subjected to antibiotic pretreatment to deplete endogenous gut microbiota. The mice were then gavaged with fecal suspensions from treatment-naïve CRC patients or healthy donors, subsequently implanted with MC38 tumor cells to establish the tumor model, and then treated with the drug. Gut microbial composition was analyzed by 16S rRNA sequencing, while tumor-infiltrating immune cells and cytokine profiles were characterized using flow cytometry and immunohistochemistry, respectively. CRC patient microbiota conferred resistance to anti-PD-1 therapy in mice, an effect completely reversed by oral Akkermansia muciniphila (Akk). Mechanistically, Akk reconfigured the tumor immune microenvironment, leading to a substantial increase in CD8+ T cell infiltration and function. Crucially, this potent local anti-tumor immunity was achieved without systemic immune activation. In summary, this study establishes that Akk amplifies the local CD8⁺ T cell response, sensitizing tumors to anti-PD-1 therapy, without inducing a systemic inflammatory response. These findings position Akk supplementation as a promising, targeted strategy to overcome PD-1 immunotherapy resistance of MSS-CRC with a favorable safety profile.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The incidence of early-onset colorectal cancer continues to increase among adults younger than 50 years, yet delays in diagnosis remain common. As an initial step of the Early-Onset Colorectal Cancer Awareness campaign, we evaluated U.S. healthcare providers' knowledge, attitudes, diagnostic practices, and perceived barriers related to the timely recognition and evaluation of early-onset colorectal cancer. This survey established baseline measures for a national early-onset colorectal cancer awareness campaign. We conducted a national cross-sectional survey of physicians, nurse practitioners, and physician assistants practicing family medicine, internal medicine, emergency medicine/urgent care, and obstetrics and gynecology. The survey assessed early-onset colorectal cancer awareness, screening recommendations, evaluation of symptomatic younger adults, perceived barriers to diagnosis, and educational needs. Descriptive statistics summarized responses, and multivariable regression identified factors associated with guideline-concordant screening and diagnostic evaluation. A total of 277 providers completed the survey. Although 87% were concerned or very concerned about early-onset colorectal cancer and 82% reported increased concern over the preceding five years, providers identified substantial barriers to timely diagnosis. Approximately one-half reported that younger adults commonly experienced symptoms for four months or longer before seeking care. The most frequently cited barriers included patients expecting symptoms to resolve (84%), insurance and financial barriers (79%), reluctance to undergo colonoscopy (77%), and failure to recognize symptoms as serious (65%). Most providers (79%) identified additional guidance on early-onset colorectal cancer symptoms, risk factors, and diagnostic evaluation as the educational resource most likely to improve care. Despite widespread awareness of the increasing incidence of early-onset colorectal cancer, patient- and system-level barriers continue to delay diagnosis in younger adults. These findings identify opportunities for targeted education, clinical decision support, and health system interventions to promote timely evaluation of symptomatic patients and improve early detection of early-onset colorectal cancer. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
A 63-year-old male with a history of untreated HIV presented to the emergency room with acute on chronic watery diarrhea, weight loss, fatigue, fever and chills. His vital signs were within normal limits and his abdomen was soft, nondistended and tender to palpation in 4 quadrants without peritonitis. He did not have leukocytosis on presentation. CD4 count was 310. CT scan showed inflammatory changes in the rectum and sigmoid colon. Comprehensive infectious workup was negative for any pathogens including cytomegalovirus (CMV), cryptosporidium, chlamydia, gonorrhea, C. difficile, cryptococcus, tuberculosis (TB) and herpes simplex virus (HSV). Colonoscopy was performed and showed a continuous area of nonbleeding ulcerated mucosa in the rectum, sigmoid, descending and transverse colon (Fig. 1). Pancolonic biopsies revealed active colitis with focal areas of basal plasmacytosis and crypt branching in left colon, suggestive of acute on chronic colitis and possible ulcerative colitis (UC). Gastroenterology and infectious disease were consulted and patient was started on IV methylprednisolone for presumed UC flare. Over the next few weeks, the patient proceeded to develop melena as well as increased lower abdominal and pelvic pain with intermittent fevers despite IV steroid treatment. The patient was trialed on IV infliximab also without significant improvement. After several weeks of steroid and biologic treatment, he developed increased abdominal pain with tachycardia and hemodynamic instability. His examination was significant for peritonitis with abdominal distension concerning for fulminant colitis. Colorectal surgery was consulted and proceeded to do an emergent total abdominal colectomy and end ileostomy. Intraoperatively he was found to have a small anterior distal rectal perforation. The decision was made to drain this area widely with rectal drain and fecal diversion and start him on IV antibiotic therapy. His final pathology from the index operation showed ulceration and acute colitis. There was no chronic crypt architectural distortion such as crypt dropout, disarray, crypt branching or basal plasmacytosis that are often seen in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). There was also increased apoptotic bodies and mitoses that were not consistent with IBD. After reviewing the clinical presentation, his disease progression, and final pathology, the treating team diagnosed the patient with HIV-associated colitis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) represents a major global healthcare burden. Tumor differentiation grade is a critical prognostic factor for evaluating patients with CRC. The objective of this study was to examine the value of dual-energy computed tomography (DECT) quantitative parameters as imaging biomarkers for the preoperative prediction of histopathologic CRC grade. A total of 117 patients with pathologically confirmed CRC who underwent preoperative contrast-enhanced DECT were enrolled and divided into low-grade (n=74) and high-grade (n=43) groups. Monoenergetic 74-keV images from the arterial phase (AP), venous phase (VP), and delayed phase (DP) were reconstructed as conventional 120 kVp-like computed tomography (CT) images. Lesion CT attenuation values, iodine concentration (IC), normalized iodine concentration (NIC), effective atomic number (Zeff), and extracellular volume (ECV) were measured in three phases by two radiologists, and clinical data were collected. Intergroup comparisons and Spearman correlation analyses were conducted to determine the associations between spectral parameters and the histopathologic grade of CRC, and multivariable logistic regression analyses were applied to identify independent correlates. Three types of predictive models were established: a baseline model incorporating clinical variables and CT attenuation values, a single spectral parameter model, and combined models integrating clinical features with different spectral parameters. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and the DeLong test were used to compare the area under the curve (AUC) between the models. Bootstrap internal validation with 1,000 resamples was performed on the optimal model. Serum carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) concentration showed significant differences between the low-grade group and high-grade group (P=0.009), whereas triphasic 120 kVp-like CT attenuation values showed no statistical differences (P>0.05). For the AP, only IC differed significantly (P=0.011); for the VP and DP, IC, NIC, Zeff, and ECV differed significantly (P<0.05), with ECV showing the strongest correlation with histopathologic grade in CRC (r=0.650: P<0.001). Multivariable analysis identified VP IC [odds ratio (OR) =4.601; P=0.046] and ECV (OR =1.492; P<0.001) as independent correlates of high histopathologic grade in CRC, with AUCs of 0.749 and 0.889, respectively. The integrated model combining clinical indicators with VP and DP spectral parameters achieved the best performance for predicting high histopathologic grade in CRC [AUC =0.904, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.845-0.962; bias‑corrected AUC =0.904, 95% CI: 0.837-0.954], with an accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity of 85.5%, 88.4%, and 83.8%, respectively. The DeLong test revealed that this integrated model had significantly better diagnostic performance than did the baseline model (AUC =0.538; P<0.001), whereas no statistically significant difference was observed between the integrated model and the VP + DP dual-phase model (P=0.504). DECT quantitative parameters have potential clinical value for predicting the histopathologic grade of patients with CRC. They may serve as imaging biomarkers and provide valuable information for understanding tumor biological behavior.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Pretreatment prediction of neoadjuvant response remains an unresolved challenge in locally advanced rectal cancer, where management is moving towards risk-adapted and response-oriented treatment strategies. Prediction remains difficult because response reflects interacting tumour-intrinsic, immune, stromal, and spatial processes that are incompletely captured by standard clinical and radiological assessment. From a technology-centred perspective, in this Review we assess how molecular, spatial, image-based, and artificial intelligence-enabled approaches are being used to study and predict response to neoadjuvant treatment from pretreatment biopsies and how readily they may be translated into clinical workflows. Genomic profiling has its clearest current clinical role in identifying hypermutated immune-responsive subgroups, whereas broader genomic, epigenomic, and immune-repertoire markers remain largely investigational. Bulk transcriptomics has generated multiple response signatures with variable reproducibility but has consistently highlighted immune activation, interferon signalling, stromal remodelling, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition as recurrent response-associated programmes; its most feasible clinical route is likely through targeted expression panels rather than open-ended transcriptome profiling. Higher-resolution approaches such as spatial transcriptomic and proteomic platforms refine these observations by localising signals to tumour, immune, and stromal compartments and capturing therapy-induced tissue reorganisation, but they are currently best positioned for deepening biological understanding and nominating rational treatment combinations for future testing. Established platforms such as digital pathology are closer to routine deployment as they build on clinically embedded workflows, although response-prediction algorithms still require robust external validation, calibration, and regulatory-grade implementation. Patient-derived models provide functional systems for testing candidate biomarkers and resistance mechanisms. Multimodal artificial intelligence may support response prediction by identifying complementary signals across data types and distilling complex signatures into parsimonious models suitable for clinical translation. Progress will depend on harmonised, longitudinal, multi-centre studies that couple biological depth with assay standardisation, model reduction, and prospective evidence that response predictors improve patient management. © 2026 The Author(s). ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Metastasis is the primary cause of mortality in colorectal cancer (CRC), a leading global malignancy. Although metabolic reprogramming is a hallmark of cancer, the stage-associated transcriptional features of metabolic pathways during CRC progression remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to characterize transcriptionally inferred metabolic heterogeneity during CRC progression and identify candidate molecular factors associated with metastasis. We performed an integrated transcriptomic analysis using TCGA and GEO datasets and compared metabolic pathway signatures across normal tissues, primary tumors, and metastatic lesions. An exploratory tumor lactate metabolism score (TLMS) was developed using Cox regression and LASSO analysis. Consensus clustering identified metabolic subtypes, and their associations with computationally estimated immune-cell signatures were assessed. The functional consequences of ENO3 loss were preliminarily evaluated using CRISPR/Cas9 knockout, cell proliferation assays, and an NSG tail-vein experimental lung colonization model. We observed a stage-associated reversal-like transcriptional pattern: primary tumors showed broad suppression of metabolic pathway signatures relative to normal tissues, whereas metastatic lesions showed reactivation of several signatures, including the pentose phosphate pathway. A six-gene lactate metabolism-related signature stratified patients into prognostic groups within the TCGA cohort. The high-risk group showed higher ssGSEA-inferred neutrophil abundance and enrichment of a neutrophil extracellular trap (NET)-associated transcriptional signature. ENO3 expression was associated with poor outcome, while ENO3 knockout reduced MC38 cell proliferation and experimental lung colonization in NSG mice. CRC progression is accompanied by stage-associated changes in transcriptomically inferred metabolic programs. TLMS and ENO3 represent exploratory candidate biomarkers that require independent clinical validation and further mechanistic investigation, particularly with respect to lactate metabolism and the tumor immune microenvironment.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Robotic colorectal surgery is increasingly used for technically demanding pelvic procedures, but contemporary cancer-specific experience from Latin American public oncology centers remains limited. To describe perioperative and pathological outcomes of a robotic colorectal cancer program at a national oncology referral center in Mexico. We retrospectively analyzed 75 consecutive patients who underwent robotic surgery for colorectal malignancy at the Instituto Nacional de Cancerología between June 2024 and March 2026. Colon and rectal cancer were analyzed as separate descriptive cohorts. Major morbidity was defined as Clavien-Dindo grade III or higher within 30 days. Fifty-seven patients (76.0%) had rectal cancer and 18 (24.0%) had colon cancer. No conversion to open surgery occurred (0/75; exact 95% CI 0-4.8%). Median operative time was 290 min (IQR 220-345), estimated blood loss 50 mL (IQR 30-100), and hospital stay 4 days (IQR 3-6). Major morbidity occurred in 13/75 patients (17.3%), reintervention in 12/75 (16.0%), and 30-day readmission in 12/75 (16.0%). Among rectal patients, 54/57 (94.7%) received total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) and 11/54 (20.4%) achieved pathological complete response. The circumferential resection margin was < 1 mm in 8/57 (14.0%). Mesorectal quality was complete in 41/57 (71.9%), nearly complete in 7/57 (12.3%), and incomplete in 9/57 (15.8%). Median lymph-node yield was 9 (IQR 6-12) for rectal cancer and 25.5 (IQR 16.25-32.25) for colon cancer. This series describes robotic colorectal cancer surgery within an established national oncology service, with a case mix dominated by low rectal procedures. The findings provide contemporary perioperative and pathological quality data for continued institutional audit; comparative studies and longer follow-up are required before conclusions regarding relative effectiveness can be made.

This study aimed to quantify how rapidly robot-assisted colon resection billing diffused after reimbursement in Japan and whether geographic variation narrowed as uptake expanded. We analyzed National Database (NDB) Open Data for fiscal years (FYs) 2022-2024. The primary outcome was the robot-assisted share of two laparoscopic billing categories for malignant colon tumor resection (robot-assisted and conventional). Variation across treating-institution prefectures was summarized using the interquartile range (IQR) for absolute spread and the coefficient of variation (CV) and Gini coefficient for relative dispersion. Longitudinal analyses included prefectures with unmasked values in all relevant years; FY2024 permitted a complete 47-prefecture cross-section. In the common 33-prefecture panel, the IQR widened from 5.73 to 6.61 and 11.79 percentage points, whereas the CV fell from 1.086 to 0.630 and 0.482 and the Gini coefficient from 0.565 to 0.347 and 0.269. Across all 47 prefectures in FY2024, shares ranged from 0.00% to 41.47%; the complete cross-section was more heterogeneous than the restricted longitudinal panel, and the 14 prefectures excluded because of earlier masking had a lower median share (6.83% versus 18.05%). Rapid national growth did not translate into geographically uniform billing-based uptake. Relative dispersion decreased while absolute percentage-point spread widened, so apparent geographic convergence depended on the scale used. Post-reimbursement surveillance should report both dimensions and account for selection introduced by disclosure-related masking.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Reduced-port surgery has been developed to minimize abdominal wall trauma while maintaining the benefits of minimally invasive surgery. However, reduced-port robotic rectal surgery remains technically challenging due to interference of external arms. The modular design of the Hugo RAS system (Medtronic, Minneapolis, MN, USA) provides greater flexibility in arm positioning to minimize external arm interference without compromising instrument maneuverability In abdominoperineal resection (APR), the incision for a permanent colostomy is inevitable. We report the first case of completely robot-assisted APR performed using the Hugo RAS system through a planned stoma site. Three robotic trocars were inserted through the planned left lower-quadrant stoma site, and one arm through the right lower quadrant. We call this approach SIPORS, Single-Incision Plus One Robot-assisted Surgery. The procedure is presented in the accompanying video. As the first case, a 50-year-old woman with rectal cancer underwent APR after systemic chemotherapy. The console time was 167 min. The procedure was completed without significant robotic arm interference. The postoperative course was uneventful except for transient cystitis. The circumferential and distal resection margins were 3 and 35 mm, respectively. The mesorectal specimen was complete, 25 lymph nodes were harvested, and the pathological stage was pT3N2bM1. SIPORS using the Hugo RAS at a planned stoma site was technically feasible and achieved an oncologically acceptable resection in this patient. It may offer improved cosmesis, reduced postoperative pain, fewer wound complications, and a lower risk of trocar-site incisional hernia. Further experience is needed to confirm its reproducibility and clinical benefits.
